title: Sr Manager, Real Estate and Workplace
description:
About ALSO.

We’re ALSO, an electric mobility company originally conceived as a part of Rivian. We’re a passionate team of builders, dreamers, doers and innovators, focused on creating entirely new (not to mention, innovative and delightful) vertically integrated, small EVs designed to meet the global mobility challenges of today and tomorrow. Our mission is to inspire everyone to ride ALSO—replacing many local car, truck and SUV miles with ones on vehicles that are more affordable, more enjoyable and 10-50x more efficient.



ALSO is seeking an execution-driven Sr Manager, Real Estate & Workplace, to lead workplace strategy, projects, programs, and teams based in our Palo Alto HQ for a global multi-site portfolio spanning office, R&D labs, commercial hubs, and retail.


This role owns team leadership, strategic planning, critical project execution, and executive-level representation alongside the Director, partnering daily with IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal, Insurance, People, and cross functional key stakeholders. Success requires ability to prioritize in a fast-paced environment, drive R&D projects to execution, disciplined governance, financial rigor, 3rd party management, and the ability to anticipate space and workplace service needs (ie, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial, and moves). Onsite 3-5 days/week, with off-hours availability for time-sensitive and critical issues.



What You Will Do 

Team & Program Leadership

 - Lead the Real Estate & Workplace team (operations, facilities, mail, logistics, culinary, janitorial) as deputy lead, balancing competing priorities with long-term focus.

 - Manage projects end to end, including portfolio administration, R&D lab build-outs, workplace programs, and occupancy data.

Strategic Space Planning & Occupancy Analysis

 - Own headcount and occupancy analysis, turning hiring plans and growth into space strategy, capacity models, and scenarios.

 - Drive long-range workplace strategy and partner with Finance and Analytics on forecasting and tradeoff recommendations to leadership.

Vendor, Contract & Budget Management

 - Manage vendors, consultants, landlords, and GCs with negotiation and financial accountability.

 - Own budget tracking, forecasting, and RFPs with Purchasing and Finance, and oversee lease transactions end to end with Legal and Risk.

Cross-Functional Partnership

 - Act as the connective tissue across IT, Engineering, Purchasing, Finance, Legal/Compliance, Analytics, and G&A.

 - Support Executive Assistants on space, logistics, and events, and communicate credibly with landlords, brokers, executives, and building inspectors.

Technical R&D Project Delivery & Operations

 - Coordinate lab infrastructure and equipment installs with Engineering and vendors.

 - Partner with the IT and EHS & Security Manager on life-safety and compliance, and serve as a point of contact for after-hours facilities emergencies.

Process Governance & Data Enablement

 - Implement standard PM frameworks, ticketing, and KPI/milestone dashboards.

 - Adopt new technology and AI-assisted tools to streamline workflows as the portfolio grows.



What You Will Bring 

 - 7+ years of progressive real estate, workplace, or facilities operations experience, with demonstrated growth from individual execution into a leadership scope.

 - Track record leading teams and operating as a trusted second-in-command.

 - Comfortable partnering across IT, Engineering, Finance, Legal, and Purchasing, and communicating credibly from AHJs to executives.

 - Working knowledge of commercial leases, vendor contracts, and budget/financial management.

 - Comfortable with ambiguity and fast-changing priorities; adaptable to new technology, software, and AI-assisted tools.

 - Familiarity with EHS, physical security concepts, and specialized lab/R&D infrastructure preferred (this role partners with a dedicated EHS & Security Manager rather than owning those programs directly).

 - Experience scaling high-tech, EV, or R&D lab environments strongly preferred.

 - Able to respond to occasional off-hours emergencies.



The salary for this position ranges from $200,000 - $220,000 per year, depending on experience, qualifications, and location.


Perks and Benefits

 - Robust health coverage. Excellent health, dental and vision insurance covered up to 100% by Also. with FSA & HSA options.

 - One Medical membership and dedicated insurance advocates.

 - Rich fertility and family building benefits with Progyny.

 - Flexible time off. 

 - 401(k) match.



Why ALSO.

We’re passionate about helping the world find a better way to get there—wherever it is you’re headed.

We’re located in the heart of Silicon Valley and have brought together a world-class team from some of the biggest brands in the technology, automotive, cycling, outdoor recreation and retail spaces. 

Together we’re working hands-on to imagine, design and build an entirely new solution to a global set of transportation challenges.

description:
About AbbVie

We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. Drug Substance Engineering Internship Overview
Envision spending your summer working with energetic colleagues and inspirational leaders, all while gaining world-class experience in one of the most dynamic organizations in the pharmaceutical industry. This is a reality for AbbVie Interns.
Micronization of drug substance is a critical process in API manufacturing for ensuring downstream critical quality attributes. Micronization processes such as pin milling and jet milling leverage feed rate control to optimize the process performance, and while feed rate is well understood for many powder systems there is a gap in understanding the feed rate control of poorly flowing materials in micronization techniques.
The Drug Substance Engineering Intern within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) will help establish a systematic approach to understand how the physical properties of powder systems impact their feeding performance in micronization processes.
Key responsibilities include:
Experimental studies to understand and characterize powder properties
Evaluate performance of micronization techniques (i.e. jet mill, pin mill) with various feed mechanisms
Analyze data and trends to identify signatures for process performance
Develop and verify computational models
Summarize and present findings in departmental and cross-functional settings
Minimum Qualifications
Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Chemical Engineering, Materials Engineering, or other related field
Must be enrolled in university for at least one semester following the internship
Preferred Qualifications
Expected graduation date between December 2027 – June 2028
Exposure to comminution processes
Experience with physical characterization techniques (flowability, adhesion, cohesion, bulk density, laser diffraction particle size determination)
Proficient in computational modeling techniques (e.g., fluid dynamics, discrete element method)

2027 Formulation Sciences Internship Overview

Join AbbVie's Pharmaceutical Technology team within Product Development, Science, and Technology (PDS&T) to support late-stage formulation development for a solid oral dosage form. This internship focuses on investigating excipient compatibility, specifically the interaction between common solid oral excipients and chemical stability. The intern will work alongside experienced formulation scientists and analytical chemists to characterize this phenomenon and help define strategies to ensure robust, high-quality drug product formulations. Currently enrolled in university, pursuing a PhD in Pharmaceutical Sciences, Chemistry, Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related scientific discipline.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. The Associate Director, Pricing is the International pricing lead for RINVOQ . The role sets RINVOQ's International pricing strategy and preserves the integrity of RINVOQ's price across its indications and markets. It turns pricing analysis into clear guidance, robust business cases and accurate financial assumptions, and supports Area and affiliate teams in achieving broad, timely and sustainable patient access that reflects the value of RINVOQ.
Key Responsibilities:
Pricing Strategy and Guidance:
Develop and maintain International pricing guidance for RINVOQ (price corridors and launch and re-pricing recommendations) in line with brand strategy, the Integrated Access Strategy (IAS) and corporate objectives.
Apply the Strategic Pricing Framework to define the price potential of new indications and formulations, and recommend indication and country launch sequencing that maximizes International value.
Develop contracting guidance and access models that address payer objections and affordability concerns while preserving the integrity of RINVOQ's price.
Monitor International pricing policy and competitor pricing, and flag risks and opportunities for RINVOQ early.
Business Cases and Pricing Governance:
Lead the development, review and challenge of RINVOQ pricing business cases from affiliates and Areas, ensuring each is analytically sound, compliant with International pricing governance and ready for decision.
Prepare and present business cases to the Executive Pricing Councils, with a clear recommendation, quantified financial impact, risks and mitigations.
PVTO and IRP Analysis:
Build and run price-volume trade-off (PVTO) analyses to evaluate price and access scenarios, breakeven volumes and the net revenue impact of pricing decisions at market and International level.
Assess International Reference Pricing (IRP) implications of every proposed price change, launch price and confidential agreement. Quantify cross-country spill-over and recommend the sequencing and price levels that preserve the integrity of RINVOQ's price across International markets.
Work with International Pricing analysts to design, run and interpret IRP, PVTO and launch-sequencing models, and turn the outputs into clear recommendations for senior stakeholders.
Plan and LRP:
Own the RINVOQ pricing assumptions in the annual Plan and Long Range Plan (LRP) process, including price evolution, launch timing, price erosion, IRP impact and risk and opportunity scenarios.
Collect, challenge and align pricing assumptions with Areas, affiliates and Finance, so that forecasts are consistent and explained.
Cross-Functional Partnership:
Area and affiliates (primary partners): help key markets turn International pricing guidance into local outcomes, covering price potential, negotiation strategy, scenarios, fallback positions and objection handling for national and sub-national negotiations.
Therapy Area teams (primary partners): make sure the pricing position is reflected in the RINVOQ IAS and brand strategy, and that indication priorities reflect price potential.
HTA: align price potential with the expected HTA outcome and value story and assess the price implications of HTA evidence and comparator choices.
Finance: reconcile pricing inputs with Plan, LRP and business case financials, and agree the net revenue impact of pricing decisions.
Act as the internal subject matter expert on RINVOQ pricing, IRP and pricing analytics.
Essential
Bachelor's degree in Finance, Economics, Health Economics, Statistics, Mathematics, Pharmacy or a related field.
At least 3 years' experience in pharmaceutical pricing, market access, health economics or commercial finance.
Strong quantitative and modelling skills, with experience building and interpreting pricing, forecasting or scenario models in Excel.
Working knowledge of International Reference Pricing and its impact on launch sequencing and price setting.
Ability to condense complex analysis into clear, concise recommendations for senior audiences. Excellent written and spoken English.
Able to influence without authority in a matrix organization, make sound calls on incomplete data, and challenge affiliate and Area proposals constructively.
Desired
Hands-on experience with pricing business cases for executive pricing committees, PVTO analysis and Plan/LRP pricing assumptions.
Knowledge of P&R systems in key markets, including Australia, Canada, China, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, Spain and the UK.
Understanding of HTA and health economic principles from a payer perspective.
Experience in immunology or another multi-indication specialty brand.

title: Associate Director, Strategy and Operations (Chief of Staff) Irvine, CA
description:
About AbbVie
At Allergan Aesthetics, an AbbVie company, we develop, manufacture, and market a portfolio of leading aesthetics brands and products. Our aesthetics portfolio includes facial injectables, body contouring, plastics, skin care, and more. Our goal is to consistently provide our customers with innovation, education, exceptional service, and a commitment to excellence, all with a personal touch. For more information, visit https://global.allerganaesthetics.com/ . Follow Allergan Aesthetics on LinkedIn.
Position Overview:
The Associate Director, Strategy & Operations, Practice Economics is responsible for helping build the structure, strategy, and operating discipline for a newly evolving Practice Economics organization within Allergan Aesthetics. This role will support the Vice President, Practice Economics and partner closely with the leadership team to translate strategic priorities into clear plans, governance, execution, and measurable customer and business impact.
This role is based in Irvine, California and will require close collaboration with Practice Economics leadership, cross-functional partners, and field-facing teams.
The ideal candidate will be a strategic, operationally strong leader who is comfortable operating in ambiguity, creating clarity, influencing across a matrixed organization, and driving disciplined follow-through on complex priorities. This individual will bring strong business judgment, executive communication skills, and the ability to connect strategy, governance, insights, cross-functional execution, and leadership communication in support of a newly evolving organization.
Key Responsibilities
Strategic Planning & Business Insights: Partner with the VP, Practice Economics and leadership team to define, refine, and execute Practice Economics strategic priorities, including annual planning, long-range planning, goal setting, prioritization, roadmaps, milestones, owners, and measurable outcomes.
Business Operations & Governance: Establish and manage the Practice Economics operating cadence, including leadership team meetings, business reviews, prioritization forums, governance mechanisms, decision-making processes, initiative tracking, and accountability routines.
Cross-Functional Initiative Leadership: Lead high-priority, cross-functional initiatives from strategy through execution by coordinating workstreams across Practice Consulting, National Accounts, Strategic Planning, Marketing, Analytics, Finance, Operations, and Field teams.
Organizational Effectiveness & Ways of Working: Help define and evolve the Practice Economics operating model, including workstream ownership, governance, decision rights, team interfaces, leadership alignment, role clarity, and repeatable processes that move the team from reactive work toward proactive planning and disciplined execution.
Executive Communications & Special Projects: Develop concise, executive-ready communications, presentations, briefing documents, strategic narratives, recommendations, decision points, and action plans for senior leadership audiences, business reviews, board-level discussions, and major stakeholder engagements.
Performance Management & Accountability: Develop and maintain dashboards, scorecards, operating tools, and progress updates that clarify performance, risks, dependencies, decisions, and execution status across key Practice Economics priorities.
Stakeholder Alignment & Influence: Facilitate alignment across stakeholders with different priorities, timelines, and decision rights while anticipating execution risks, removing barriers, escalating issues, and ensuring initiatives remain connected to broader Practice Economics strategy and customer and business impact.
Education: Bachelor’s degree required. MBA or advanced degree preferred.
Experience: 10+ years of experience in strategy, business operations, commercial operations, management consulting, project leadership, or related functions. Experience leading complex cross-functional initiatives in a matrixed environment. Healthcare, aesthetics, pharmaceutical, medical device, commercial excellence, or customer success experience preferred. Experience supporting senior leadership teams or helping build and scale a new function, center of excellence, or transformation capability preferred.
Skills: Strong business acumen, analytical capability, executive communication skills, and ability to influence without authority. Experience developing operating rhythms, governance processes, executive updates, and performance management tools. Strong PowerPoint, storytelling, executive-level synthesis, and data-driven problem-solving skills.
Attributes: Strategic thinker with operational discipline. Proven ability to manage ambiguity, prioritize competing demands, and convert strategic ideas into disciplined execution. Ownership, accountability, high follow-through, executive presence, curiosity, flexibility, and a solution-oriented mindset. Ability to build trust and drive alignment across teams.

description:
About AbbVie
AbbVie's mission is to discover and deliver innovative medicines and solutions that solve serious health issues today and address the medical challenges of tomorrow. We strive to have a remarkable impact on people's lives across several key therapeutic areas including immunology, oncology and neuroscience - and products and services in our Allergan Aesthetics portfolio. The Director II, Transformation & Enablement will lead the development and execution of strategic initiatives designed to strengthen organizational effectiveness, accelerate capability building, and enable future growth across U.S. Market Access. This role will serve as the leader of a centralized Transformation & Enablement organization responsible for driving operational excellence, organizational effectiveness, strategic planning support, capability development, and enterprise transformation efforts across the Market Access organization.
The role will oversee a centralized Transformation & Enablement team responsible for Payer Strategy Enablement, Account Enablement, Future Fit capability development, and strategic transformation initiatives. This team will be accountable for developing and scaling the capabilities, tools, processes, governance, and ways of working that define the future operating model of U.S. Market Access. The Director II will serve as the orchestrator of Market Access transformation, partnering with senior leaders across the organization to identify emerging needs, align on future-state priorities, and drive implementation of capabilities that improve enterprise performance, agility, and competitiveness.
The position will partner closely with the Market Access Leadership Team to align priorities, drive strategic initiatives, improve organizational effectiveness, and ensure the organization has the capabilities, infrastructure, and support model necessary to execute in an increasingly complex and rapidly evolving access environment.
This role offers a unique opportunity to shape the future operating model of U.S. Market Access while influencing strategy, execution, talent development, innovation, and organizational transformation across one of AbbVie's most critical commercial capabilities.
Responsibilities:
Transformation & Capability Leadership
Define and lead the long-term Transformation & Enablement vision for U.S. Market Access
Establish and scale future-state capabilities required to address evolving payer, customer, policy, and market access dynamics
Develop and maintain the U.S. Market Access capability roadmap, identifying organizational needs and opportunities for improvement
Drive pull-through of Future Fit, operating model, contracting, value proposition, evidence generation, AI, and enablement initiatives across the organization
Identify organizational pain points and opportunities to improve execution, collaboration, scalability, and effectiveness
Serve as the primary leader responsible for translating future-state design concepts into implemented capabilities, tools, governance, and ways of working, partnering with senior leaders across the enterprise to shape the future Market Access operating model and drive large-scale organizational transformation
Define and evolve the capability development ecosystem across U.S. Market Access, ensuring effective integration of enablement, training, onboarding, field development, and knowledge management resources to support current and future business needs
Continuously assess emerging needs and develop solutions that strengthen Market Access competitiveness and organizational performance
Future Market Access Capabilities
Lead development of enterprise capabilities supporting payer strategy, analytics, evidence generation, value propositions, customer engagement, and market evolution response
Partner with Commercial, Medical, HEOR, Finance, BTS, and other stakeholders to identify future capability requirements
Champion innovation and adoption of emerging tools, technologies, analytics, and AI-enabled solutions across Market Access
Drive standardization of key Market Access deliverables and processes, including Integrated Access Strategies, value propositions, planning frameworks, and enterprise tools
Build organizational readiness for future market access challenges through capability development, process evolution, and organizational design
Establish scalable models for capability deployment and field adoption, leveraging partnerships with training and learning organizations to ensure strategic priorities, customer insights, and market access capabilities are effectively embedded across the organization
Strategic Leadership Support
Serve as a strategic advisor and thought partner to the Head of U.S. Market Access and Market Access Leadership Team
Drive alignment on organizational priorities, strategic objectives, and key business initiatives
Support development of strategic overviews, executive briefings, business reviews, and leadership communications
Maintain visibility of critical initiatives and help ensure leadership focus remains on the most important business priorities
Lead selected strategic projects on behalf of Market Access leadership
Track progress against key organizational priorities and strategic initiatives
Organizational Effectiveness & Enablement
Lead a centralized team supporting Payer Strategy, Account Teams, Future Fit initiatives, and broader Market Access capabilities
Drive consistency and best practices across planning processes, governance, reporting, training, and execution
Establish scalable tools, operating practices, and support infrastructure that improve organizational effectiveness
Ensure strategic initiatives are translated into actionable plans with clear ownership and accountability
Partner with leadership to improve organizational agility, prioritization, and resource allocation
Oversee implementation of processes and ways of working that improve cross-functional collaboration and execution
Provide leadership and strategic direction for the U.S. Market Access enablement and training support model, defining clear roles, expectations, and engagement approaches that maximize organizational effectiveness and capability development
Cross-Functional Leadership
Serve as a primary point of coordination across U.S. Market Access and key partner organizations
Build strong partnerships with Commercial, Finance, Pricing, HEOR, Medical, APEX, Patient Services, BTS, Government Affairs, and other stakeholders
Help align efforts across functions and ensure Market Access priorities are represented in enterprise initiatives
Drive governance, decision-making, and issue resolution across complex cross-functional initiatives, bringing together senior leaders to resolve barriers, align priorities, and accelerate execution
Promote cross-functional collaboration and alignment around shared business priorities
Communications, Culture & Engagement
Oversee development and execution of communications strategies supporting Market Access priorities and organizational objectives
Lead planning and execution of major organizational events, leadership forums, planning meetings, and offsites
Partner with BHR to support leadership development, onboarding, engagement, and talent initiatives
Foster a high-performance culture focused on collaboration, accountability, innovation, and continuous improvement
Operational Excellence
Drive continuous improvement of Market Access ways of working, governance processes, and operating practices
Improve organizational visibility and transparency through enhanced reporting, dashboards, planning tools, and metrics
Ensure effective management and follow-through of leadership decisions, strategic initiatives, and organizational priorities
Continuously evaluate organizational performance and implement improvements that enhance efficiency and business outcomes

Experience leading teams and developing talent in matrix organizations
Strong understanding of Market Access, customer strategy, commercial operations, or related healthcare functions

Establish and scale a sustainable Transformation & Enablement capability for U.S. Market Access
Improve organizational effectiveness through enhanced capabilities, tools, governance, and ways of working
Accelerate implementation of Future Fit and strategic transformation initiatives
Increase organizational capacity by enabling leaders and teams to focus on strategy, customers, and business priorities
Build scalable capabilities that position U.S. Market Access for future success amid evolving access, policy, channel, and customer dynamics
Strengthen collaboration, alignment, and accountability across teams and functions

Strategic leadership and enterprise thinking
Organizational effectiveness and change leadership
Exceptional communication and executive influence skills
Strong business acumen and problem-solving capabilities
Ability to translate strategy into execution

High degree of emotional intelligence, resilience, adaptability, and organizational savvy

Position Summary
The Director, Utilities & Electrical owns strategic discipline leadership, people leadership, technical governance and project enablement for electrical power systems, clean utilities, black utilities, energy infrastructure, reliability, maintainability, electrical safety and operational readiness within AbbVie Global Engineering.
The role provides senior technical and organizational leadership for AbbVie’s global manufacturing network and strategic capital investments through standards ownership, front-end engineering support, technical decision-making, project risk management and disciplined execution across priority investment programs, manufacturing sites and technology platforms.
The Director leads and develops a global team of electrical and utilities technical experts, establishes clear priorities and accountabilities, and ensures the organization has the capability and capacity required to support brownfield expansions, modernization programs, debottlenecking, infrastructure upgrades, lifecycle asset replacement and greenfield manufacturing investments.
The role serves as the senior Global Engineering authority for electrical and utilities strategy, ensuring systems are safe, compliant, resilient, energy efficient, maintainable and capable of supporting current and future manufacturing requirements.
The Director partners with Strategic Investments, project delivery teams, operations, quality, EHS, validation/CQV, site engineering, sustainability, digital/automation and external engineering partners to deliver technically robust, scalable and business-aligned engineering solutions.
Global Engineering Governance and Standards
Establish, own and deploy global engineering standards, design criteria, specifications, technical practices and governance expectations for electrical power systems, clean utilities, black utilities, energy infrastructure, reliability, maintainability and electrical safety.
Act as the senior discipline authority for material electrical and utilities decisions affecting safety, quality, compliance, cost, schedule, operability, resilience or lifecycle value.
Define discipline strategy and multiyear capability roadmaps aligned with AbbVie’s manufacturing network strategy, sustainability objectives and strategic investment priorities.
Govern consistent application of standards, design principles, lessons learned and engineering playbooks across regions, sites and capital projects.
Establish assurance and review processes that verify technical quality at key project stage gates.
Lead resolution and escalation of significant discipline risks, deviations from standards and cross-project technical issues.
Represent Global Engineering in enterprise technical governance forums and communicate clear, executive-ready recommendations to senior stakeholders.
Strategic Capital Investment Leadership
Provide senior owner-side engineering leadership for the electrical and utilities scope of strategic capital investments, including new facilities, major capacity programs, technology platform deployments, infrastructure solutions and lifecycle asset strategies.
Lead discipline input to front-end engineering, facility concepts, site master planning, investment option evaluation, business cases and technology selection.
Define electrical and utilities design strategies for strategic projects, including power architecture, utility generation and distribution, redundancy philosophy, capacity planning, energy performance, maintainability, monitoring and operational readiness.
Ensure discipline assumptions, deliverables, risks, interfaces, resources and decisions are incorporated into program plans, cost estimates and execution strategies.
Establish project assurance priorities and direct senior technical reviews at concept, basic design, detailed design, construction, commissioning and handover stages.
Balance safety, quality, compliance, reliability, sustainability, cost and schedule when making or recommending investment decisions.
Apply global lessons learned and network standards to improve project quality, speed, predictability and readiness across the portfolio.
Provide clear escalation to the VP, Global Engineering and Strategic Investments leadership when decisions have material enterprise, program or network impact.
Electrical and Utilities Technical Leadership
Lead technical decision-making for medium- and low-voltage power distribution, substations, transformers, switchgear, motor control, emergency and standby power, uninterruptible power supplies, grounding, lightning protection and electrical protection systems.
Provide governance for electrical safety, arc-flash risk, hazardous-area classification interfaces, protection coordination, power quality, system studies and safe equipment lifecycle management.
Direct strategies for clean utilities, including purified water, water for injection, clean steam, process gases and associated generation, storage, distribution, monitoring and sanitization systems.

Help ensure the accuracy of worldwide consolidated inventory costs and inventory-related expenses.

Resolve margin and costing inquiries from affiliates in a timely and accurate manner.

Support the annual planning process.
Perform ad hoc analyses and support projects and process improvements as needed.

Bachelor’s degree in Finance or Accounting preferred
Proficient Excel Skills required, experience with SAP preferred
Cost Accounting experience in manufacturing highly desirable along with experience in supply chain finance operations.
Strong analytical, communication, problem solving, and interpersonal skills
Minimum 2+ years of progressive and related experience.

Demonstrated experience adapting to change and embracing learning

AbbVie Analytical Research & Development (Analytical R&D) is a global analytical scientific organization responsible for all CMC analytical activities related to the development of AbbVie's pharmaceutical products.  Our scope includes AbbVie's diverse pipeline of innovative small molecule medicines and spans from the selection of Discovery candidate molecules through Early-Stage Clinical Development.  We are building a world-class team of scientists and leaders who will drive the advancement of industry-leading analytical capabilities and make meaningful contributions to advance AbbVie's pipeline of innovative medicines.  Careers in AbbVie Analytical R&D provide unique opportunities to work with global and cross-functional teams to drive exceptional science and innovative product development strategies.  We are looking for diverse candidates with strong scientific and leadership experience to join the AbbVie Analytical R&D team and can offer exciting and rewarding career opportunities for these candidates.
Position Description:
For the Principal Research Scientist I position, we are seeking a highly motivated and experienced data scientist to provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, artificial intelligence/machine learning (AI/ML), advanced analytics, and data automation within Analytical R&D. The successful candidate will partner closely with analytical scientists to frame high-value scientific questions, engineer and integrate complex analytical data, and develop fit-for-purpose models, visualizations, and digital solutions that accelerate data-driven decisions across pharmaceutical development.
The candidate will perform and direct data science and application-development activities, mentor and develop scientists, and provide leadership across multiple projects and initiatives. They will conceive, execute, and communicate multidisciplinary strategies; translate between analytical scientists, statisticians, data engineers, software and IT partners; and convert innovative concepts into sustainable, adopted solutions with measurable scientific and business impact.
This role requires a strong combination of data science depth, pharmaceutical or scientific domain awareness, product-oriented solution development, and collaborative leadership. The scientist will help shape the Analytical R&D data science strategy, establish reusable standards and best practices, coordinate initiatives across a global network, and foster productive partnerships with internal data science, statistics, information technology, and R&D organizations.
Responsibilities:
Provide scientific and technical leadership for analytical data science, AI/ML, advanced analytics, visualization, and data automation initiatives supporting pharmaceutical development.
Consult with analytical scientists and project teams to define the scientific or business question, assess data readiness, select appropriate analytical approaches, and translate results into clear recommendations and decisions.
Lead the end-to-end delivery of data products and analytical solutions, including problem framing, data acquisition and integration, exploratory analysis, feature engineering, model development and validation, visualization, deployment, documentation, user adoption, and lifecycle support.
Develop and apply statistical, machine-learning, chemometric, and/or generative-AI methods to complex analytical data while ensuring approaches are scientifically sound, interpretable, reproducible, and fit for intended use.
Engineer, curate, and analyze structured and unstructured data from laboratory instruments, scientific systems, documents, and development workflows; improve data quality, traceability, accessibility, and reuse.
Design and deliver intuitive applications, dashboards, reports, and automated workflows that reduce manual effort, improve consistency, and enable scientists to obtain timely insights from their data.
Mentor, guide, and develop data scientists and scientific colleagues; provide technical coaching, peer review, and hands-on support, and create learning opportunities that strengthen data literacy and analytical capability across the organization.
Lead or coordinate a portfolio of data science initiatives, establish priorities and delivery plans, manage risks and dependencies, and communicate progress, value, and recommendations to project teams and senior stakeholders.
Establish and promote standards for analytical data assessment, model validation, software development, documentation, version control, testing, data governance, and sustainable solution support.
Build and foster a global network with Analytical R&D, Development Sciences, statistics, enterprise data science, IT, and external partners; connect teams to the appropriate expertise and facilitate effective cross-functional execution.
Identify high-value opportunities, generate new scientific proposals, evaluate emerging AI/ML and digital technologies, and champion responsible innovation that advances scientific understanding, development speed, quality, and operational efficiency.
Communicate complex methods and findings clearly to technical and nontechnical audiences through decision-focused presentations, reports, visualizations, and scientific publications where appropriate.
Ensure solutions and activities comply with applicable safety, quality, regulatory, data-integrity, privacy, security, and AbbVie requirements.
Bachelor’s, Master’s, or Ph.D. in Data Science, Computer Science, Statistics, Applied Mathematics, Engineering, Chemometrics, Computational Science, Analytical Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a closely related discipline, typically with a minimum of 14 years (BS), 12 years (MS), or 6 years (Ph.D.) of relevant industry experience.
Demonstrated experience applying data science, AI/ML, statistics, or advanced analytics to scientific, pharmaceutical, biotechnology, chemical, or other complex R&D problems.
Advanced proficiency in Python and/or R and strong working knowledge of relevant data-science libraries, statistical modeling, machine learning, data visualization, and reproducible analytical workflows.
Experience integrating, cleaning, transforming, and analyzing complex and heterogeneous data; working knowledge of SQL, relational data concepts, APIs, and modern data-management practices.
Demonstrated ability to build and deliver production-quality analytical applications, dashboards, automated workflows, or reusable data products. Experience with tools such as Streamlit, Shiny, cloud platforms, workflow automation, or equivalent technologies is desirable.
Strong understanding of model development and evaluation, experimental design, uncertainty, validation, interpretability, and the limitations and appropriate use of AI/ML methods.
Demonstrated leadership through mentoring, technical direction, project or portfolio leadership, influence across functions, and delivery of complex initiatives. Prior direct people-management experience is beneficial but not required.
Proven ability to partner with domain scientists, quickly learn scientific workflows, translate ambiguous needs into tractable analytical problems, and balance technical rigor with practical, fit-for-purpose delivery.
Experience with software-development practices such as Git/version control, modular coding, testing, documentation, code review, deployment, and lifecycle management.
Excellent analytical problem-solving, project-management, written and oral communication, and stakeholder-management skills, including the ability to explain complex concepts to diverse audiences.
Self-motivated, collaborative, and adaptable, with demonstrated scientific curiosity, creativity, sound judgment, and the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced R&D environment.
Knowledge of pharmaceutical development, CMC, analytical laboratory workflows, regulated environments, data integrity, or scientific data standards is strongly preferred.
Experience with computational chemistry and molecular modeling approaches to investigate molecular properties, structure–property relationships, or other scientific questions relevant to pharmaceutical development is desirable.

Act as a subject matter expert in BioARD, lead phase-appropriate analytical development strategies for biologics characterization including ADC, PDC, AOC, fusion proteins, multi-specific antibodies, and other novel modalities.
Design and execute the buildout of biotherapeutics extended characterization methods, to facilitate in-process analytics, batch release/stability, RS qualification, and comparability study.
Make lab-based, data-driven, and phase-appropriate contributions to project team and deliver results in a team-oriented setting and will work across scientific disciplines to drive programs through critical milestones.
Represent key area function in cross-functional project teams, provide hands-on analytical support, technical oversight to portfolios.
Collaborate and integrate scientific objectives associated with development of new/improved products or technology; contribute to scientific exchange and publications.
Author, review lab notebook, analytical report, and analytical sections of regulatory filings. Primary author of external publications, presentations, and patents. Present at leading scientific conferences.
May mentor/supervise a team of one or more, guide and evaluate the performance of those individuals; is accountable for the effective performance of the team/individuals.
BS or equivalent education with 14+ years of experience; MS or equivalent education with 12+ years of experience; PhD in scientific discipline (e.g., Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, or Biology) with typically 6+ years of industry experience, is required.
Demonstrated proficiency and substantial hands-on experience in mass spectrometry-based characterization of biologics, including intact/subunit analysis, peptide mapping, disulfide bond mapping, etc., as well as hands-on experience in mass spec data processing and interpretation using various MS software platforms.
Strong working knowledge and familiarity with separation-based analytical techniques, including SEC, HIC, HILIC, RPLC, IEX, CE, icIEF, etc.
Knowledge in key analytical CMC areas, such as risk-based analytical development and method validation, CQAs assessment, reference standard qualification, comparability study.

Provides technical guidance to junior engineers and collaborates with cross-functional teams, ensuring integration of systems, equipment, and technologies. Delivers high‑quality technical outputs for complex projects and programs; defines and validates methods, documents results and key assumptions, ensures adherence to applicable standards and controls, and communicates technical progress, impacts and recommended mitigations to project leads and stakeholders.

Deliver assigned infrastructure projects: Manage assigned campus development consisting of a set of buildings or systems from utilities, Spine, warehouse, laboratory, administration, cafeteria, laboratories, car park, offices and office buildings. Translate overall program or campus objectives into clearly defined package deliverables and deliver against approved scope, schedule, budget, and quality requirements.
Own project planning, cost, and schedule control: Develop and maintain package or building execution plans, budgets, forecasts, schedules, milestones, and performance measures. Align package plans with the integrated campus schedule, monitor commitments and progress, address variances, and provide timely, accurate reporting to the Infrastructure Project Director.

Ensure construction completion, testing, qualification or verification as applicable, punch-list resolution, documentation, training support, and asset handover are completed. Close contracts and capture lessons learned to improve delivery across the portfolio.

Required: Bachelor’s degree in engineering or a related technical discipline.
Preferred: Advanced degree, Project Management Professional (PMP) certification, or relevant engineering or project-management credentials.
Experience
Recommended minimum: At least 10 years of relevant engineering or capital-project experience, including direct accountability for delivering complex infrastructure projects or major packages.
Demonstrated delivery experience spanning planning, design, procurement, construction, commissioning, and handover in pharmaceutical, biopharmaceutical, or comparable regulated manufacturing environments.
Experience with campus utilities, building systems, site infrastructure, or support facilities, including interfaces with cGMP manufacturing operations.
Hands-on experience managing scope, budgets, forecasts, schedules, risk, contractor performance, procurement activities, contract administration, and change control.
Experience leading multidisciplinary project teams and coordinating designers, contractors, vendors, Engineering, Construction, Commissioning, Operations, Procurement, EHS, and Quality in a matrixed organization.
Preferred: Greenfield campus or major expansion experience; commissioning and qualification exposure; and implementation of Factory of the future concepts relevant to infrastructure delivery.

Project execution and accountability: Converts portfolio priorities into practical package plans and drives deliverables to completion within delegated authority.
Technical and design integration: Understands utilities, infrastructure, building systems, and applicable cGMP design principles; integrates operational requirements, vendor inputs, and project interfaces.
Financial and schedule management: Uses budgets, forecasts, integrated schedules, milestones, and performance measures to identify variances and drive corrective action.
Commercial and contract management: Develops clear scopes, evaluates bids, administers approved contracts, monitors contractor obligations, and applies disciplined change control.
Risk management and problem-solving: Anticipates constraints, evaluates options and delivery impacts, implements mitigation, and escalates decisions with clear recommendations.
Construction and commissioning readiness: Coordinates safety, quality, completion, testing, turnover documentation, and operational handover across delivery teams.
Team leadership and stakeholder influence: Directs and coaches assigned team members, builds accountability, and aligns stakeholders without relying on formal reporting authority.
Communication and continuous improvement: Provides concise status and decision updates, maintains reliable project records, and applies lessons learned to improve delivery consistency.

Monitor event conditions and adjust plans in response to changing risks, schedules, attendance, or operational needs.
Document incidents, observations, and after-action findings; recommend improvements for future events.

AbbVie’s Biologics CMC organization develops processes to support the advancement and manufacture of biologic medicines. AbbVie is seeking a highly motivated scientist to lead development of microbial-based recombinant peptide production processes. This position will serve as a technical lead across expression-system and strain development, fermentation, recovery, purification, and scale-up.
Recombinant production of short peptides can be challenging due to intracellular degradation, low expression, aggregation, and limited solubility. The successful candidate will develop and optimize practical strategies to address these challenges and advance robust, scalable processes for therapeutic peptide production. When aligned with program needs, the candidate will also evaluate and apply genetic code expansion (GCE) strategies to enable the site-specific incorporation of non-canonical amino acids. Develop and assess fusion-tag and carrier-protein strategies—including His-tag, GST, SUMO, and inclusion-body expression—to improve peptide stability, expression, host tolerance, and recovery.
Design and conduct clone-screening studies using microscale cultivation, parallel bioreactors, and other appropriate scale-down or high-throughput approaches.
Develop and optimize peptide recovery processes, including cell harvest and lysis, inclusion-body isolation and processing, and chemical or enzymatic cleavage of fusion partners.
Troubleshoot peptide-specific process challenges, such as aggregation, low solubility, degradation, incomplete cleavage, and co-eluting impurities; recommend and pursue appropriate solutions.
Interpret analytical results, including HPLC, UPLC, and LC-MS data, to assess peptide identity, mass accuracy, purity, and process-related impurities; partner with analytical teams to address characterization needs.
Evaluate emerging technologies and process approaches for recombinant peptide production, including genetic code expansion when relevant to program needs.
Apply AI/ML approaches, where appropriate, to analyze peptide sequence, structure, and experimental data in support of design, optimization, and candidate prioritization.
Communicate scientific plans, progress, challenges, conclusions, and recommendations clearly to project teams and other stakeholders.

Thorough theoretical and practical understanding of relevant scientific disciplines, with hands-on experience in microbial physiology and recombinant expression systems, particularly  E. coli  and/or yeast.
Demonstrated ability to independently design, execute, and interpret critical experiments to address scientific or development questions.
Experience developing or optimizing expression processes for peptides, small proteins, or other products susceptible to degradation, or instability.
Experience with strain or clone screening, fermentation, and process optimization; familiarity with bioreactors and scale-down or parallel cultivation approaches.
Demonstrated experience with preparative chromatography and peptide or protein purification, as well as peptide recovery and fusion-partner cleavage strategies.

The Drug Product Design and Development (DPDD) group within the Synthetic Molecule CMC organization at AbbVie is responsible for the design and development of drug products that enable the delivery of AbbVie’s candidate synthetic molecules in dosage forms to support various stages of clinical evaluation, from proof of concept to pivotal studies and life cycle innovation. The candidate will work with cross-functional teams to develop drug delivery and formulation strategies, lead the design, characterization and understanding of formulations/processes, as well as advance biopharmaceutical characterizations of clinical formulations.  In this role, the candidate will play a crucial role as a project lead within dynamic, engaging, and cross functional teams with the ability to apply expertise and leadership skills to advise teams, solve complex problems and drive innovation. The candidate is also expected to foster productive collaborations and demonstrate effective communication within scientific teams and senior CMC management.

Typography is central to how ideas are communicated. We're seeking a Senior Software Development Engineer to lead this exciting journey in our San Francisco location.

Own and evolve our deployment platform. Lead strategy for CI/CD, PR environments, and release safety across a mixed fleet that includes containerized services, serverless services, and static front ends.
Build the foundation for AI-accelerated development. Help build our agent factory and grow our internal agentic toolkit and skill library.

Modernize our services for the AI era. Identify where an existing service is held back by its current build and lead the fix.
Rethink our security posture for agentic threats. Lead how we secure autonomous agents and their tool use.
Expose Adobe Fonts to the agentic ecosystem. Extend our Model Context Protocol (MCP) surface and conversational, intent-based font discovery.

A security outlook for this new surface — you think about how agentic systems fail and get abused, and proactively build guardrails accordingly.

Track record of delivering high-impact platform work used across multiple teams, leading complex cross-team technical efforts, and balancing near-term delivery with long-term maintainability, security, and operability.
Excellent written and verbal communication.
Typically 12+ years of software engineering experience, with demonstrated senior-level impact.

Ruby on Rails at scale, and experience decomposing or modernizing a large monolith.
GPU/model-serving infrastructure and low-latency inference (e.g. SageMaker, Kubernetes GPU platforms); search-engine internals (OpenSearch/Elasticsearch, vector/hybrid search).
Experience building developer platforms, internal tooling, or agent harnesses adopted by other teams.
Event-driven architectures and secrets-management platforms (Vault, CyberArk).
Front-end depth with modern component systems (Web Components/Lit, React/TypeScript, build systems).

title: Senior Manager, Business Technology Enablement
description:
Airbnb was born in 2007 when two hosts welcomed three guests to their San Francisco home, and has since grown to over 5 million hosts who have welcomed over 2 billion guest arrivals in almost every country across the globe. Every day, hosts offer unique stays and experiences that make it possible for guests to connect with communities in a more authentic way.
The Community You Will Join:
We are looking for a Senior Manager to lead BizTech Enablement and Innovation (BEI), BizTech's solutions partner to the rest of the company. BEI works with Finance, Legal, People, Marketing, Global Operations, Policy and Communications, Design, and other non-technical functions to understand how they work, turn their problems into working solutions, and make sure employees know about and adopt the technology BizTech provides. The team also brings what it learns back to BizTech product teams and vendors to shape their roadmaps. You will report to the Director, Tech Foundations.
The Difference You Will Make:
This is a strategic leadership role within a large business unit. For the next 18 months, the team's focus is AI. You will own the company's approach to AI adoption and impact outside of Engineering, set the vision for AI-enabled work, hold functions accountable to measurable outcomes, and serve as BizTech's primary partner to E-Team leaders on AI transformation.
More broadly, you will lead how Airbnb's non-technical functions discover, adopt, and get value from business technology. That covers quick consultations and fast-track solutions, go-to-market for new BizTech services, and building or buying new solutions where existing tools fall short. In the near term, you will define where Airbnb should be on AI-enabled work in two years, build the team and partnerships to get there, and make the trade-offs required to deliver it.
Success in this role is measured in business outcomes, not tool rollouts: functions that have redesigned their work around technology and AI, defined their own impact metrics, and can show the efficiency and quality gains, supported by a simpler tool landscape with fewer duplicate and unsupported tools.
A Typical Day:
Help define and own the multi-year strategy for AI adoption and impact across Airbnb's non-technical functions, aligned with company and Tech priorities.
Assess current gaps, existing capabilities, and emerging AI trends to anticipate how functions will need to work 18 to 24 months out, and translate that into a roadmap and investment.
Simplify the tools business teams use by steering them to supported solutions and closing the gaps that lead them to find their own.
Set organizational OKRs and success criteria for near and long-term initiatives, and hold teams and partners accountable for delivery.
Make and communicate hard trade-offs across competing functional demands, platform constraints, and budget.
Serve as the senior BizTech partner to leadership teams on AI transformation, including regular readouts to executives and senior Tech leadership.
Establish the framework by which each function defines, measures, and reports the business impact of AI, and drive adoption of that framework as a standard.
Build a metric-driven accountability culture: clear baselines, targets, and ownership for every function, with a single trusted source of truth for adoption and impact data.
Tailor narratives for different audiences, from detailed methodology with data and engineering partners to concise decision framing for executives.
Seek feedback from partner teams and use it to improve delivery; raise risks to leadership early.
Listen actively and anticipate where change will meet resistance.
Design and continuously refine the operating model that connects different technical functions and networks into one coordinated enablement system.
Shape the enablement approach for AI usage so functions can build and share AI solutions at scale.
Partner with platform and product teams to influence the AI tooling roadmap based on the needs of non-technical users.
Direct external partner and consulting engagements, including scope, governance, and return on investment.
Set quality, reliability, and security standards for the AI solutions the team and functions build; own operational issues in production and drive the fixes that prevent repeats.
Make sure tech debt and the long-term upkeep of shipped solutions are prioritized across the team's roadmap.
Lead a multi-disciplinary, globally distributed organization including managers, Business Solutions Engineers, Systems Architects, and Program Managers.
Create a team environment that values constructive debate, risk-taking, and learning from experiments, and that fosters belonging across regions.
Build an 18+ month talent plan and a succession pipeline, including hiring at L10 and above.
Coach, mentor, and grow the team to communicate clearly, resolve conflict early, and build inclusive teams.
Pilot new technologies, including AI, with business teams, and hand proven solutions to product owners for long-term support.
Coach leaders across functions to connect AI capabilities to business value.
Establish mechanisms that turn learnings from individual functions into reusable patterns across the company.
Represent BizTech in company-wide AI forums and contribute to hiring committees, talent processes, and Airbnb's internal AI community.
Role model Airbnb's core values and strengthen the company's mission through the way AI is introduced to employees.
Your Expertise:
12+ years of industry experience in business technology, enterprise systems, digital transformation, or technical program leadership, including 5+ years leading managers and multi-disciplinary teams.
Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, Business, or a related field, or equivalent experience.
Demonstrated track record setting and delivering multi-year strategy for a company-wide technology or transformation program with executive visibility.
Experience leading business technology consulting, solutions engineering, or IT business partnering for non-technical teams, including influencing product and vendor roadmaps.
Experience owning the quality, reliability, and support of technology solutions in production.
Experience building trusted relationships with, and influencing, C-level and E-Team executives, including the ability to align or challenge senior leaders on priorities.
Deep, hands-on understanding of generative AI tools and agentic workflows, and how they change the nature of non-technical work.
Strong analytical judgment: able to define measurement frameworks, interpret adoption and impact data, and ensure data quality and credibility at an executive level.
Proven ability to lead through ambiguity and rapid change, including shifting org structures, evolving technology, and competing priorities.
Experience designing operating models across multiple teams and organizations without direct authority.
Experience attracting, hiring, and developing senior talent and managers across regions.
Preferred: experience leading enterprise AI adoption or change management at a large technology company.

- Lead product delivery and adoption, building on shared pricing capabilities. Define evaluation criteria, permitted actions, and responses to missing or conflicting evidence with engineering and science partners.

A morning discussion with scientists might focus on how well a new model predicts customers’ responses to price changes. Together, you examine where its predictions match observed purchasing behavior and where they fall short, drawing on context from retail partners to connect those gaps to the pricing decisions the model needs to support.

description:
At Amazon, we're working to be the Earth’s most customer-centric company. To get there, we need exceptionally talented, bright, and driven people. This Product managers will be responsible for driving optimization efforts across various organizations and processes to improve shipping costs at Amazon. This includes defining the right set of metrics and processes, establishing ambitious goals and driving towards them, working with technology and operations partners to design, develop and deploy intelligent processes and improvements.
The North American Stores (NAS) organization is focused on continuously optimizing its P&L to drive long-term profitability. One of the most significant levers? Outbound fulfillment costs. The NAS Ship Cost Optimization (SCO) team tackles this head-on—leveraging technology for scale and launching innovative products that optimize costs systematically and with measurable impact.
This team has delivered over $1 billion+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements over the past four years by reducing packaging waste, correcting dimensional defects, optimizing regional fulfillment, and building Gen-AI products that reimagine how Amazon collaborates with selling partners. In 2026, the team is targeting significant savings through initiatives spanning cube reduction, AI-powered vendor outreach, regionalization strategies, sortability defect reduction, and improved placement—against a total addressable opportunity of $1.5B+.
As a Sr Product Manager on this team, you will own products and initiatives that directly improve the profitability of one of Amazon's largest businesses. You will develop a deep understanding of the inputs driving ship costs—placement, regional fulfillment, sortability, ship method choices, and dimensions—and translate that knowledge into products, policies, and partnerships that deliver hundreds of millions in savings. You will work across partner teams spanning Supply Chain Technology, Operations, Transportation, Finance, and Category Management, and you will leverage AI and automation to build the next generation of cost optimization products.
This is a role for someone who thinks in systems, communicates with precision, and thrives at the intersection of data, product strategy, and cross-organizational influence.
Key job responsibilities
- Own and drive the end-to-end product roadmap for one or more SCO initiatives (e.g., Cube Reduction, CRISP Gen-AI service, regional fulfillment strategies, or Sortability Overrides), from opportunity sizing through execution and measurement.
- Develop deep subject matter expertise in the inputs that drive outbound ship costs—placement, regional fulfillment, sortability tier economics, dimensional accuracy, and ship method choices—to identify high-impact opportunities others miss.
- Build and scale AI-powered products such as CRISP (Cube Reduction, Improving Sizing and Product Design), a Gen-AI LLM service that delivers automated packaging and product redesign recommendations to 20,000+ selling partners.
- Influence and align cross-functional stakeholders across VP-level organizations including Supply Chain Technology (SCOT), Transportation, Fulfillment Tech, Finance, Category teams, and Retail Business Services (RBS) to secure resources, resolve dependencies, and drive shared goals.
- Design and run controlled experiments to validate hypotheses, which enable product feature decisions and deliver results at scale.
- Define success metrics and tracking mechanisms (e.g., monthly flash reporting, ASIN-level cost attribution, vendor response rates) that create transparency and accountability for initiatives targeting $200MM+ in annual savings.
- Partner with Science and Engineering teams to improve targeting methodologies (dynamic ship cost impact models, out-of-stock probability signals, ASIN similarity algorithms) and automate manual workflows.
- Represent the team in leadership forums, crafting data-driven narratives that communicate progress, risks, and trade-offs to senior leaders with clarity and confidence.
A day in the life
You start the morning reviewing product metrics and triaging customer feedback to decide where to focus. Mid-morning, you are in a design review with your engineering and design partners, working through tradeoffs on a feature approaching launch. After lunch, you draft a working-backwards document for a new initiative, pulling in input from finance and marketing stakeholders. Later in the afternoon, you sit in on a customer research session to pressure-test assumptions before finalizing roadmap priorities. You close the day by updating your team on progress and aligning on next steps.
About the team
The NAS Ship Cost Optimization team is a small, high-impact product team that punches well above its weight. Over the past four years, the team has delivered $1B+ in cumulative bottom-line improvements to the Stores P&L by building innovative products—including the Gen-AI powered CRISP service—and championing cost-smart policies across the fulfillment network.
The team operates with strong leadership visibility at all levels, given the scale of results delivered and the innovative, AI-forward approach to problem solving. You will join a closely knit group that Thinks Big, earns trust through results, and works collaboratively across some of Amazon's most complex operational systems.
If you want to own products that move a multi-billion dollar P&L—and do it by combining analytical rigor, creative product thinking, technology-driven scale, and genuine cross-functional partnership—this is the team.

Join the Transportation Engineering Systems (TESS) team where you'll directly influence how Amazon's transportation network operates at scale. As a Program Manager on the Transportation Engineering Systems (TESS) team, you will learn how Amazon's proprietary transportation systems make decisions to move packages from the fulfillment network to customers. You will manage system configuration changes that control those systems, working directly with business leaders and program teams to create new transportation flows and design configurations that execute at scale. In this role, you will execute network design changes, dive deep into package flows, troubleshoot system errors, identify process improvements, and build automation, analytics, and reporting capabilities leveraging AI. You will lead stakeholder meetings, manage projects, and contribute to doc writings for the team.
Key job responsibilities
-Manage system configuration changes across Amazon's proprietary transportation systems to support new and existing package flows
-Track program milestones and communicate status to business leaders and stakeholders
-Execute network design changes end-to-end, coordinating with business leaders and program teams to ensure timely delivery
-Dive deep into package flow data to troubleshoot system errors, identify root causes, and implement fixes
-Identify process improvement opportunities and build automation to reduce manual effort and increase accuracy
-Develop analytics and reporting capabilities leveraging AI to drive data-driven decision-making
-Proactively identify and mitigate risks in system configurations before they impact customers
-Document processes, standard operating procedures, and configuration playbooks for the team.
-Contribute to additional doc writing such as QBR, MBR, and Lessons Learned.
A day in the life
Your daily execution responsibilities will come via an intake queue which generates work tickets assigned to you. There could be a variety of audit and reporting duties as well. You will review dashboards and metrics that track transportation network performance, identifying opportunities for optimization. Throughout the day, you'll attend or facilitate meetings with cross-functional teams—from operations managers to software engineers—ensuring alignment on priorities and removing roadblocks. You'll work autonomously to solve ambiguous problems, whether that's defining requirements for a new system feature or analyzing why a particular network configuration isn't performing as expected. Your work directly influences decisions about how Amazon moves packages from fulfillment centers to customers' doorsteps.
About the team
The Transportation Engineering Systems (TESS) team sits at the critical intersection of Amazon's business operations and technical infrastructure. We're responsible for configuring and optimizing the transportation network that powers Amazon's logistics operations globally. Our team culture values data-driven decision-making, customer obsession, and innovative problem-solving. We work collaboratively across organizational boundaries, partnering with operations teams, software engineers, and business leaders to deliver solutions that scale. As part of TESS, you'll contribute to systems that impact millions of customer deliveries while working with talented professionals who are passionate about operational excellence.
Basic qualifications: - 2+ years of program or project management experience
Preferred qualifications: - Knowledge of Excel at an intermediate level (e.g., pivot tables & charts, multiple criteria lookups, nested logical/IF formulas, data cleansing, array formulas, etc.)
- Experience in requirement gathering and ability to write clear and detailed requirement document
- Knowledge of Lean principles and DMAIC methodology
- Experience in MS Access and SQL

title: Program Manager, Integrated Planning, GEMS, NA Startup
description:
Amazon is seeking a Program Manager to join the Startup Integrated Planning team within the Global Engineering, Materials, & Sustainability (GEMS) organization. This team owns the integrated planning function for North America's infrastructure project portfolio, connecting cross-functional workstreams into unified, reliable schedules that guide execution across large-scale new build and expansion/retrofit projects.
This Program Manager will contribute to the strategic evolution of the integrated planning program, helping mature planning as a discipline. The role oversees a team of contracted project planners, setting the bar for quality and ensuring consistent delivery, while balancing program-level strategy, cross-functional influence, and scaling mechanisms.
This is a rapidly scaling environment where processes exist but are still maturing. Success requires strategic thinking, comfort navigating ambiguity, and the judgment to refine and extend existing frameworks. A strong background in integrated scheduling is critical for providing effective program management at this scale.
This role requires up to 50% travel in the US and Canada and availability to work from a corporate office when not traveling. Candidates should either live near or be willing to relocate within a reasonable commuting distance of the office. Relocation assistance may be provided.
Key job responsibilities
Program Strategy & Contracted Planner Oversight
• Shape and advance the workforce and vendor strategy for contracted planners, including capacity modeling, skill-mix optimization, and procurement negotiations that scale with portfolio growth.
• Oversee contracted project planners: set expectations, provide training on planning standards, review deliverable quality, and support escalations.
• Assign and rebalance planners across projects based on priority, complexity, and workload.
• Track project budgets, manage invoicing, and provide funding inputs for planning resources.
Planning Quality, Standards, & Governance

• Ensure weekly planning status reports are accurate, complete, and distributed on time to stakeholders.
• Track planning health via KPI dashboards measuring schedule integrity, milestone adherence, plan variance, and delivery date accuracy.
Standardization & Continuous Improvement
• Develop, maintain, and enforce Standard Operating Procedures for all planning activities.
• Develop and improve planning tools, templates, and AI-driven automations to boost planner productivity and eliminate manual workflows.
• Identify and lead initiatives that advance planning maturity, including automation, tooling, and capability building.
• Capture lessons learned from completed projects and convert them into repeatable, scalable best practices.
Risk Management & Reporting
• Identify and mitigate program-level planning risks; own escalation paths and drive issues to resolution.
• Ensure planners identify cross-functional dependencies and surface risks early, before they become execution problems.
• Develop and refine risk and reporting frameworks that give leadership the signal needed to make portfolio-level decisions
• Provide clear, data-driven status reporting to senior leadership on portfolio-wide planning performance.
Program-Level Cross-Functional Partnership
• Build and maintain program-level relationships with key partner functions (design, operations, construction, launch, IT, engineering) to drive planning adoption and standardization.
• Serve as the planning liaison with partner functions, championing integrated scheduling practices and ensuring planning inputs are prioritized.
• Drive continuous improvement of integrated planning by gathering feedback from partner functions and refining how planning intersects with their workflows.
• Represent the Integrated Planning program in global and cross-functional forums, aligning planning standards and resolving systemic gaps across disciplines.
