title: Rotational Development Program
location: Atlanta, Georgia, United States; Dallas, Texas, United States
description:
About Flexport:
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. That’s why it’s our mission to make global commerce so easy there will be more of it. We’re shaping the future of a $10T industry with solutions powered by innovative technology and exceptional people. Today, companies of all sizes—from emerging brands to Fortune 500s—use Flexport technology to move more than $19B of merchandise across 112 countries a year.
The recent global supply chain crisis has put Flexport center stage as we continue to play a pivotal role in how goods move around the world. We are proud to have the support of the best investors in the game who believe in our mission, solutions and people. Ready to tackle global challenges that impact business, society, and the environment? Come join us.
Build the operational and technical skill set that runs global trade
At Flexport, we believe global trade can move the human race forward. We're shaping the future of a $10T industry with technology and people who understand it end to end. The Rotational Development Program (RDP) exists because that combination — real supply chain fluency plus the ability to build and automate — doesn't exist at scale in the market today. So we're building it ourselves.
This is an 18-month program, not a rotation for rotation's sake. Every assignment is live, revenue-generating work. Every participant leaves with a certification in AI and low-code tooling running alongside their operational and commercial training. And every graduate places into a role with real scope: primarily Account Management, with paths into Automation Engineering, Forward Deployed Engineering/Consulting, Sales Engineering, or a traditional Ops/Sales/Customs track.
What you'll do
You'll rotate through three functions, six months each, with AI/low-code curriculum running continuously across all three:
Gateway Ops (Air or Ocean). Own the shipment lifecycle. Execute bookings, manage exceptions, and hold data integrity to Flexport's standard. Build your first automation and reporting skills through structured coursework running in parallel.
Customs. Become a global trade expert by navigating the complex world of customs regulations to ensure goods comply with international laws. Simultaneously, move into applied technical work: SQL, workflow automation, Lean process improvement, etc.
Sales / Account Management. Take on go-to-market work and build client-facing skills, operating with more independence. Your capstone: identify a real business problem in the function you're sitting in and build the tooling or process fix that solves it. You'll present it to leadership at graduation.
Throughout the program, you'll get:
A day-to-day manager in your current rotation and a Rotation Program Manager tracking your development, with mid-point and end-of-rotation evaluations at every stage.
Certifications in AI/low-code tooling, from foundational bootcamp through applied builds to a capstone project.
Bi-weekly cohort touchpoints and a standing alumni mentor community.
Increased earning potential as you clear program benchmarks
This role is for you if you
Are on track to graduate, or recently graduated, and want to build a career at the intersection of supply chain operations and technology — not just run one or the other.
Are genuinely curious about AI and low-code tooling and want to build real fluency, not just check a resume box.
Can operate with minimal supervision, prioritize a high volume of work, and communicate clearly under pressure.
Want real ownership fast? This program hands you live client and business work from the very beginning — it is not a shadowing or classroom based program.
Have a "compliance-first" mindset. We operate in a heavily regulated industry, and that matters in every rotation.
Ready to build the future of global trade — and the skill set to run it?
Apply now.
Commitment to Equal Opportunity
At Flexport, our ability to fulfill our mission of making global commerce easy and accessible relies on having a diverse, dedicated and engaged workforce. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment regardless of race, color, religion, sex, national origin, age, physical and mental disability, health status, marital and family status, sexual orientation, gender identity and expression, military and veteran status, and any other characteristic protected by applicable law.
Global Data Privacy Notice for Job Candidates and Applicants
Depending on your location, the General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR) and California Consumer Privacy Act (CCPA) may regulate the way we manage the data of job applicants. By submitting your application, you are agreeing to our use and processing of your data as required. Please see our Privacy Notice available at  www.flexport.com/privacy  for additional information.

title: Associate Manager, Facilities Maintenance
description:

In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is seeking a skilled and experienced Associate Manager, Facilities Maintenance to join our team. The ideal candidate will be responsible for installing, maintaining, and repairing electrical systems in commercial, and industrial settings. The Sr Facilities Coordinator will work under the supervision of the Sr Manager Site Operations and will play a key role in ensuring that scheduling of both preventative and corrective maintenance of both hard and soft services happen in a timely manner to keep operations online. These include HVAC, MEP systems, Janitorial, Security, Life-Safety & Site Services. Participation in EHS initiatives is expected as well as being an ambassador of safety throughout the facility.



This is an exciting opportunity to help shape and be part of the growth of a fast-moving company with breakthrough technology and an incredible mission! 



Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Evaluation of service contracts as well as schedule against F&E calibration and PM schedules.

 - Coordinate with external contractors for specialized maintenance and repair tasks.

 - Facilitate inspections of facility systems to identify any repairs or upgrades needed.

 - Maintain accurate records of maintenance activities, repairs, and inspections in CMMS

 - Generate historical reports and develop KPI's for monthly, quarterly, annual dashboards as well as predictive maintenance scheduling purposes.

 - Maintain & participate in CAPA's and RCA's following failure modes around the facility

 - Assist with property management upgrades and contractors as well as supporting external agency audits and inspections for compliance and permitting needs

 - Support Office services varying needs and requirements

 - Take lead in managing Capital Projects coordination of vendors, budget and any delays that can arise in a timely manner

 - Familiarity with BMS and troubleshooting required

 - Oversee the daily operations, maintenance, safety, and physical resources of facilities buildings, grounds, and utility systems

 - Ensure the facility adheres to local, state, and federal building, fire, and health codes (e.g., OSHA, ADA, local ordinances).

 - Coordinate with EHS on safety audits, emergency response planning, and incident resolution

 - Support space utilization planning, office layouts, and other soft services around the facility

 - Assist in budget planning & tracking as well as projecting out TI costs based on Capital projects

 - Possess the flexibility to perform miscellaneous job-related duties as assigned, supporting the broader goals and needs of the facilities group




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Certification: High school diploma or equivalent; technical certifications or an associate degree in a related field nice to have.

 - Experience: Minimum of 8  years of experience in facilities management or equivalent with a strong background in facilities maintenance, HVAC, electrical, plumbing, mechanical systems.

 - Technical Skills: Strong planning ability, excellent  judgment, and clear communication of directions required.

 - Problem-Solving: Excellent problem-solving skills with a proactive approach to maintenance issues. Ability to read and interpret technical documents, schematics, and manuals.

 - Communication: Strong verbal and written communication skills with the ability to interact professionally with clients and team members. Ability to lead and direct outside vendors with professionalism; experience in working with outside contractors.

 - Physical Fitness: Ability to work in various environments, including confined spaces, at heights, and in adverse weather conditions. Capable of lifting and carrying heavy equipment as needed.

About the Role:
As an Inside Sales Representative for our SpringWell water filtration business, you'll help guide homeowners to the right high-performance filtration and treatment solutions. You'll manage a high volume of inbound leads by phone, chat and email, using consultative selling to recommend tailored, trustworthy solutions.
Success in this role comes from learning quickly, taking initiative, communicating clearly, and partnering across teams to refine processes and elevate the customer experience. You'll build trust with homeowners by asking the right questions, simplifying complex product information, and recommending solutions that best meet their needs and goals.
POSITION LOCATION:  Remote in the United States
Compensation includes a  lower base , but total earnings with commissions typically fall  between $90K–$120K , with  senior‑level associates landing toward the top end . Commissions start  immediately  and are based on overall business performance—not individual quotas—creating a more predictable and scalable earning path.
Key Responsibilities:
Be the first voice homeowners hear from SpringWell, engaging inbound prospects by phone, chat, email and scheduled follow-ups, and independently owning the full sales cycle for standard and moderately complex system configurations.
Conduct structured, needs-based discovery to understand each customer's water quality concerns, translating test results and technical detail into plain language a homeowner can act on.
Educate customers on SpringWell products and solutions in a clear, consultative way, and recommend system configurations aligned to their needs, budget and installation requirements.
Progress assigned opportunities through defined sales stages toward close, confidently handling common objections on pricing, installation and product differentiation.
Deliver a professional, trust-building customer experience that drives conversion and builds long-term brand credibility - the kind of conversation that makes someone recommend us to a neighbor.
Maintain accurate, timely CRM records including call notes, follow-ups and pipeline activity, so the forecast reflects reality.
Keep building product depth across system capabilities, installation factors and competitive alternatives, escalating advanced technical scenarios while learning to resolve them independently over time.
Meet or exceed assigned revenue and productivity targets, balancing high inbound lead volume with conversion quality and follow-up discipline, and spotting upsell or cross-sell opportunities within approved product configurations.
Share what you're hearing (recurring questions, objections and water concerns) with teammates, marketing and product, so the whole team gets sharper.
2+ years of inside sales experience, with a track record of results
Proven ability to independently manage a full sales cycle from qualification through close
Strong needs-based discovery and objection-handling skills
Experience selling higher-consideration or consultative products, rather than purely transactional ones
The ability to manage high inbound lead volume while maintaining conversion discipline
Proficiency with CRM systems for managing pipeline, follow-ups and forecasting
Preferred Qualifications:
Background selling water treatment, home services, or other technical home-improvement systems (e.g., HVAC or solar).
Deep understanding of residential water quality concerns and installation requirements.

title: Maintenance Technician
description:
This is a 2nd Shift Position.
Key Responsibilities:
Conduct routine inspections, diagnostics, and repairs on automated machinery, conveyor systems, robotics, and other equipment to ensure their reliable operation.
Perform preventative maintenance activities, including lubrication, calibration, and replacement of parts, to minimize downtime and extend the lifespan of equipment.
Utilize advanced diagnostic tools and equipment to troubleshoot and diagnose issues, identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions in a timely manner.
Collaborate with a team of engineers and technicians to optimize the performance of our automated systems and implement process improvements.
Maintain accurate documentation of maintenance activities, including work orders, equipment logs, and inventory records.
Add PM tasks and parts into the CMMS system.
Follow all safety protocols and guidelines, ensuring compliance with occupational health and safety regulations.
Assist in the training of new technicians and operators on the operation and maintenance of automated systems.
Supports Facility Management (FM) business aspects to assure facilities equipment sustainably performs as designed (i.e. preventive maintenance plans and performance, spare part availability, design improvement planning, random inspections, etc.)
Stay updated with the latest industry trends and advancements in automation technology to provide input on system upgrades and enhancements.
Coordinate to maintain a clean work environment inside/outside the warehouse. Working safely and continually finding ways to improve safety at the facility, following the safety regulations by the company and OSHA.
Issues effective and efficient resolution through communication, analytical, projected, and problem-solving skills.
Must be able to work and troubleshoot (240VAC), (480VAC) and low voltage electrical systems.
Qualifications and Requirements:
High school diploma or equivalent; technical certification or associate degree in a relevant field is preferred.
Proven experience as a maintenance technician, preferably in a highly automated environment such as a distribution center or manufacturing facility.
Strong mechanical and electrical aptitude, with the ability to read and interpret technical manuals, schematics, and diagrams.
Proficiency in troubleshooting complex machinery and equipment, including conveyors, robotics, PLCs, and automated storage systems.
Familiarity with preventative maintenance practices and tools, and the ability to perform routine inspections and repairs on a variety of equipment.
Excellent problem-solving skills, with the ability to analyze issues, identify root causes, and implement effective solutions under time constraints.
Strong attention to detail and ability to follow safety procedures to ensure a safe working environment.
Effective communication skills, both verbal and written, with the ability to collaborate and coordinate with team members and other departments.
Flexibility to work in shifts and respond to emergency maintenance situations as required.

We are seeking a Manager, Global Sourcing – Plastics, Chemicals & Coatings -  to join our team in a highly collaborative and supportive environment. This role contributes to the success of the organization’s global sourcing strategy, ensuring the achievement of cost efficiencies, supplier excellence, and the long-term sustainability of the supply chain.
Each role is a vital part of our supply chain community, with a focus on building trust, nurturing relationships, and fostering teamwork across the organization. As you grow within the role, you will have more opportunities to mentor, support, and guide others, ensuring accounting strategies align with our shared vision for success.
RESPONSIBLIITIES:
Working as a Global Team: Ability to work as part of a virtual global team to collaborate across geographic and organizational boundaries to deliver better business results and share best practices across a global team
Lead the development and execution of global sourcing strategies for assigned categories (plastic extrusions, injection molds, chemicals, and coatings) to deliver cost savings, innovation, and supplier value.
Lead a team of two category managers: One for injection molded & extruded plastics and the other for chemicals and coatings
Establish and maintain strong relationships with key suppliers, ensuring performance standards are met and fostering long-term partnerships.
Strong knowledge of building products industry including best practices and technology trends.
Exhibits subject matter expertise regarding commercial and technology trends, to advise internal users on current and future market capabilities.
Drive negotiations for supplier agreements, with a focus on cost optimization, quality, service, and risk management.
Identify and mitigate risks related to supply chain disruptions, price fluctuations, and geopolitical factors.
Collaborate with internal stakeholders to understand business needs and align sourcing strategies with corporate goals.
Drive cost reduction and efficiency improvements through the identification of new suppliers and innovative sourcing strategies.
Desired incumbent has proven record of leading a team of 2 or more associates in a global strategic sourcing environment.
Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain Operations, Operations Management, Chemical Engineering, or a related field.

description:

Fortune Brands Innovations is hiring a Manager, Product Integrity to join our Connected Products team .  Product Integrity is the team that confirms our connected products — Flo by Moen water devices, Yale and August smart locks, and Master Lock connected padlocks — do what their requirements say they do before they reach a customer. This role leads that team and owns the bridge between requirements and proof: taking what Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance ask for and turning it into tests with a method, a sample size, and a pass/fail criterion.
The role also owns 100% end-of-line testing at the factory, including test fixture design and test software. Depending on test complexity, fixtures are built fully in-house or developed with a supplier.
We are looking for a leader who can spearhead the product quality and integrity function covering test definition, systems integration, test execution, and holding a high product integrity bar. This leader will lead a hardware testing team.  The right person understands the whole product — electrical, mechanical, firmware, and how they interact — well enough to argue a requirement with Product, an interface with Architecture, and the statistics with Reliability, and then run the lab that proves it.
Position location: this position is eligible to work in a hybrid environment out of our North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA locations.
What you will own
The Product Integrity team. Lead a team of test engineers covering production and 100% test, hardware test, reliability test, quality inspection, and overall confirmation of product requirements. You set the direction and the standard; the team executes.
Requirements into tests. Turn every hardware requirement in the PRD — from Product, Systems Architecture, and Compliance — into a testable requirement with a method, a sample size, an acceptance criterion, and a gate. Product defines the design envelope; you define how we test to it.
Gate evidence. Every stage gate (EVT, DVT, PVT) carries your evidence package: what was tested, against which requirement, with what result.
Reliability. Define the reliability test plan for each program and own the statistics behind it: sample sizes, confidence levels, and acceleration factors for environmental testing.
Production test. Develop fixtures and test software that meet approved cycle times, with test limits tied to expected field performance.
Field performance. Review returns and field data, and feed what you learn back into requirements and test plans.
The team and the logistics
Team: test engineers covering production test, hardware test, reliability test, and quality inspection. The lab is in North Olmsted.
Location: North Olmsted, OH or San Francisco, CA. If based in San Francisco, expect occasional travel to North Olmsted.
Travel: ~15%. Travel to factories in Nogales and Tecate, Mexico; Hanoi, Vietnam; and between North Olmsted and San Francisco.
Qualifications
10+ years on connected consumer hardware spanning electrical, mechanical, and firmware.
Experience developing factory test fixtures at both board level and end of line.
Experience writing requirements and V&V plans.
Reliability engineering fluency: accelerated life testing, Weibull and AFR math, sample sizing at a stated confidence, HALT/HASS, thermal, drop, and cycle life. You can design a plan and read a failure.
Production test experience: fixtures, test software, DFT, cycle time, and yield at a contract manufacturer.
Has led a small technical team and is comfortable setting direction for test engineers who are more hands-on than you.
Nice to have
Battery power model development.
Sensor products with calibration and drift requirements.
Sealed or outdoor enclosures.
RF performance characterization.
Certification literacy across safety (UL), RF (FCC), and interop (Matter/CSA); NSF/IAPMO for water products or BHMA for locks.

Our thirst for technology is a part of everything we do. The Data Center Engineering team takes the physical design of our data centers into the future. Our lab mirrors a research and development department -- cutting-edge strategies are born, tested and tested again. Along with a team of great minds, you take on complex topics like how we use power or how to run state-of-the-art, environmentally-friendly facilities. You're a visionary who optimizes for efficiencies and never stops seeking improvements -- even small changes that can make a huge impact. You generate ideas, communicate recommendations to senior-level executives and drive implementation alongside facilities technicians.
With your technical expertise, you ensure compliance with codes and standards, develop infrastructure improvements and serve as an expert in your specialty (e.g., cooling, electrical).
As a Data Center Services Electrical Engineer, you will play a crucial role in the field-level implementation and operational support of Google’s rapidly expanding data centers. You will be responsible for overseeing the design, construction, and commissioning of complex Electrical distribution systems, ensuring projects are delivered safely, swiftly, and with high quality. This involves managing site-level electrical engineering issues, ensuring compliance with design standards and local regulations, supporting quality assurance, and providing technical guidance to vendor teams. We're looking for a strong communicator and collaborator who grows on construction sites and has experience with complex mechanical systems, ideally within mission-critical facilities, heavy industrial, oil and gas, or semiconductor industries.
Ability to be onsite 5 days a week.
Individual pay is determined by factors including job-related skills, experience, and relevant education or training.
US: $144000 - $208000 (USD) + 15% bonus target + equity + benefits
Learn more about benefits at Google .
Own and resolve site-level electrical issues during project execution. Maintain all DC-related electrical design requirements, interface documents, and ensure compliance with the change control process.
Partner with core engineering to integrate new technologies, providing site-specific requirements during BOD development and coordinating schematics with the EOR to meet local requirements.
Understand ongoing electrical project requirements, respond to Requests for Information (RFIs) with the Engineer of Record (EOR), and manage the site bug process with cross-functional teams.
Collaborate with DCDE core teams to develop and manage site electrical designs—from Basis of Design (BOD) to Issued for Construction (IFC)—for new builds, upgrades, and renovations.
Provide technical support to operations and data center services to define electrical design requirements for multiple DC projects from inception to completion.
Minimum qualifications:
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.
5 years of experience in mission critical facility design and construction environments.
Experience in electrical infrastructure.

Professional Engineering (PE) license.
Experience in design, construction, and commissioning of high voltage substations, medium or low voltage electrical distribution systems, AC/DC systems, and associated power management or SCADA tools.
Experience in estimating, electrical design, operation, and commissioning of substations, switchgear, ATP/ATS, emergency power systems and their control systems, power monitoring, and electrical protection.
Experience working with data center equipment and environments (e.g., switchgear, generators, transformers, controls, security monitoring systems, fire safety systems), with a strong understanding of start up/commissioning processes.
Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, Power Engineering, a related technical field, or equivalent practical experience.

Education:

Diversified duties involving a general knowledge of product lines and service parts. Requires use of a wide range of procedures and the exercise of judgment to determine what action should be taken within the limits of standard practice.

We provide professional expertise and high-quality equipment for savvy food service customers. Every Traulsen product is engineered, fabricated, assembled, and tested at our facilities in Fort Worth, Texas.
TOTAL REWARDS PACKAGE
Our total rewards package is broad and offers comprehensive support from health and wellness to retirement and financial stability. For more details see  https://www.itw.com/careers/benefits-compensation/
POSITION SUMMARY
As a member of the Manufacturing Engineering team, the Fixture Designer/Fabricator is responsible for fabricating, assembling, maintaining, troubleshooting, and designing custom jigs, fixtures, and production equipment that support manufacturing operations. This hands-on role plays a key part in improving safety, quality, efficiency, and productivity across the manufacturing process.
This position provides opportunities to develop advanced fixture design, fabrication, and troubleshooting expertise through hands-on training and mentorship, with a path toward increased technical responsibility within the Fixture/Foam Team.
POSITION RESPONSIBILITIES
Fabricate, assemble, modify, repair, and maintain custom manufacturing fixtures, jigs, tools, and mechanical equipment.
Perform welding and metal fabrication using appropriate techniques, including MIG and TIG welding, cutting, grinding, drilling, and fitting components.
Read and interpret technical drawings, blueprints, sketches, and fabrication instructions to build accurate mechanical assemblies.
Troubleshoot, diagnose, and repair mechanical and pneumatic systems, identifying root causes and implementing effective solutions.
Verify dimensions, alignment, fit, functionality, and workmanship throughout fabrication and assembly processes.
Identify and recommend design, fabrication, and process improvements to enhance safety, quality, efficiency, and reliability.
Support the design, development, and continuous improvement of manufacturing fixtures and production equipment.
Utilize hand tools, power tools, welding equipment, machining equipment, and other manufacturing technologies safely and effectively.
Learn and apply CNC routing, CAD software, and specialized foam fixture construction and troubleshooting techniques as required.
Develop and maintain fabrication, operating, maintenance, and project documentation.

The Production Team Leader is responsible for the day-to-day leadership, planning and execution of North American production. The role has full line-management responsibility for the production team and ensures equipment is built safely, meets quality requirements and is completed in line with agreed delivery commitments.
Combining visible shop-floor leadership with practical operational coordination, the position owns production scheduling, capacity planning, Kanban execution and daily production performance. Responsibilities:
Team leadership and development
Lead, coach and develop the production team, setting clear expectations for safety, quality, delivery, productivity and workplace standards.
Manage daily work allocation, attendance, leave planning and performance reviews; address performance concerns with support from Human Resources and the Operations & Engineering Director.
Maintain regular shop-floor presence, build effective working relationships and involve employees in identifying and implementing improvements.
Maintain a team skills matrix and coordinate training and cross-training with Manufacturing Engineering and Engineering to improve capability, flexibility and coverage.
Production scheduling and capacity planning
Own and maintain a documented production schedule showing job priorities, assigned resources, expected effort, key milestones and completion dates.
Review available capacity against workload, employee skills, planned absence and material and engineering constraints; identify risks and propose practical recovery actions.
Assess requests to bring forward, defer or add orders, communicating achievable dates and the impact on existing commitments to Regional Sales Managers and Customer Experience.
Coordinate engineering release and technical readiness with the Engineering Team Leader and material availability with the Senior Buyer before confirming production plans.
Daily production flow and material readiness

Manage daily production flow, work in progress and line clearance, keeping job status and operational records accurate and accessible.
Manage shop-floor Kanban execution, monitor stockouts and trigger replenishment in line with agreed processes; work with the Senior Buyer to review replenishment levels and support assigned purchasing activities.
Identify material shortages and overdue items early, communicate required dates and production impact to the Senior Buyer, and agree follow-up actions; monitor commitments for directly assigned purchase orders and escalate delivery risks promptly.
Coordinate production-team participation in cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation, supporting the Senior Buyer, Logistics and Accounting.
Support cycle counts, the annual inventory count and inventory reconciliation in coordination with Supply Chain, Logistics and Accounting.
Safety quality and workplace standards

Reinforce safe working practices, report hazards and near misses, and follow through on assigned corrective actions with the relevant safety and functional owners.

Job Description:
Job Description
Brooks Instrument ( www.brooksinstrument.com ), an industry leader in flow and pressure instrumentation for critical applications, is seeking candidates for a   Quality Engineer position that will be based at the company headquarters in Hatfield, Pennsylvania (suburban Philadelphia). The company has manufacturing locations in Pennsylvania, Hungary, Malaysia, and Korea, and also maintains sales and service offices throughout the world. Our high-tech products are used in laboratory and process applications in end markets such as: oil & gas, petrochemical, medical devices, waste water, life sciences, and analytical instruments.
Brooks is a division of ITW (Illinois Tool Works), a fortune 200 company. ITW is one of the world’s leading diversified manufacturers of specialized industrial equipment, consumables, and related service businesses. The company has operations in 56 countries and employs over 50,000 employees. These talented employees, many of whom have specialized engineering or scientific expertise, contribute to ITW’s global leadership in innovation. The company is proud of its broad portfolio of nearly 10,000 active patents, and is focused on fully leveraging its highly differentiated business model to deliver solid growth with consistent best-in-class margins and return on capital.
Basic Functions
Serve as the point of contact for quality control planning, development, application, and maintenance of quality standards for processing materials into finished product.  Receive only broad supervision from the department manager and must be capable of advanced decision-making in the manager’s absence.  Product/industry knowledge is broad and support is often given to other departments as needed.  Major challenges include support of the division quality function concurrent with:
Business growth
Best business practices
Introduction of new products and processes
Meeting division continuous improvement goals
Achieving customer satisfaction

Performs basic quality engineering functions, quality audits and sets quality standards for both in-process and finished products and materials.
Reports on quality analyses, product or process non-conformance issues, and recommends necessary corrective actions and procedure changes.
Interface with the plant management staff to ensure that quality improvement activities are in sync with plant quality and operational objectives.
Interface with all hourly employees, supervisors, department managers and division personnel while leading and coordinating improvement activities.
Coordinate the resolution of product quality concerns (process/customer) and facilitate responsiveness to customers.

Support and promote Continuous Improvement Process (CIP) activities.

Employ statistical process controls and techniques to reduce scrap/rework and to drive continuous improvement.

Initiate plans, procedures, and/or actions to prevent/eliminate product and systemic quality problems.

Miller is building a new software-as-a-service business from the ground up: cloud software for the welding and fabrication industry, backed by nearly a century of industry leadership and the resources of ITW. Own delivery of projects end to end
Take high-level, often ambiguous problems, break them into well-defined work, and deliver independently.

Improve software development, testing, and deployment processes.

4+ years of professional software development experience.
Hands-on experience building and operating cloud-hosted web applications or services in production (Azure preferred).

Experience with CI/CD pipelines, automated testing, and monitoring production systems.
Demonstrated ability to own delivery end to end, work through ambiguity, and debug and improve code written by others, including AI-generated and partner code.
Experience using AI-assisted development tools in professional work, with a clear view of where they help and where they don’t.
Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Software Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience.

Experience at a SaaS product company (multi-tenant architecture, subscription products).
Infrastructure as code (e.g., Bicep, Terraform) and containers (e.g., Docker, Kubernetes, Azure Container Apps).
Experience working with or reviewing the work of contract or outsourced development teams.
Exposure to SOC 2, ISO 27001, or secure software development practices.
IoT, connected equipment, or industrial and manufacturing data experience.
Modern front-end frameworks (e.g., React, Angular, Blazor).
Experience building AI or LLM-powered features into products.
Agile/Scrum experience and familiarity with delivery metrics such as DORA.
Curiosity about welding, fabrication, and the people who do the work.

Join a collaborative and growth-focused team where your expertise will directly impact the company’s financial health and operational success. We value innovation, accountability, and continuous improvement.

Job Description:

Illinois Tool Works Inc. StampTech Fasteners TM Division Description:
The ITW StampTech Fastener TM Division serves the major OEMs and Tier suppliers in the North American automotive market.  The division supplies stamped metal fasteners and engineered fastener assemblies that leverage our deep-draw stamping technologies.  The annual revenue for the division is approximately $160M.  Locations include Gallatin, TN, Lexington, KY & Naugatuck, CT.
The Division drives profitability by leveraging its innovative solutions and application engineering.  In addition to ITW’s industry leading research and development capabilities, StampTech Fasteners TM enhances our customers’ competitive advantage by maintaining advanced engineering and manufacturing facilities in North America, exchanging product, process, and benchmarking information with sister units worldwide and continually improving processes, material, and designs to ensure every product provides value and meets customer expectations.

Operates machine tools such as lathes, milling machine, and grinders to machine parts and verify conformance of machined parts to specifications.
Smooths flat and contours surfaces with equipment to fit and assemble parts together and into assemblies and mechanisms.
Connect sensors in dies to ensure quality.
Examines standard or previously used dies, tools, and jigs and fixtures, and recommends design modifications regarding construction and function of part.
Develop specifications and general descriptions for specialty tooling and draws or sketches design of product.
Operates overhead crane.
Maintains a safe, clean, and organized work environment at all times.

Competently perform all tasks with a focus on safety within a fast-paced environment.
Contributes to team effort by focusing on continuous improvement and success for the entire team.

Able to work a 2nd or 3rd shift schedule

Must have own tools.
Ability to comply with all company procedures, policies, and work Instructions.
Experience operating a forklift.

title: Business Process Lead FP&A Transformation
description:
It started with a simple idea: what if surgery could be less invasive and recovery less painful? Nearly 30 years later, that question still fuels everything we do at Intuitive . As a global leader in robotic-assisted surgery and minimally invasive care , our technologies—like the da Vinci surgical system and Ion —have transformed how care is delivered for millions of patients worldwide.
We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function of Position:
The Business Process Lead, FP&A Transformation is the enterprise process owner for how forecasting is designed, executed, and continuously improved at Intuitive. This high-impact individual contributor will lead the transformation of legacy, manual, and fragmented workflows into a simpler, faster, and more accurate forecasting operating model. Working with FP&A leadership across the organization, this role translates business needs into scalable processes, aligns stakeholders, pilots improvements, and drives sustained adoption.
The successful candidate is a systems thinker, process architect, and change leader who creates clarity in ambiguity, challenges unnecessary complexity, and connects process design to measurable outcomes. Success will be reflected in a forecasting model that is faster, simpler, more accurate, well governed, and consistently adopted across FP&A. Innovative thinking to challenge the current state to fully transform the forecast process.
Role and Responsibilities:
Diagnose and Design: Map end-to-end forecasting workflows, handoffs, decision points, rework loops, and elapsed-time gaps.
Identify root causes related to ownership, decision rights, data readiness, calendar design, and manual workarounds.
Design the future-state operating model, including workflow sequencing, inputs and outputs, decision gates, escalation paths, and integration points.
Prioritize, Pilot, and Scale: Build a transformation roadmap that sequences process, data, and automation opportunities by value, feasibility, risk, readiness, and dependencies.
Facilitate prioritization decisions with Finance leadership and clearly communicate trade-offs.
Design and lead pilots with defined scope, success measures, timelines, and learning objectives.
Measure outcomes, refine the approach, and scale proven changes while maintaining process integrity.
Track adoption and outcomes using measures such as cycle time, rework, compliance, engagement, and forecast accuracy trends.
Establish feedback loops and governance to sustain improvements.
Required Skills and Experience:
8+ years of progressive experience in business process excellence, finance transformation, FP&A operations, or a related discipline.
Experience partnering with Data, Systems, or Technology teams without directly owning technical delivery.
Success leading enterprise-scale process redesign from diagnosis through future-state design, pilot, rollout, and adoption.
Expertise with AI/ML-enabled forecasting and responsible integration of model outputs into financial processes.
Experience translating ambiguous problems into process blueprints, RACIs, decision gates, requirements, and prioritized roadmaps.
Lean Six Sigma, BPM, Design Thinking, or formal change management training or certification.
Proficiency with process-mapping tools such as Visio, Lucidchart, or Miro.
Hands-on experience facilitating process mapping and cross-functional working sessions.
Executive communication skills for VP- and C-suite audiences.
This role requires working onsite in our Sunnyvale, CA office Tuesday, Wednesday, and Thursday every week.
Required Education and Training:
Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Business, Operations, Data Analytics, Information Systems or a related field.
Preferred Skills and Experience:
FP&A transformation experience, including forecasting operating model redesign, planning-cycle optimization, or driver-based planning.
Ability to influence without authority across senior leaders, business owners, and technical teams.
Strong analytical capabilities and experience evaluating transformation outcomes.
Experience in a publicly traded technology or medical-device company and a SOX-compliant environment.

title: Lead Director of Photography
description:

We’re a team of engineers, clinicians, and innovators united by one purpose: to make surgery smarter, safer, and more human. Every day, our work helps care teams perform with greater precision and patients recover faster, improving outcomes around the world.
The problems we solve demand creativity, rigor, and collaboration. The work is challenging, but deeply meaningful—because every improvement we make has the potential to change a life.
If you’re ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare , you’ll find your purpose here.
Primary Function
The Lead Director of Photography is a creative and craft leader within Intuitive’s Studio, responsible for advancing the visual language of moving image, motion, and photography across Brand & Creative.
This is a hands-on role for someone with strong visual instincts, a clear point of view, and the range to move between creative development and execution. They can define how something should look and feel, then step behind the camera and make it happen.
The Lead DP partners closely with designers, art directors, writers, producers, editors, motion designers, and, as needed, strategy and social teams. They contribute as a creative peer to senior creative talent and executive creative leadership, confidently advocating for ideas while remaining curious, adaptable, and open to feedback from anyone.
Moving image is central to the role. The Lead DP also leads the development of Studio’s photography practice, creating high-end photography on select projects and elevating standards, practices, and output across the team. This responsibility does not include direct management of photographers.
We’re looking for someone who loves making things, brings fresh thinking, shares knowledge generously, and is as willing to do the heavy lifting as they are to lead the room.
What You’ll Do
Define and evolve our visual language
Advance Studio’s approach to moving image, motion, and photography in close partnership with Creative.
Contribute from the earliest stages of development, translating ideas, stories, and brand objectives into distinct visual approaches.
Bring production craft into the development of ideas, helping shape what we make and how we make it.
Explore new approaches to shooting, editing, lighting, composition, and motion that strengthen storytelling and help evolve the brand’s look and feel.
Lead cinematography and filmmaking
Serve as lead DP across Studio productions, owning the approach to camera, lighting, lenses, composition, movement, coverage, and image capture.
Develop treatments, visual references, shot lists, and storyboards, including rough sketches when useful.
Direct projects, talent, interviews, or scenes when the assignment calls for it.
Lead camera and lighting crews with clear direction, thoughtful preparation, and sound creative and technical judgment.
Adapt to changing conditions while protecting the story, creative intent, and quality of the work.
Elevate the photography practice
Shoot high-end photography on select assignments that benefit from your expertise.
Establish and continually raise standards for lighting, composition, technique, and execution across photography produced by Studio and its partners.
Improve photography workflows, equipment practices, and quality standards.
Guide and mentor teammates and external partners through constructive feedback and shared expertise.
Shape the story through post
Partner with editors and motion designers to develop new approaches to structure, pacing, rhythm, movement, and sound.
Bring ideas and constructive creative challenge that help teammates expand how they tell stories.
Contribute hands-on editing support when needed.
On larger projects, contribute to casting, music, editorial, color, and finishing, staying engaged through final delivery.
Work independently and collaboratively
Independently plan and execute smaller shoots, including assignments without a dedicated producer.
Collaborate effectively within larger teams of creatives, producers, directors, agencies, production partners, and specialized crews.
Recommend an approach and production scale appropriate to the idea, budget, schedule, and intended result.
Prepare thoroughly, solve problems resourcefully, and follow through on commitments.
Strengthen the team
Lead through the quality of your work, the clarity of your ideas, and how you treat people.
Share knowledge and mentor teammates through the work, helping develop their craft, judgment, and confidence.
Give useful feedback, welcome different perspectives, and share credit.
Contribute beyond your own assignments to improve the work and capabilities of Studio and Brand & Creative.
What You Bring
A strong body of work demonstrating accomplished cinematography, high-quality photography, and thoughtful visual storytelling. Please identify your contribution to each project.
Deep practical knowledge of cameras, lenses, lighting, composition, movement, exposure, and image capture.
The ability to connect visual decisions to a story, audience, and creative idea.
The confidence and judgment to present ideas, lead a shoot, and collaborate as a peer with senior creative partners.
The ability to communicate visually through references, treatments, shot lists, storyboards, or sketches.
Working editing proficiency and an understanding of editorial, motion, music, color, and finishing.
Resourcefulness across small independent assignments and larger productions.
Curiosity, initiative, reliability, and a commitment to developing both your own work and the people around you.
How You Work Matters
Low ego is essential. You bring conviction without defensiveness, take feedback seriously regardless of its source, and treat everyone with respect. You remain willing to execute the details and do the heavy lifting, regardless of experience or seniority.
We welcome both emerging creative leaders ready for broader responsibility and experienced practitioners eager to contribute and mentor. Your work, judgment, and approach to collaboration matter.
Travel: Approximately 20% travel is expected, depending on production needs.
Required Skills, Experience, and Training
12+ years of experience
Experience working in or closely with Brand & Creative teams.
A bachelor's degree in film, design, media arts, communications, or adjacent fields; equivalent professional experience is also acceptable.

If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
The Team
The Incubator within Future Forward at Intuitive is a cross-functional innovation group focused on identifying, evaluating, and developing new clinical opportunities and technology platforms. The team operates at the earliest stages of innovation, working from unmet clinical needs through concept generation, derisking, and early development. By partnering closely with engineering, clinical, and business leaders, the Incubator helps shape Intuitive’s long-term growth by advancing transformational technologies that improve patient outcomes and expand access to care.
Primary Function of the Position
The Physician, Corporate Strategy is an MD physician innovator embedded within Intuitive’s Future Forward Incubator. This role translates clinical insight and early-market understanding into new growth opportunities, helping identify unmet clinical needs, evaluate strategic fit, and shape technology concepts from initial hypothesis through early de-risking. We are open to candidates who bring one of two complementary profiles: (1) strong clinical practice experience with exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) deep venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience with an MD background and enough medical/clinical fluency to credibly assess patient care, procedure workflows, and clinician needs. The successful candidate will work closely with engineering, clinical, product, regulatory, reimbursement, and strategy partners to determine which opportunities should advance and how they should be clinically and commercially framed.
Essential Job Duties
Identify, frame, and prioritize unmet clinical needs using clinical immersion, literature review, market sensing, and voice-of-customer input.
Translate physician and patient insights into concise need statements, opportunity hypotheses, clinical workflows, requirements, and early de-risking plans.
Evaluate early-stage opportunities for clinical importance, feasibility, strategic fit, adoption barriers, competitive landscape, and potential business impact.
Partner with engineering and design teams to define clinical use cases, procedural workflows, performance goals, and prototype feedback loops for new platforms.
Lead or support early clinical de-risking activities, including preclinical studies, simulated use, workflow validation, and early feasibility planning where appropriate.
Develop point-of-view assessments on emerging technologies, startups, venture-backed innovation, adjacent markets, and external partnership opportunities.
Collaborate with regulatory, reimbursement, health economics, product, and commercial strategy partners to shape indication strategy and development pathways.
Engage KOLs, clinicians, entrepreneurs, academic innovators, and external partners to validate concepts and inform investment decisions.
Communicate findings to senior stakeholders through clear written recommendations, executive presentations, and data-driven opportunity narratives.
Experience and Qualifications
MD or DO required; active clinical practice is valued but not required for candidates with substantial innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Must demonstrate at least one of the following experience profiles: (1) meaningful hands-on clinical practice or procedural care experience plus exposure to innovation, venture, startups, business development, Biodesign, or product development; or (2) strong venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, corporate strategy, or product strategy experience plus sufficient clinical fluency to evaluate medical needs and care pathways.
Ability to identify unmet clinical needs and convert observations into structured hypotheses, need statements, development plans, or investment theses.
Experience conducting clinician, patient, or stakeholder interviews and synthesizing voice-of-customer input into actionable product or strategy recommendations.
Comfort operating in ambiguous, early-stage environments where the path forward is uncertain and evidence must be built iteratively.
Strong cross-functional influence skills and ability to collaborate with engineering, clinical, regulatory, reimbursement, product, and business stakeholders.
Ability to evaluate clinical workflows, procedure economics, adoption barriers, competitive dynamics, and strategic implications for new technology platforms.
Clear executive communication skills, including crisp written synthesis, structured presentations, and the ability to explain complex clinical concepts to non-clinical audiences.
Curiosity, ownership mindset, and enthusiasm for building new technologies that can transform care delivery and improve patient outcomes.
Biodesign or equivalent needs-based innovation training preferred; experience in venture, startups, business development, product strategy, or corporate strategy strongly preferred.
Education and Training
MD or DO required.
Surgical or interventional specialty training preferred, but not required if the candidate demonstrates strong innovation, venture, startup, business development, Biodesign, or corporate strategy experience.
Clinical practice experience, residency/fellowship training, or comparable patient-care exposure preferred for candidates coming from a primarily clinical background.
Candidates with fewer years of clinical training or limited active practice experience may be considered if they bring substantial experience in early-stage innovation, venture-backed companies, medical technology strategy, product development, business development, or Biodesign.
Biodesign, MBA, MPH, MS, fellowship, or other formal training in innovation, product development, health economics, or business strategy is a plus.

Ability to travel to clinical sites, customer locations, or conferences including international (up to 25%)

The Future Forward organization is Intuitive’s advanced concepts group. We explore emerging technologies, prototype next-generation solutions, and build software experiences that shape the future of robotic-assisted surgery.
If you're ready to contribute to something bigger than yourself and help transform the future of healthcare, you'll find your purpose here.
Position Summary
The Quality Assurance Manager, Audits & Inspections is responsible for the planning, execution, management, and continuous improvement of the company’s GxP audit and regulatory inspection readiness programs supporting late-stage pharmaceutical development.
The role provides hands-on leadership for internal, external, vendor, and study-related audits and establishes a sustainable inspection-readiness program as the organization progresses through Phase 3 clinical development toward regulatory submission, pre-approval inspection, and commercialization readiness.
Working under the direction of the Head of Quality Assurance, the Manager partners with Clinical Operations, CMC, Regulatory Affairs, Pharmacovigilance, Nonclinical, and other functional teams to identify compliance risks, assess inspection readiness, manage audit observations and corrective actions, and ensure the organization and its critical service providers remain prepared for regulatory inspection.
This is a hands-on individual-contributor role requiring demonstrated experience conducting GxP audits and supporting FDA and/or other health-authority inspections.
Key Responsibilities
Audit Program Management
Develop and maintain a risk-based annual and multi-year GxP audit program covering internal functions, clinical studies, CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, pharmacovigilance providers, and other critical GxP vendors.
Plan, schedule, conduct, document, and close GxP audits in accordance with approved procedures and applicable regulatory requirements.
Develop audit plans, agendas, checklists, reports, observations, and follow-up documentation.
Evaluate audit observations for regulatory significance, systemic risk, and potential impact on product quality, subject protection, data integrity, and regulatory submissions.
Track audit findings, commitments, CAPAs, and effectiveness activities through closure.
Perform audit trending and provide periodic reporting of significant findings and emerging compliance risks to QA leadership.
Regulatory Inspection Readiness
Develop and maintain the company’s inspection-readiness program for FDA and other applicable health authorities.
Support readiness for BIMO, GCP, GMP, GLP, GVP and, as applicable, Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Conduct inspection-readiness assessments, mock inspections, document reviews, interview preparation, and functional readiness exercises.
Identify potential inspection vulnerabilities and coordinate remediation activities with responsible functional owners.
Maintain inspection-readiness tools, procedures, playbooks, request-management processes, and supporting documentation.
Support development and maintenance of inspection war-room, document-request, response-review, escalation, and communication processes.
Regulatory Inspection Management
Support the Head of Quality Assurance in coordinating and managing regulatory inspections.
Facilitate inspection logistics, document requests, SME preparation, inspection-room activities, and real-time issue escalation.
Review proposed responses and supporting evidence for accuracy, completeness, consistency, and regulatory defensibility.
Support evaluation and response to inspection observations, including FDA Form 483 observations and comparable health-authority findings.
Track post-inspection commitments and associated CAPAs through completion and effectiveness verification.
Vendor and Partner Quality Oversight
Conduct qualification, routine, for-cause, and risk-based audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, and other GxP service providers.
Evaluate vendor audit findings in the context of sponsor oversight responsibilities and program risk.
Partner with functional owners to establish appropriate remediation and escalation plans.
Support vendor qualification and ongoing performance monitoring based on audit results, quality events, compliance history, and risk.
Compliance Risk & CAPA
Identify emerging or systemic compliance risks through audit findings, inspection trends, quality events, and other quality intelligence.
Support or lead root-cause investigations associated with significant audit and inspection findings.
Review CAPAs for adequacy, proportionality, sustainability, and regulatory defensibility.
Perform or coordinate CAPA effectiveness verification associated with audit and inspection observations.
Escalate significant compliance risks promptly to the Head of Quality Assurance.
Cross-Functional Quality Partnership
Serve as a hands-on QA resource to functional teams preparing for audits and regulatory inspections.
Provide training and coaching to employees and SMEs regarding inspector interactions, documentation practices, inspection conduct, and response expectations.
Collaborate with QMS and GxP QA program functions to translate audit and inspection findings into sustainable improvements to the Quality Management System.
Maintain appropriate independence and objectivity when conducting audits and evaluating compliance.
Promptly escalate requests requiring significant regulatory interpretation, acceptance of material compliance risk, or final compliance disposition to the Head of Quality Assurance before communicating a final QA position.
Required Qualifications
Bachelor’s degree in life sciences, pharmacy, chemistry, engineering, or another relevant discipline.
Minimum of 7 years of progressive pharmaceutical, biotechnology, or regulated life-sciences Quality Assurance experience.
Demonstrated hands-on experience planning, conducting, documenting, and closing GxP audits.
Experience conducting audits of CROs, CDMOs, laboratories, clinical sites, or other regulated service providers.
Demonstrated experience supporting FDA or other health-authority regulatory inspections.
Strong working knowledge of applicable FDA regulations, ICH guidance, and GxP requirements.
Experience with audit observations, investigations, CAPA development, remediation, and effectiveness verification.
Strong technical writing skills and ability to produce clear, evidence-based audit reports and compliance assessments.
Ability to independently evaluate complex compliance issues and appropriately escalate significant risks.
Preferred Qualifications
Experience supporting Phase 3 and late-stage pharmaceutical development.
Experience preparing for or supporting FDA BIMO and/or Pre-Approval Inspections (PAI).
Cross-functional auditing experience spanning GCP, GMP, GLP, and/or GVP.
Experience with clinical-stage organizations operating through outsourced CRO/CDMO models.
Experience developing or implementing formal inspection-readiness programs.
Lead Auditor certification, ASQ certification, RQAP, or comparable professional credential is desirable but not required.
Key Competencies
The successful candidate should demonstrate strong auditor judgment and independence, exceptional attention to detail, regulatory and compliance acumen, concise technical writing, effective interviewing skills, and the ability to distinguish between isolated procedural deficiencies and systemic compliance risk. The individual must be comfortable challenging conclusions when warranted while maintaining productive working relationships with operational teams.

Primary Function of Position:
The purpose of this job function is to serve as a Scientific Research Program Manager (SRPM) in the Digital Business Unit to support research projects, within the United States and across the world, to demonstrate the performance and impact of Intuitive Surgical’s Digital products and services. This role has responsibility to oversee initiation, progress, and conduct of evidence-generation studies to include those conducted by internal scientific teams as well as Intuitive-sponsored studies and studies done in collaboration with external research partners. The SRPM serves as a contact to all parties involved in projects, internal and external.
Roles & Responsibilities:
Manage and execute a portfolio of internal and external collaborative research studies and evidence-generation activities for Intuitive Surgical’s Digital products and services, with or without the assistance of research coordinator(s)
Be responsible for the management of the research studies including project development, budgeting, investigator selection, analysis of potential participant recruitment, preparation of study related documents (e.g., protocols, case report forms, informed consents, research agreements), and management of Institutional Review Board and / or Ethics Committee submissions with follow through to ensure a successful outcome

Maintain study documentation (e.g., correspondence, documentation required by the U.S Code of Federal Regulations (CFR), deviations, budget information)
Plan and manage the project timelines to ensure research studies are conducted in a timely manner and within the project budget
Proactively anticipate and communicate concerns, issues, and delays in the project and develops risk assessment and contingency plans
Prepare project status updates and power point presentations for reporting to internal  and external stakeholders for assigned projects
Prepare reports in support of external and internal steering or advisory committees as needed
Manage publication development, submission, and response to peer review for related to research studies
Ensure compliance with corporate (e.g., SOP's) and regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and US and international guidelines)
Ensure audit readiness of research projects to relevant regulatory and legal standards
Management of Contract Research Organization (CRO) or independent research service providers (e.g., identification of suitable partner(s), development of contracts or statements of work, and management of stakeholders to ensure project success)
Facilitate participation in meetings and reporting with adherence with Intuitive Surgical policies
Review and develop internal processes (e.g., SOPs)
Build, nurture, and maintain relationships with external research partners and stakeholders, which may include but are not limited to surgeon key opinion leaders, operating room staff, hospital and health system administrative and technology leaders, surgical and scientific professional society leaders, and healthcare technology industry partners

Bachelor’s degree or equivalent in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, or computer/data science (required); graduate degree (preferred)
Experience working in the healthcare technology industry in a clinical affairs or scientific research function with evidence of full project management responsibility for at least three years (required)
Five years of experience in the management of research, with experience in clinical research management in both academic/hospital and industry settings (preferred)

Protocol and CRF development experience (required)
Excellent organizational skills with the ability to manage multiple projects with competing priorities (required)
Ability to manage a minimum of three to five research projects across different surgical disciplines and/or products (required)
Excellent communication and interpersonal skills with strong negotiation abilities  (required)
Ability to work independently and across teams whilst keeping open communication with key stakeholders (required)
Strong numerical and literary analytical skills with the ability to assess data and literature
Experience reviewing data sets to evaluate data quality
Experience with studies of health information technologies including artificial intelligence is an advantage
Ability to manage CROs or external consultants

Excellent problem-solving skills and initiative

Collaborate with Cardiac Surgery Program leaders and cross-functional evidence stakeholders to identify evidence gaps, align on evidence priorities, and develop evidence-generation plans

Strong quantitative and literature analysis skills, with the ability to assess data and scientific literature and review data sets for data quality.

Strong problem-solving skills and initiative; English-language proficiency required.

Bachelor's degree or equivalent in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field.

Work may require presence in hospital and surgical/operating room environments. Ability to travel 25%-50% of the time.

Graduate degree in life sciences, medicine, medical sciences, engineering, computer science, data science, or a related field.

Experience publishing research in an academic or industry capacity.
Proficiency in a second language.

Primary Function of the Position
This position requires a candidate with extensive experience supporting evidence generation strategy and execution of clinical studies. The Senior (Clinical Study Manager 4) role will develop and execute strategies for clinical and outcomes research studies to support regulatory approvals and key strategic evidence initiatives. As a member of the Clinical Affairs team, this role will be responsible for working with key stakeholders to design and develop clinical protocols and execute clinical studies (pre-market or post-market studies), with minimal supervision. The candidate will be required to work closely with clinical research associates (CRAs), clinical trial assistants (CTAs) and data management for the conduct and execution of the study, as well as with biostatisticians to review and interpret results of clinical studies, develop clinical study reports, or support the development of clinical publications. During trial execution, the CSM will drive the progress of the trial during site selection, site start-up and through enrollment and follow-up. The CSM will clearly provide guidance to the monitors about monitoring needs, and oversee compliance work on the study. The CSM will also take a leadership role in external communication with investigators and study teams. The ideal candidate will have experience previously managing multi-center, premarket studies in the United States (IDE for 510k or PMA submissions) and utilizing resources to research and scope research topics and to provide recommendations on clinical trial strategy. The candidate is also expected to have experience reviewing, interpreting and summarizing clinical literature.
Essential Job Duties
Responsible for leading assigned clinical research activities
Collaborate with internal stakeholders, investigators and KOLs to develop and review study design and concepts, prepare protocol and study outlines and subsequently driving identified initiatives
Responsible for the planning and execution of the clinical studies including site selection, analysis of potential patient recruitment and projections, creation of study related documents (protocols, case report forms, Informed consents, Clinical trial agreements, study reports), organizing IRB/EC submissions with follow-thorough to ensure successful progress
Responsible for independently conducting clinical studies on schedule and within budget while ensuring high quality and compliance
Perform on-site and remote site qualification visits, site initiation visits, interim monitoring visits and site close out visits.
Conduct clinical study monitoring to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance as well as overall data accuracy in accordance with the study clinical monitoring plan
Complete source data verification of clinical study data entered in an Electronic Data Capture (EDC) system or on a case report form at sites  or in data  listings to ensure regulatory and protocol compliance and overall accuracy
Liaise with sites and support in internal audit/inspection and ensure sponsor audit readiness
Liaise with external vendors and sites to negotiate contracts and budgets in collaboration with the legal team and management
Track study progress and provide regular status reports
Work closely with Biostatisticians on data analysis, interpretation and synthesis, in order to develop clinical study reports and /or support development of scientific publications
Track, process and manage site payments and support in study financial tracking by developing tracking tools as necessary
Organize and lead study meetings and other study activities as assigned
Mentor junior clinical study manager(s); provide guidance to CRAs and CTAs on monitoring and other study needs
Follow corporate (e.g., SOP’s) and regulatory requirements (e.g., GCP and US and OUS guidelines) and proactively manage studies, following such guidelines and requirements
Conduct literature searches and familiarize with literature to stay informed and abreast of relevant scientific/clinical knowledge and/or to determine evidence gaps
Critically appraise scientific literature and write clinical summaries to assist research and the development of clinical strategies and clinical investigational protocols
Review and revise Clinical Operations Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to assist Clinical Affairs leadership with continuous process improvement initiatives
For post-market research, collaborate with commercial groups (i.e., marketing) to understand market trends and utilize information to support of business goals through Clinical Affairs activities
For post-market research, provide scientific expertise to the Health Economics and Outcomes Research department for development of outcomes research analysis (including identification of appropriate diagnosis or reimbursement codes, selection of clinical outcomes for procedures of interest)
Work with clinical investigators to prepare manuscripts, abstracts, slide presentations, and poster presentations for scientific meetings and publications in collaboration with management
Support regulatory submission and approval of pre-market clinical studies and 510k(s), responsible for addressing regulatory body questions on clinical study design and results (e.g., protocol, ICF, eCRF, clinical study reports).
Qualifications
Required Skills and Experience
Previous experience implementing, supporting and managing medical device trials Significant knowledge of clinical and/or outcomes research study design
Strong experience in protocol and ICF development, writing clinical section(s) for regulatory submission
Strong experience in conducting literature searches, reviews and appraisal of the scientific data
Excellent ability to interact with physicians and other professionals inside and outside the company
Knowledge of Good Clinical Practice ICH/GCP and other applicable regulations, fundamental understanding of clinical research and monitoring requirements
Experience negotiating clinical research contracts and budgets
Must be able to work effectively on cross-functional teams
Must be able to travel 25-40% or depending on business requirements
Must be able to manage multiple projects and/or balance competing priorities
Strong communication, presentation and interpersonal skills with high attention to detail and organization
Ability to learn quickly, adapt to shifting requirements, and self-educate on different surgical specialties as applicable to clinical projects (“Self-starter attitude”)
Ability to lead project team consisting of CRAs and CTAs and support management with relevant study updates
Exhibits strong work ethic to help meet aggressive timelines or multiple projects when necessary with a problem-solving mindset
Required Education and Training
Advanced degree in a scientific or bioengineering field (M.S., Ph.D., or M.D.) with minimum 5+ years of clinical research experience; OR
Bachelor's degree in a scientific or bioengineering field with minimum 8+ years of clinical research experience; OR
Minimum of 10+ years of clinical research experience combined with relevant scientific or technical training.
Preferred Skills and Experience
Comfortable in a hospital environment, experience working with nurses and surgeons preferred
Understanding of statistics, statistical methods, and design of experiment is strongly preferred
Extensive experience with close and independent management of pre-market clinical studies (First Human Use or IDE) used for regulatory submissions
Strong track record of KOL management for multi-center studies
Experience working on global or multi-national studies

Our team designs and builds the embedded platform software infrastructure that supports critical
performance, safety and user-facing features of the da Vinci™ Surgical System, Intuitive’s flagship product.
We’re looking for a high energy, experienced embedded software engineer to take technical ownership
across our embedded platform software stack.
In this role, you will lead board bring-up initiatives, drive architectural decision for our next-generation platforms, and serve as a technical anchor for the team – mentoring junior engineers and collaborating cross-functionally with hardware, system software, and FPGA teams. Lead board bring-up activities for next generation-based platforms including bootloader configuration, BSP customization, peripheral driver integration and system validation – taking end-to-end ownership from initial power-on through production readiness.
Own development and drive the technical direction of embedded software for video networking, UI display, and machine learning applications on Linux-based systems – including architectural decisions, code review and performance optimization.
Design and own comprehensive test strategies to validate board functionality, peripheral interfaces, and system performance metrics – including defining acceptance criteria and driving resolution of complex hardware-software integration issues.
Partner with and technically guide hardware engineers to identify, root-cause and resolve board-level issues during early development phases – serving as the primary software interface for cross-functional hardware bring-up
Architect and lead the development of automated test frameworks for board validation and regression testing – establishing scalable infrastructure usable across multiple platform variants.
Mentor junior and mid-level engineers through code reviews, technical guidance, and hands-on debugging support – actively contributing to the growth of the team.
Author and maintain technical documentation including design specifications, bring-up procedures, and failure analysis reports in compliance with FDA-regulated development processes.
