Minimum of 8 years of related experience and a Bachelor's degree; or 6 years experience and a Master's degree; or a PhD with 3 years of experience; or equivalent experience
Expert-level proficiency in C or C++ for embedded systems development, including memory management, real-time constraints, and performance-critical code
Experience in bare-metal, embedded Linux, including kernel internals, custom device driver development, BSP bring-up, and user space application development
Proficiency with embedded development and debugging tools including GDB, JTAG, logic analyzers, oscilloscopes, and cross-compilation toolchains
Proven hands-on experience with hardware interfaces and protocols (I2C, I2S, T1S, SPI, UART, USB, Ethernet, CAN) – including bring-up debugging, and driver development for each
Debugging and root-cause analysis skills, with a track record of resolving complex, multi-layer Hardware-FPGA-software integration failures in time-critical environments
Demonstrated ability to mentor and technically develop junior and mid-level engineers
Effective written and verbal communication skills for technical documentation and cross-functional team collaboration
Preferred Skills & Experience
Hands-on experience with NVIDIA Jetson platforms (TX2/Xavier/Orin or similar) or comparable ARM-based SOCs in a production embedded environment
Hands-on experience with GPU acceleration (CUDA) and hardware-accelerated inference frameworks (TensorRT) in production embedded systems
Experience with QNX RTOS or other real-time operating systems in safety-critical applications.
Proficiency in Python and bash scripting for test automation, bootup design, and build system integration
Demonstrated ability to root cause complex hardware-software interactions
Demonstrated experience in and comfort with all phases of the product development lifecycle including design, implementation, debug, verification, validation, and transfer to manufacturing
Experience designing software products in an FDA or other regulated industry or for mission critical applications; comfortable with concepts of design input, design output, traceability, risk analysis, and mitigations

The Future Forward group within Intuitive Surgical is searching for a Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer to architect, design, and bring up the electronic hardware behind next-generation robotic and vision systems. This role is an exciting opportunity to join a small and innovative team in the early phases of product development, where design decisions made at the schematic and architecture level shape the performance of the entire system.
Joining Intuitive Surgical means joining a team dedicated to using technology to benefit patients by improving surgical efficacy and decreasing surgical invasiveness, with patient outcomes as our highest priority. The Sr. Electrical and Electronic Design Engineer owns analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuit design from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, design verification, and transfer to manufacturing. The ideal candidate designs for electromagnetic compatibility and signal integrity from the first block diagram rather than after the first chamber failure, and can isolate the most difficult board-level and system-level failures on the bench. A strong sense of integrity, care, and attention to detail is required, together with a commitment to developing products of the highest quality.

Design analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits from concept through schematic capture, layout direction, prototype bring-up, and transfer to manufacturing.
Lead schematic and design reviews, and guide PCB layout for signal integrity, power integrity, and manufacturability.
Design for EMC and EMI from the start through grounding, shielding, filtering, isolation, and ESD protection, and support pre-compliance and compliance testing.
Bring up and debug prototypes in the lab, and drive hardware issues to root cause and a verified fix.
Integrate sensors, cameras, illumination, motor drives, and compute platforms in partnership with Mechanical, Firmware, Software, Vision, and Test teams.
Document designs, verification protocols, and results under Intuitive design controls.
Mentor engineers and help shape design practices, reference designs, and the technology roadmap for future products.

Minimum 8 years' experience designing production electronics in the medical device, automotive, or robotics industry, including at least one product taken from concept to production.
Bachelor of Science degree in Electrical Engineering, Electronics Engineering, Computer Engineering, or Computer Science; a Master of Science degree preferred.
Strong schematic design, review, and debug skills across analog, digital, and mixed-signal circuits, using Altium Designer, Cadence OrCAD/Allegro, or Siemens Xpedition.
Practical EMC and EMI design and troubleshooting experience, with working knowledge of standards such as IEC 60601-1-2, CISPR 11/32, or the IEC 61000-4 immunity series.
Solid signal integrity and power integrity fundamentals for high-speed interfaces such as MIPI CSI-2, LVDS, PCIe, USB, DDR, or Ethernet, including impedance control, return paths, crosstalk, and decoupling.
Direct experience with imaging and vision hardware, motor drive electronics, or precision sensing, and with transferring designs into manufacturing and production test.
Confident in the lab with oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, near-field probes, and logic or protocol analyzers, working with embedded interfaces such as I2C, SPI, UART, CAN, USB, and Ethernet, and using Python or MATLAB for test automation and data analysis.
Experience under a regulated quality system such as ISO 13485, FDA 21 CFR Part 820, IEC 60601-1, and ISO 14971, or automotive functional safety such as ISO 26262, is desired; FPGA design experience with VHDL or SystemVerilog is a plus.
Clear communication, strong documentation habits, and the ability to lead technical decisions, work independently, and mentor others.

About the Team
Future Forward Research — Synthetic Data, builds the simulation and data infrastructure that powers Intuitive's autonomous surgical capabilities.
The Role
You'll build the virtual surgical worlds and the data pipelines that train our perception and policy models. Day to day, that means designing simulation environments, generating large volumes of labeled synthetic data, and working with ML engineers to close the sim-to-real gap for robotic surgery. It's a hands-on engineering role at the intersection of 3D simulation, machine learning, and robotics.
What You'll Do
Design and build high-fidelity simulation environments for surgical tasks.
Generate scalable synthetic datasets including photo realistic imagery, segmentation masks, depth, optical flow, and kinematic state — and own their quality, versioning, and delivery.
Implement domain randomization and procedural scene generation to maximize sim-to-real transfer.
Model deformable soft-tissue physics, tool-tissue contact, and instrument kinematics that match Intuitive's platforms.
Partner with ML engineers to define task curricula, reward functions, and evaluation benchmarks.
Develop and refine sim-to-real transfer strategies, and validate simulated behaviors against benchtop phantoms and real systems.
Build reusable tools, APIs, and documentation so the broader team can spin up new tasks without deep simulation expertise.

We care more about real depth in a few of these than shallow coverage of all of them.
Strong software engineering. You write maintainable, tested code in Python, C++ and/or C#, and you're comfortable in a Linux / Git / Docker / GPU workflow.
Hands-on simulation or graphics experience. You've built things in a physics simulator, game engine, or rendering/VFX pipeline — robotics simulators, real-time engines, and offline graphics pipelines all count.
A feel for data and models. You've produced data that trained an ML model (or worked closely alongside that), and you understand how data quality and distribution show up in model behavior.
Working knowledge of 3D and physics fundamentals — coordinate frames, rendering, rigid-body and contact dynamics — enough to reason about why a simulated scene does or doesn't look and behave correctly.
You've likely spent several years building games, simulation, graphics, robotics, or data systems — but we're far more interested in what you've built than in a specific number on your résumé. Primary Function of Position
The DaVinci Specialist (DVS) will provide expert clinical & technical support, build, customize and coordinate education & training to physicians, nurses, and hospital staff on the use of DaVinci surgery, devices and therapies. This role partners closely with the sales team, specifically the Clinical Sales Representative and Clinical Sales Manager, to ensure safe and effective product adoption and quality control while driving positive patient outcomes.
The DaVinci Specialist is a dedicated program execution & clinical education partner for hospitals running a da Vinci robotic surgery program.   Based on its expertise, this role focuses on identifies and tailors the nature and extent of staff in-servicing, day-to-day program execution, technology onboarding and operational support, communicating identified needs to hospital OR operations and leadership. The DVS will work alongside the daVinci Clinical Sales Representative .
Essential Job Duties
Collaboration & Field Partnership (Within a CSM Team)
Partner with the local CSR/CSM and cross-functional business partners to create, own, scale and execute best practices and deployment of ecosystem resources.
Lead account support plans that drive safe program execution and increase customer autonomy over time, including setting objectives, timelines and resources for relevant customers, in consultation with CSR/CSM.
Identify, solicit and provide field feedback and customer insights to internal teams to improve training, support resources, and customer experience.
Support adoption of digital solutions by helping customers build comfort and capability through in-servicing and troubleshooting.
Clinical & Technical Support
Identify and provide on-site, non-scrubbed operating room support for procedures utilizing the da Vinci Surgical System and associated technologies.
Support OR teams with room readiness and procedural workflow, including system setup support, docking workflow support, and intraoperative troubleshooting.
Serve as a clinical product expert to help ensure optimal, safe system use and adherence to applicable IFUs, hospital policies, and safety protocols.
Motivate and support adoption of advanced instruments and accessories by ensuring teams understand proper setup, handling, and intended use.
Partner with and promote consistent readiness and workflow by supporting day-to-day execution of the robotic program, coordinating with OR leadership, nursing, SPD/sterile processing, and biomedical teams.
Assist with operational support activities such as facilitating appropriate internal handoffs for service needs.
Ensure the right stakeholders are aligned (OR, SPD, biomed, IT) for successful day-to-day operation and new technology onboarding to help reduce friction.
Maintain accurate internal documentation of support activities per company process (e.g., case support notes, training records, service/escalation tracking).
Training & Education (Care Team Enablement)
Determine the need for, customize and deliver customer-specific hands-on training and in-services to nurses, surgical technologists, SPD teams, and other care team members on safe and effective use of da Vinci platforms and associated technologies.
Support onboarding and education for new users through structured training touchpoints (e.g., new staff orientation, refresher training, workflow standardization).
Lead new site start-ups by identifying and delivering onboarding programs and coordinating training logistics with the CSR/CSM and hospital stakeholders.
Support new technology installs by coordinating readiness activities and providing post-install education to care teams.
Act as a resource for ongoing education, product updates, and workflow optimization.
Escalation & Customer Issue Management
Analyze and leverage utilization, turnover, and other relevant case data to recommend operational changes to customers
Provide first-line support and expertise for common setup and workflow issues during live cases and training sessions.
Identify, resolve and where necessary escalate issues appropriately to internal partners (e.g., Technical Support, Field Service, Clinical/Medical counterparts).
Market & Clinical Insights
Collect and communicate customer feedback and experiences to clinical counterparts and internal business partners.  Prioritizing, distilling and reporting relevant customer feedback, in real time.
Stay up to date on clinical literature, competitive products, and evolving treatment guidelines.
Assist in clinical trial support when required.
Assist in field action activities when necessary.
Required Skills and Experience
Experience: 2+ years in an operating room-related role
Clinical experience is preferred.
Experience as a robotics coordinator, surgical assistant, and/or surgical nurse plus industry experience strongly preferred.
Understanding of soft tissue anatomy & procedures.
Exhibit a working knowledge of typical hospital policies.
Excellent communication, teaching, and interpersonal skills.
Strong problem solving and troubleshooting skills.
Ability to work in high-pressure environments (managing multiple ORs) and coordination of multiple tasks at one time.
Adaptability to evolving technologies and complex procedures.
Team oriented with a commercial mindset.
Willingness to travel up to 40%. Primary travel will be within a CSM team.
Ability to travel within a Clinical Sales Manager team geography, supporting multiple hospitals.
Flexibility to support early starts, after-hours cases, and weekend procedures based on customer need and territory utilization.
Required Education and Training
Associates degree. Bachelor’s degree preferred.
Degrees in (RN, PA, NP, RT, or other clinical credentials) are welcomed.
Working Conditions
Ability to stand for extended periods and provide in-person case support within an operating room (OR) environment, which includes pushing, pulling, lifting and squatting.

Sanitation:

Tree house Stackers Clean Douglas Clean Surge Room Clean the Roll Hart Wrappers Product pumps and pipes Natecs PFM Wrappers Oil System Triple Tube and Barrel system CIP Units Brenton OEE System COP tanks

Role purpose. The Manager, Canada Cheese & Dairy will lead the procurement strategy and commercial management for the full Canadian Business Unit portfolio of Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix. The role is accountable for category value delivery, supplier strategy, supply continuity, cost competitiveness, cross-border compliance and cross-functional execution across maintenance, productivity and innovation workstreams. The Manager will connect the Canadian Business Unit with North American category experts, translate market and business requirements into a Canada-specific sourcing strategy, and ensure clear information flow between Procurement and Canadian Business Unit leadership. Job Description
Primary Responsibilities:
Strategic Sourcing & Commercial Management • Own and execute end-to-end sourcing strategies for the Canadian Cheese and Dairy portfolio, including market analysis, supplier segmentation, sourcing events, negotiations, contracting, implementation and ongoing commercial governance. • Develop and maintain a multi-year Canada sourcing strategy aligned with North American category strategies while reflecting Canadian market dynamics, business priorities, regulatory requirements and supply-chain constraints. • Partner closely with North American category experts to leverage market intelligence, supplier relationships, sourcing scale and best practices, while maintaining clear accountability for Canadian Business Unit outcomes. • Lead complex and high-value negotiations, supplier award recommendations and contracting, ensuring appropriate cost, service, quality, capacity, flexibility and risk protections. • Develop and communicate a strong point of view on Canadian and North American cheese and dairy markets, including commodity drivers, manufacturing economics, capacity, trade flows, tariffs and regional supply-demand dynamics. • Ensure pricing, contracts, specifications, supplier records and sourcing decisions are accurate, current and compliant within relevant source-to-pay and business systems.
Canada Cheese & Dairy Portfolio Responsibilities • Lead procurement for Cheese, Dairy Powders, Cheese Powders and Cream Mix across the Canadian Business Unit, balancing cost, functionality, specification, service and supply requirements. • Provide portfolio-level governance across maintenance, productivity, innovation, reformulation, promotions, plant transitions, capacity changes and new business opportunities. • Partner with R&D, Quality, Manufacturing, Commercial, Finance, Materials Management and the Canadian Business Unit to define requirements, technical specifications, project economics and implementation timing. • Lead supplier and procurement readiness for innovations, renovations, reformulations, promotions, plant transitions, product maintenance and business continuity initiatives. • Assess and manage category complexity, including product specifications, lead times, minimum order quantities, yields, conversion economics, supplier capacity and cross-border supply lanes. • Build and maintain contingency strategies for critical materials, suppliers, manufacturing locations and logistics routes serving Canada.
Cross-Border, Quota, Tariff & CDC Managemen t • Own procurement coordination for cross-border cheese and dairy flows into and out of Canada, ensuring commercial plans reflect applicable quotas, tariffs, customs requirements and regulatory obligations. • Lead procurement management of Canadian Dairy Commission (CDC) requirements and related processes, working with internal and external experts to support compliant and cost-effective execution. • Monitor quota availability, tariff exposure and cross-border cost implications, incorporating these factors into sourcing decisions, budgets, supplier negotiations and risk assessments. • Coordinate with Trade Compliance, Legal, Finance, Logistics, customs brokers, suppliers and category experts to resolve cross-border issues and maintain continuity of supply. • Maintain clear governance, documentation and escalation paths for quota, tariff and CDC activities affecting the Canadian portfolio.
Forecasting, Inventory & Materials Management • Provide leadership and governance for coordination with Materials Management on forecasts, inventory policies, material requirements, lead times, capacity and availability across the Canadian portfolio. • Lead cross-functional resolution of supply disruptions, delivery issues, allocation constraints and inventory imbalances, with clear escalation, ownership and recovery plans. • Drive improvements in forecasting discipline, inventory visibility, supplier communication and working-capital performance in partnership with Mount Royal Planners, Materials Management and Finance.
Supplier Relationship & Performance Management • Own strategic relationships with key Cheese and Dairy suppliers serving the Canadian market. • Support the management of key Canadian Semi-Finished Goods suppliers, including Agropur and other strategic partners, in close alignment with the relevant North American category owners. • Define supplier strategies and performance expectations across cost, quality, service, delivery, capacity, innovation, sustainability and risk. • Lead strategic business reviews, negotiations, performance interventions, improvement plans and resolution of escalated commercial or supply issues. • Establish fit-for-purpose supply agreements, pricing mechanisms, service commitments, capacity protections and risk mitigations. • Develop a resilient, competitive and capable Canadian supply base, including qualification of alternatives and management of supplier concentration or dependency risks. • Build collaborative supplier relationships that enable innovation, continuous improvement, transparency and long-term value creation.
Canadian Business Unit Leadership & Stakeholder Management • Act as the principal Procurement partner for Cheese & Dairy within the Canadian Business Unit, aligning category strategies and sourcing actions with Business Unit priorities. • Participate in Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team sessions as the Cheese & Dairy Procurement representative. • Cascade relevant market, supplier, cost, supply, policy and project information into the Canadian Business Unit Leadership Team, and communicate decisions, priorities, risks and required actions back to Procurement and North American category teams. • Influence senior cross-functional stakeholders and resolve competing priorities across Procurement, Materials Management, Manufacturing, R&D, Quality, Finance, Commercial and the Canadian Business Unit. • Prepare and deliver monthly business updates to the Associate Director, Cheese & Dairy, covering market developments, category performance, productivity, supplier performance, inventory and supply risks, strategic decisions and next steps. • Represent the category in annual planning, productivity, innovation, risk and business review forums.
Project Management & Continuous Improvement • Lead cross-functional programmes related to productivity, innovation, portfolio maintenance, supplier transitions, specification changes, risk mitigation, supply continuity and process improvement for Canada. • Establish governance, milestones, resources, decision forums and escalation paths for priority category initiatives. • Drive improvements in procurement processes, category analytics, supplier performance management, contracting, forecasting, inventory coordination and cross-border execution. • Ensure compliance with procurement policies, sourcing governance, approval requirements, contracting standards, supplier due diligence and internal controls.

Location
New Ulm, Minnesota – Home of  VELVEETA and DELI DELUXE!
Work Schedule
Monday – Friday work week, 2nd shift, afternoons
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
The Senior Rotating Analyst is responsible for all finished product testing. Occasionally may also be responsible for blender testing, blender standardization, problem solving and in process testing. Works from brief verbal and complex written instructions and is expected to exercise individual judgment and resolve questions independently in a timely manner. When 1 to 2 lines are running, Analysts work alone – therefore they must exercise good judgment with all aspects of in process and finished product testing when issues arise. Rotating Analysts are expected to work between areas and help out when needed. Must have good written and oral communications skills. Work requires mathematical skills including fractions, decimals and knowledge of personal computers. Work is expected to meet the high standards of Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal parameters. Must be able to perform sensitive adjustments of complex controls requiring skill in fine tuning of the process variables.
Job Responsibilities:
Regular Moisture/Finished Product Testing:
Performs five-hour vacuum moisture tests or NIR moisture test on every hourly sample for every product run daily. Responsible for all accurate recording of data and documenting out of standard results. Performs recheck testing on all samples out of standard and special samples. Calculates all results by use of personal computers and makes decisions accordingly. Performs moisture and fat tests on raw material cheese as requested by supervisor. Responsible for cleaning, labeling and preparation utensils and equipment. Responsible for cleaning and maintaining work area at all times. Responsible for performing pH tests on hourly samples, as specifications require. Accountable for all retests and monitoring of equipment. Responsible for performing extraneous tests as required on finished product and raw materials. Projects as requested by supervisors.
Fat Testing:
Performed tests, requires safety awareness at all times due to the chemicals being worked with. Safety eye wear, apron and gloves are mandatory in this area. Performs fat tests on samples as required by specifications. Performs fat tests on blender samples on an as needed basis. Responsible for all special fat testing required on natural cheese samples. Performs fat testing on ingredients and liquid loads as specifications require. Accountable for all data entry, calculating and recording of fat results. Accountable for any data that is out of standard and must be retested and/or special samples received. Responsible for knowledge of all fat testing procedures, techniques and methods as prescribed by Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards.
Salt and Lactose Testing:
Preforms tests on samples as required by specifications. Accountable for all data entry, calculating and recording of all Salt and Lactose results. Accountable for any data that is out of standard and must be retested and /or special samples received. Responsible for knowledge of the procedures, techniques and methods as prescribed by Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Responsible for all critical control point checks performed in areas. Responsible for cleaning and maintaining work area and equipment at all times.
Rapids Area:
When required, responsible for accurate testing of blend samples for moisture and fat on a timely basis. Methods used include NIR, vacuum oven and Roccal Method. Concise and quick decisions must be made based on these results. Responsible for solving blender errors/problems using G40 personal computer. Responsible for activating, adding and deleting liquid load data in the G40 for proper blender standardization. Responsible for maintaining and operating the G40 back up and special standardization programs on the personal computer. Prepares in process testing tools for each blender standardization. Maintains an ample supply of folded, numbered and weighed foils daily. Responsible for knowledge of all methods, techniques and procedures according to Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Responsible for maintaining and cleaning work area at all times.
Hot Tests/In-Process Testing:
When required, performs in-process testing on certain blenders on a timely basis. Accountable for all decisions made for corrections at the cooker to adhere to 100% compliance for every product. Timely decision making skills are utilized. Utilizes various methods for testing including a vacuum oven and NIR units. Performs in process testing on wet mix and liquid loads. Responsible for additions and data reporting. Personal computers and mathematical skills are used to compute data. Utilizes a personal computer for computing calculations on all vacuum tests. Responsible for an in-process test on certain blenders of standardized product. Communicates correction/additions to the cook room cooks. Responsible for checking all corrections. Responsible for knowledge of proper methods, techniques and procedures according to Kraft Heinz, AOAC and legal standards. Accountable for maintaining and cleaning of work area at all times. Responsible for all critical control point checks performed in areas.
Responsibilities:
Work on programs and other requests. Record cooker steam out results and grade the steam out pads. Test standardized cream, cream whey and WPC as required by the specifications and record results. When needed, performs blender checks as required. Involves retesting blender samples for moisture and fat. Responsible for the salvage of blender, moisture, fat, NIR, naturals and raw material samples. Miscellaneous testing required on ingredients as to adhere to the specifications. Preparation of solutions for miscellaneous testing (pepsin, acid pH). Responsible for cleaning five-hour ovens centrifuge, grading room buckets, fat bottles, beakers, moisture pans and all other lab dishes and glassware. Prepares fat (Roccal) solution and fills acid bottles. Monitoring and cleaning of water bath and acid dispensers. Monitor the hazardous waste that is produced by some of the testing and dispose of it properly. Responsible for air exposures and swabs for start-up, qualifications and regular production. Responsible for entering COA results into SAP for incoming ingredients. Responsible for net content scale and weight verifications.
Maintenance:
Responsible for all thermometer checks in the Laboratory. (Primary, secondary and calibration thermometers) for start-up. Responsible for all balance and scale calibrations in Laboratory for start-up.
General Requirements:
Computer skills, operating knowledge of SAP, Quality Suites, Excel, demonstrated math skills (including decimals, fractions, divisions) and decision-making skills. Person must be willing to train in other areas of the Lab (Special Testing, Bacti, etc.) or take upgrading when offered.
Safety:
Follow all OSHA and safety procedures. Working with acids, heat and glassware are a safety hazard. Knowledge of proper treatment, response, and care and preventative measures required.
Equipment Operated:
Primarily responsible for the safe and efficient operation of NIR units, G40, 6500, personal computers, vacuum ovens, centrifuges, water baths and scales.
Value of Material:
Lack of responsible decision making skills and inattention to required duties may result in substantial monetary losses, delays or inconveniences. The results not are readily detectable until 10-20 hours later.
Lifting Requirements:
Moderate - Lifting requires handling materials up to 20 lbs. frequently or less and up to 45 lbs. infrequently.
Working Conditions:
Fair – Standing throughout the shift required of several job areas. Hazards are present when working with Laboratory testing reagents and disposals. Work may be a fast pace and hectic; therefore, cautions and common sense must be exercise. Exposure to noise and unfavorable working conditions (such as wet slippery floors) at times.
Training:
The Senior Rotating Analyst will have a three phase training period; 30 days, 3 months and 6 months. An evaluation will be done after each phase. The successful Senior Lab Analyst will be able to demonstrate the following competencies throughout each phase of training:
30 days
Decision making skills
Technical aptitude
Math and computer skills
3 months
Effective communications skills
Dependability
Analytical skills
6 months
Self-confidence
Team working skills
Versatility

Job Description
Job Purpose
​​The Principal Scientist for CX Product Insights is the technical authority and methodologist for consumer experience research for Away From Home initiatives. You architect fit-for-purpose CX learning strategies across the end-to-end product lifecycle, from front-end exploration and ideation through launch readiness, ensuring methodological rigor, evidence quality, and decision-ready synthesis that accelerates innovation. You translate consumer needs into clear product and packaging experience requirements, influence cross-functional teams toward consumer- and customer-centric decisions, and balance speed vs. rigor based on decision risk. You elevate functional capability through coaching, playbooks/toolkits, and ways of working, and guide internal teams and suppliers to the right level of rigor for the decision at hand. You’ll partner closely with R&D (Product & Process Development, Packaging, Sensory), Marketing/Brand, Insights, Analytics, Culinary, and external suppliers to ensure consumer learning is converted into practical product, packaging, and technical decisions.
​
Essential Functions & Responsibilities
​​Provide CX technical leadership for the Away From Home team, defining key learning needs tied to business and technical decisions at each development milestone.
​Serve as subject matter expert (SME) for product and packaging design consumer research, bringing deep methodological expertise across qualitative and quantitative approaches.
​Architect end-to-end CX learning plans from upstream exploration to downstream validation, with clear decision framing, success criteria, and evidence standards aligned to risk and timelines.
​Translate complex consumer experience insights into actionable experience requirements that inform product and packaging design, managing tradeoffs and defining what success looks like.
​Lead high-stakes stakeholder readouts with compelling decision narratives, synthesizing insights and tailoring technical depth to both executive and technical audience.
​Serve as technical consultant on away from home product and pack methods and research design, best fit to the learning objectives that align with specific operators and venue types.
​Evaluate, pilot, and standardize emerging CX methods and analytics (including vendor capabilities), documenting best practices, limitations, and evidence thresholds before scaling.
​Coach and upskill scientists and partners through playbooks, training, and consultative support that embed CX rigor, curiosity, and storytelling excellence across functions.
​Oversee vendor strategy and performance: capability alignment, quality assurance, data integrity, and delivery expectations.
​Manage multiple simultaneous workstreams with disciplined prioritization, documentation, and strong stakeholder communication in a fast paced innovation environment.
​Provide continuity and backup coverage for the CX leadership team as needed.
​Ensure compliance with data integrity, privacy, and internal research governance requirements.​
Expected Experience & Required Skills
​​Bachelor’s degree minimum (Consumer Behavior, Psychology, Marketing Research, Engineering, Food Science, Human Factors, Industrial Design, or related STEM field), advanced degree preferred
​Minimum of 8+ years (BS), 7+ years (MS) or 6+ years (PhD) in consumer/product research, consumer experience, or applied insights supporting innovation, product development and commercialization.
​CPG or food & beverage experience strongly preferred, with demonstrated progression in technical expertise, including independent research strategy development, methodological leadership, and influencing cross-functional product and packaging innovation decisions.
​Experience in product consumer research to support away from home product R&D initiatives
​Recognized expertise across CX research methods (qualitative and quantitative), including end-to-end study design, instrument development, analysis planning, synthesis, and storytelling; ability to select methods based on decision risk and learning objectives.
​Proven ability to influence product and packaging innovation/renovation decisions by translating consumer needs into clear experience requirements and decision criteria
​Direct experience in consumer research methodology focused on packaging technical design
​Strong technical oversight: expert scoping, critical review of study quality, and ability to QA vendor work (methods, analysis, and interpretation).
​Clear, succinct communication across audiences, including leadership-level implications, tradeoffs, and uncertainty/limitations.
​Demonstrated capability building: coaching, technical training, and establishing best practices/standards in a matrixed organization.
​Strong cross-functional leadership and stakeholder management; sound escalation judgment and ability to correct misinterpretations of evidence.
​Strong prioritization and independent execution across a complex portfolio with multiple concurrent projects.
​Working proficiency with quantitative/statistical interpretation used in CX and product testing; comfort using and overseeing common research platforms and analysis tools (survey/testing platforms, analysis packages, dashboards/BI), consistent with internal standards.
​Ability to travel up to 20% of the time.​
Work Environment & Schedule
We believe the office is a critical driver of innovation, connection, and development, but also realize providing flexibility to our employees is critical. To create a more agile and modern workplace, this position will be able to work virtually for up to two days each week and will be expected to work in-person at the assigned work location at least three days per work week.

Follows procedures to immediately engage Designated Responsible Individuals (DRIs) for appropriate communication, reporting, and incident management of data center technical or safety related incidents with direct-line management, internal business partners, and impacted engineering group contacts. Participates in bridge calls to provide details on incident status and executes on-site follow-up actions as directed if necessary. May leverage learnings to contribute to the improvement of quality of service and support.   Coordinates training packages for technicians on procedures for installation, deployment, upgrade, refresh, simple change, decommission and/or replacement of infrastructure cabling, network, storage, or server equipment. Provides guidance to technicians for developing an effective execution order of assigned tasks and ensures technicians have access to tools and/or supplies required to perform work. title: Logistics Technician
description:
Overview
As a Logistics Technician, you will perform cycle audits, execute incoming/outgoing deliveries, coordinate security escorts for third-party vendors, and document inbound and outbound deliveries. This opportunity will allow you to deepen your knowledge of inventory management principles, warranty process management, data bearing device destruction and advance your career in the process.
Microsoft’s Cloud Operations & Innovation (CO+I) is the engine that powers our cloud services. As a CO+I DIAT, you will perform a key role in delivering the core infrastructure and foundational technologies for Microsoft's online services including Bing, Office 365, Xbox, OneDrive, and the Microsoft Azure platform. As a group, CO+I is focused on the personal and professional development of all employees and offers training and opportunities including Career Rotation Programs, Diversity & Inclusion training and events, and professional certifications.
Our infrastructure is comprised of a large global portfolio of more than 200 Data Centers in 32 countries and millions of servers. Our foundation is built upon and managed by a team of subject matter experts working to support services for more than 1 billion customers and 20 million businesses in over 90 countries worldwide.
With environmental sustainability and optimization at the forefront of our data center design and operations, we continue to grow and evolve as we meet the ever-changing business demands that hold Microsoft as a world-class cloud provider.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more. As employees we come together with a growth mindset, innovate to empower others, and collaborate to realize our shared goals. Each day we build on our values of respect, integrity, and accountability to create a culture of inclusion where everyone can thrive at work and beyond.
In this environment, you may be asked to go on business travel to support other metros periodically, 0-25% of the time and have the ability to work 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours that may include evening, nighttime, weekends and/or holidays
Microsoft is unable to sponsor a work visa for this role due to the nature of the role's job duties
Responsibilities
Customer Service
Maintains a strong focus to understand the impact of their work when completing tickets and assigned Inventory and Asset Management (IAM) tasks. Ensures IAM tasks are completed accurately as requested, as well as meet company and industry standards and policies. Becomes familiar with guidelines set by the Microsoft contractual agreements with suppliers and maintains a strong customer focus. Recognizes potential stakeholder impact of external and internal events and issues, communicates potential impact, and plans for impact accordingly.
Data Bearing Device (DBD) Destruction Performs destruction of data bearing devices (DBD) following all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) and Microsoft policies as necessary. Ensures DBD serial number matches with database. Supports decommissioning servers, maintaining compliance and meeting Service Level Agreements (SLAs).
Fleet Management Performs weekly vehicle inspections.
Inbound and Outbound Logistics
Performs data entry to document inbound and outbound packages. Executes incoming/outgoing deliveries as instructed by management (e.g. purchase order [PO] receiving, Rack Movement Supervisor [RMS] activities). Ensures accurate documentation of incoming and outgoing deliveries as well as records. Applies appropriate customs documentations and standards for outbound packages.
IT Inventory Management Develops working knowledge of stock control and inventory management practices and procedures. Performs cycle audits and data corrections to ensure all inventory controls are met and helps report and reconcile inventory discrepancies. Ensures detailed physical inventory tracking and staging, identifying opportunities to improve inventory and address space constraints. Performs material movement, including shipping/receiving and inventory management per standard process.
Operational Excellence Follows existing procedures to run processes and ensures execution with consistency, accuracy, and timeliness of delivery. Completes required security and data management training while complying with security and data management procedures/policies. Participates in training for relevant site-specific procedures and tools (e.g., forklift, pallet jacks, technician on-hand processes, inventory maintenance software, RMA portals, Rack Movement).
Procurement Notifies management about ordering stock shortages. Escalates any issues to management.

Engages in Task Hazard Analysis (THA) consistently for every task to be performed and ensures sign off from appropriate person for any related risks. Conducts rack movement activities, supporting training on devices and tools and upholding safety standards. Follows established protocols on dealing with unsafe materials out of containment, leveraging safety alert system, escalating to management, and properly disposing of them.
Tactical Shift Management Performs assigned tasks and escalates issues during high-volume work activity or escalation-based situations. Seeks guidance from management before proceeding with the next step of a process. Begins monitoring inbound and outbound schedules, escalating deviations from scheduling, with guidance.
Travel and Work Hours (Applies to but is not limited to US-based Data Center roles) May travel up to 25%, typically domestically to and from multiple locations during the workday. Working 12-hour shifts, including shift assignments during non-standard business hours such as evenings, nights, weekends, and holidays.
Warranty Process Management Engages supplier to initiate warranty claim when automation is not available and processes the orders. Processes failed vendor hardware devices using online/other tools, including information processing, packaging, shipment, and receipt of return for Return Merchandise Authorization (RMA) and non-RMA devices. Performs manual return processes for non-RMA failed parts. Begins to perform manual ordering processes of Original Equipment Manufacturer (OEM) parts. Follows all Service Level Agreements (SLAs) related to RMA and non-RMA warranty process.

To meet this legal requirement, and as a condition of employment, the successful candidate’s citizenship will be verified with a valid passport
This position is not eligible for visa sponsorship. Candidates must have authorization to work in the United States that does not now or in the future require employer sponsorship.

title: Paid Social Advertising Manager
location: United States, Washington, Redmond; United States, California, Mountain View
description:
Overview
Do you live and breathe social? Know what makes someone stop scrolling, and how to turn that moment into measurable business results? Believe that reliable social advertising starts with the platform and the audience, not a resized TV spot? We are looking for a creative, data-driven, and highly accountable paid social professional to join our Windows Devices & Services (WDS) Creative & Integrated Marketing team. We believe successful campaigns are built through supportive partnership, clear ownership, candid feedback, inclusive decision-making, and disciplined execution.
The Paid Social Advertising Manager will be the team's subject-matter expert and strategic lead for paid social across Windows campaigns. This person will shape how our campaigns show up on social platforms, from audience and channel strategy through leading social-first creative development, creator partnerships, launch, optimization, and learning. You will work across platforms including Meta (Facebook and Instagram), TikTok, YouTube Shorts, Snapchat, Reddit, X, etc and help the team stay ahead of emerging trends, formats, and AI-driven approaches.
This role will work closely with other advertising campaign managers, creative leads, product marketing, integrated marketing, media, social and community, research and insights, analytics, legal, platform partners, and external creative and media agencies. The candidate combines deep, hands-on platform fluency with sharp marketing/creative judgment, can translate business objectives into paid social strategies that perform, and is as comfortable in a creative review as in a results dashboard.
About the Team:
The Windows Devices & Services (WDS) Creative & Integrated Marketing team sets a high bar for craft while supporting one another, staying curious, and bringing positive energy to complex, fast-moving challenges. We value people who simplify ambiguity, anticipate what is needed, respectfully push for clarity, and create the conditions for teams and agencies to do quality work. The team translates product and business priorities into integrated consumer experiences and performant advertising campaigns that build the Windows brand, create demand for products, and help customers understand why Windows products matter. Global Advertising leads the development and delivery of consumer paid advertising campaigns.
Microsoft’s mission is to empower every person and every organization on the planet to achieve more, and we’re dedicated to this mission across every aspect of our company. Our culture is centered on embracing a growth mindset and encouraging teams and leaders to bring their highly qualified contributions each day. Join us and help shape the future of the world.
Let’s build the future—together.
Responsibilities
The  Paid Social Advertising Manager i s responsible for the following:
Key Responsibilities :
Lead paid social strategy for Windows campaigns, translating business goals, audience insights, and media plans into platform-specific approaches with clear objectives, KPIs, and success measures.
Serve as the team's paid social subject-matter expert, advising campaign leads, creative teams, and leadership on platform selection, creative formats, and flighting across social and emerging platforms.
Partner with creative and production agencies to brief, develop, and review social-first creative built for each platform's behaviors, including short-form and vertical video, Stories and Reels, carousels, interactive units, and native-feeling executions designed for mobile, sound-off viewing, and the first few seconds.
Lead paid development of creator content, including partnership and whitelisted ads, working with social, creator, and legal partners on talent selection, briefing, creative development, production, finishing, and oversight on integration into a paid campaign.
Partner with media team on partner/channel selection, creative rotation, versioning, QA/QC of assets, and hold agencies accountable for performance, quality, and service-level expectations.
Own in-flight optimization: monitor performance closely, interpret signals, and act quickly on creative rotation, placements, and shifts to improve results against goals.
Build and run a structured creative and audience testing agenda, including A/B tests, multivariate tests, and lift studies, that produces learnings the team can scale across campaigns and markets.
Partner with research, analytics, and measurement teams to define measurement plans covering perception lift, conversion lift, attribution, and incrementality, and connect paid social results to business outcomes such as perception shifts and device sales.
Deliver clear, insight-driven reporting and post-campaign analyses for working teams and senior leaders, turning data into recommendations and practical improvements for future campaigns.
Ensure social assets meet platform specifications, brand standards, accessibility requirements such as captions and alt text, and Microsoft privacy, brand safety, and suitability policies. Partner with CELA to plan and route reviews of claims, disclosures, and offer language.
Partner closely with other Paid Advertising Campaign Managers and cross-functional leads, so social workstreams are integrated into the campaign plan of record, workback schedules, asset delivery, and launch readiness.  Responsible for on-time and budget launches.
Build relationships with platform partners to access beta products, proficient practices, research, and support, and bring forward new opportunities in formats, targeting, and AI-driven tools.
Support global and regional activation by creating paid social playbooks, toolkits, and proficient practices for localizing and scaling campaigns across markets as needed.
Model Microsoft leadership principles by creating clarity, generating energy, and delivering success across teams without relying on direct authority.
Other
Embody our culture and values .
Qualifications
Required Qualifications:
Bachelor's Degree in Business, Advertising, Marketing, Communications, or related field AND 4+ years experience in media, marketing, or advertising on the client or agency side
OR equivalent experience.
5+ years campaign management experience, digital marketing experience, and/or product, project, or site management experience.
Preferred Qualifications:
Master's Degree in Business, Advertising, Marketing, Communications, or related field AND 6+ years experience in media, marketing, social marketing, or advertising on the client or agency side.
8+ years of experience leading paid advertising and paid social campaigns , including campaign strategy, execution, optimization, and performance measurement.
6+ years of experience partnering with and managing external creative, advertising, and media agencies to deliver high-quality campaigns on time and against business objectives.
6+ years of experience working with creators, influencers, and external partners to develop authentic, platform-relevant content and campaigns.
4+ years of experience across major social platforms, including Meta, TikTok, YouTube, Snapchat, Reddit, X, and/or emerging social channels.
Proven ability to develop and deliver strategies across multiple social channels , adapting creative and messaging to maximize engagement and campaign impact.
Ability to use campaign data, audience insights, and performance metrics to optimize paid and organic social strategies and improve results.
Experience developing and optimizing social-first creative, including short-form video, vertical video, Reels, Stories, carousels, and other native social formats.
Experience partnering with creative, advertising, media, and/or production agencies, with the ability to hold external partners accountable for performance, quality, timelines, and deliverables
Experience developing and managing creator/influencer content and partnerships for paid advertising campaigns.
Experience developing or executing A/B testing, audience testing, creative testing, and/or campaign measurement strategies to identify actionable insights.
Demonstrated ability to lead cross-functional work, create clarity from ambiguity, and influence decisions without direct authority.

description:
Overview
Research Internships at Microsoft provide a dynamic environment for research careers with a network of world-class research labs led by globally-recognized scientists and engineers, who pursue innovation in a range of scientific and technical disciplines to help solve complex challenges in diverse fields, including computing, healthcare, economics, and the environment.
The AI & Human Systems  group at Microsoft Research New York City (MSR NYC) and Microsoft Research New England (MSR NE) is seeking multiple Research Interns.
AI & Human Systems brings together researchers and applied scientists who have been part of the Fairness, Accountability, Transparency, and Ethics in AI  (FATE),  Sociotechnical Alignment Center  (STAC),  Economics and Computation , and  Computational Social Science  (CSS) groups. This posting is for candidates interested in working with researchers and applied scientists across any of these areas. Group members collaborate extensively with one another and with other groups across Microsoft.
The group shares a common goal: a world where AI boosts productivity, accelerates innovation, and helps people flourish by focusing their attention, enhancing their capabilities, and safeguarding their agency. Research Interns will contribute to this goal by working with mentors on research that advances it.
Our research draws on diverse disciplinary perspectives to study, measure, and design AI systems and understand their effects on people, teams, organizations, markets, economies, and societies. Topics include, but are not limited to: AI measurement and evaluation; measuring the impacts of AI on individuals, organizations, and society; human–AI interaction and meaningful human engagement with AI; and the design of agentic systems, markets, and institutions that shape how AI participates in the economy and society.
Applicants should demonstrate an interest in studying AI and human systems, a desire to work in a highly interdisciplinary environment, and experience using AI to thoughtfully enhance their own research. title: Senior AI Engineer
description:
Overview
In the 1980s, Microsoft Office transformed knowledge work by moving paper-based documents and ledgers into digital documents, spreadsheets, and presentations. Today, Office and the broader Microsoft ecosystem connect how organizations work - their knowledge, decisions, business processes, and institutional expertise. The next transformation is creating AI-native work experiences across Copilot in Office and the Copilot SuperApp, including Copilot Cowork, where intelligent agents understand domain-specific work, reason across organizational context, and complete complex workflows. As a Senior AI Engineer on the Microsoft Office AI team, you will bring these experiences to hundreds of millions of people.
Achieving this vision starts with understanding the work itself, directly from the people doing it. Every professional domain has its own workflows, terminology, constraints, business rules, and standards for what constitutes a good outcome, much of which remains buried in long-tail domain knowledge. You will work closely with customers, users, and domain experts to discover how work happens in practice, identify high-value opportunities for AI, and rapidly validate ideas against real customer needs. From there, you will translate ambiguous problems into practical product and technical decisions: which domain-specific workflows agents should handle, what knowledge and tools they need, how much autonomy they should have, and where human judgment remains essential. Success requires moving fluidly between customer conversations and hands-on engineering, turning real-world insights into measurable improvements in how people work.
As a Senior AI Engineer , you will turn those insights into systems that work in real customer environments. You will prototype, build, evaluate, deploy, debug, and continuously improve production-grade domain agents across Copilot in Office and Copilot Cowork, working hands-on across grounding, orchestration, tool use, enterprise permissions, reliability, observability, and evaluation. You will collaborate directly with customers to validate solutions against real enterprise data, existing applications, security boundaries, and operational constraints, using production feedback to diagnose failures and iterate quickly.
As common patterns emerge across customers and domain-specific workflows, you will turn repeated solutions into reusable Office AI platform capabilities for agent development, knowledge access, orchestration, evaluation, and debugging. If you share our passion for turning domain expertise into production-grade agents across Copilot, we invite you to join us.

Invent and lead industry-defining domain-specialized agent experiences by working directly with customers and domain experts to understand complex and long-tail workflows, explore new interaction paradigms, and build robust system architectures that enable natural collaboration between humans and AI.

ABOUT THE TEAM

The AI Deployment team enables organizations to turn OpenAI products into real, sustained impact through world-class enablement and training execution.

Our mission is to help customers successfully adopt and operationalize AI across their organizations. We partner with enterprises to translate the potential of OpenAI’s technology into durable capability—through structured training, technical enablement, and scalable deployment programs.

By helping customers move from experimentation to production, the ADM team accelerates time-to-value, deepens product adoption, and helps make OpenAI indispensable to how organizations work.




ABOUT THE ROLE

The AI Deployment Manager is a specialist post-sales enablement role focused on delivering high-impact enablement and adoption services across OpenAI’s product suite. This role is responsible for designing and delivering enablement experiences that support a repeatable adoption framework, driving sustained activation, expanding breadth and depth of usage, and measurable business value across OpenAI’s product suite, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents.

This role blends strong product fluency, instructional design, and customer advisory. You will lead live workshops, deliver services, and design adoption interventions for audiences ranging from everyday business users to technical practitioners and executive leaders, helping customers understand not just what OpenAI’s products can do, but how to apply them effectively in real world workflows.

Success in this role means accelerating customer confidence, increasing product adoption, supporting successful launches of new product capabilities, and helping customers translate product features into tangible outcomes across teams and business functions. You will own outcomes related to activation and sustained usage by shaping how enablement drives measurable customer impact.

This role is based in San Francisco or New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.




IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

 - Own the enablement of OpenAI products, including ChatGPT Enterprise and Agents, helping define effective enablement patterns that support adoption across business and technical teams within enterprise organizations.

 - Serve as a Subject Matter Expert (SME) for designated product areas, building deep expertise, supporting internal enablement, identifying emerging customer use cases for new product surfaces, and aggregating customer feedback to inform product development.

 - Lead customer enablement across the full customer lifecycle, from initial onboarding through expansion, optimization, and long-term adoption.

 - Design and deliver high-impact engagements, including onboarding sessions, advanced capability trainings, executive briefings, hackathons, and hands-on workshops for audiences ranging from senior leaders to working teams.

 - Drive customer activation, sustained usage, and measurable business value through structured enablement programs designed for durable, organization-wide adoption.

 - Partner closely with Sales, Solution Architects, and Delivery Leads to drive adoption across our core product suite.

 - Develop and refine reusable training assets, playbooks, and best practices based on patterns observed across customers and regions.

 - Gather customer feedback from training and enablement engagements, synthesize themes across accounts, and relay insights to internal stakeholders to inform product and program improvements.


YOU MIGHT THRIVE IN THIS ROLE IF YOU:

 - Have 6+ years of experience in customer facing, enablement, or instructional roles, engaging C-level, business, and technical audiences in complex enterprise environments.

 - Possess exceptional presentation and communication skills, particularly when translating AI capabilities into clear, practical value for senior and executive level audiences.

 - Have strong product fluency across ChatGPT, Agents, and the broader OpenAI ecosystem, with a practical understanding of how AI capabilities can be applied to real world workflows and enterprise use cases.

 - Have experience leading workshops and enablement programs, with the ability to design learning journeys, facilitate live sessions, and respond to questions in real time.

 - Can identify patterns across customers and translate them into scalable approaches that improve adoption across the broader customer base.

 - Can connect product capabilities to concrete business outcomes such as productivity gains, operational efficiency, cost reduction, risk mitigation, or revenue impact.

 - Are comfortable thinking on your feet in live customer environments, adapting quickly to new information, shifting priorities, and real time questions while maintaining clarity, ownership, and momentum.

title: BIM Designer & Coordinator: Civil
description:
About the Team

Industrial Compute develops the infrastructure that powers OpenAI’s AI systems. Our Design organization connects engineering, construction, and digital delivery to support complex data center campuses from initial planning through deployment.

Working with internal teams, design consultants, and construction partners, we develop coordinated designs that address site constraints, infrastructure requirements, and future growth. Our BIM team provides the models and workflows needed to deliver consistently across the portfolio.

About the Role

We are seeking a hands-on Civil BIM Designer & Coordinator with a minimum of 8 years of relevant experience to support the planning and design of large-scale, mission-critical data center campuses and associated power generation, energy storage, and utility facilities.

In this role, you will develop, coordinate, and maintain civil models using Civil 3D and AutoCAD. Your scope will include site layouts, grading, drainage, roads, and utilities, coordinating buildings with generating equipment, battery energy storage systems (BESS), water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, substations, and cooling systems.

You will work closely with civil engineers, BIM team, discipline designers, equipment vendors, and delivery partners to turn engineering requirements into clear models and deliverables. Your work will support early design reviews, resolve site coordination challenges, and establish repeatable civil BIM practices across concurrent projects. Detailed engineering requirements and specialist analyses will be provided by the responsible engineers.

We are looking for a hands-on civil specialist who can independently manage modeling assignments, communicate design dependencies, and maintain quality as projects evolve.

Key Responsibilities

 - Advance feasibility, constructability, and phasing: Prepare layout, grading, routing, and earthwork options for early design reviews; incorporate noise, exhaust dispersion, heat-rejection, safety, and environmental constraints. Model heavy-equipment delivery routes, turning movements, crane areas, laydown, maintenance clearances, staged construction, temporary-to-permanent generation transitions, and future expansion.

 - Lead civil site development: Create and maintain surfaces, grading and earthwork models, equipment and building pads, roads, alignments, profiles, and corridors. Incorporate flood protection, stormwater management, and containment or separation process-drainage requirements.

 - Develop and coordinate plant utility systems: Model gravity and pressure networks for gas supply, cooling and process water, fire water, wastewater, electrical duct banks, and communications. Coordinate utility models, routes, corridors, crossings, connections, and clearances with engineers, consultants, utility providers, vendors, and construction partners.

 - Integrate campus and power-generation infrastructure: Coordinate civil models with buildings, power plants, BESS, substations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, cooling systems, and other site utilities. Support simple-cycle and combined-cycle gas turbine, reciprocating engine, and CHP layouts while incorporating equipment separation, service access, and fire access.

 - Coordinate equipment, foundation, and thermal interfaces: Integrate vendor general arrangements, foundation footprints, equipment elevations, trenches, pits, and pipe-support locations with inputs from structural, geotechnical, mechanical, and electrical engineers. Coordinate civil interfaces for heat-recovery steam generators, steam-turbine facilities, heat exchangers, cooling towers, air-cooled condensers, radiator arrays, and thermal-distribution corridors.

 - Govern civil model data and multidisciplinary alignment: Manage Civil 3D data shortcuts, external references, coordinate systems, styles, templates, and parts libraries. Coordinate Civil 3D, Revit, vendor, and combined-discipline models; verify coordinates, origins, elevations, units, orientation, and model alignment in Navisworks.

 - Drive coordination and quality: Lead model reviews, investigate clashes and spatial conflicts, communicate design changes, and track issues through resolution. Review civil models and drawings for completeness, reference integrity, consistency, and compliance with project BIM requirements.

 - Deliver and improve civil BIM: Prepare plans, profiles, sections, model exports, review packages, and model-based quantities appropriate to each project phase. Maintain reusable content, document workflows, and improve delivery across data center, power-generation, energy-storage, and utility projects.

Qualifications

 - Minimum 8 years of civil design, BIM modeling, or civil infrastructure drafting experience, plus a relevant degree/diploma or equivalent practical experience.

 - Experience supporting mission-critical facilities or complex industrial infrastructure across multiple disciplines.

 - Advanced Civil 3D and AutoCAD proficiency, including grading, corridors, utility networks, sheet production, data shortcuts, references, coordinate systems, and model dependencies.

 - Experience with site-survey data, GIS, point clouds, NavVis or similar laser-scanning/reality-capture workflows.

 - Experience with Navisworks, Revizto, and Autodesk Forma for model coordination, issue tracking, and markups.

 - Ability to independently deliver civil packages, interpret engineering and vendor information, identify missing inputs, and escalate engineering decisions appropriately.

 - Strong communication and organizational skills across changing priorities and concurrent projects.

Preferred Skills

 - Direct experience with hyperscale, colocation, or other mission-critical data center campuses, from conceptual site planning through detailed design and construction coordination.

 - Experience supporting civil design and model coordination for one or more of the following: gas turbine or reciprocating engine power plants, combined-cycle or CHP facilities, BESS installations, water treatment plants, gas metering and conditioning facilities, or comparable industrial infrastructure.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Controls Engineer to design, program, integrate and commission on-site power generation and microgrid control systems serving large AI data center campuses. You will own control architecture and functional requirements across generation packages, balance-of-plant systems, electrical protection, microgrid controls, and data center monitoring. You will work from concept through factory testing, site commissioning, performance validation, and operational improvement.

This role requires hands-on experience with industrial control systems, including PLC and DCS programming, plant-level control sequences, equipment integration, simulation, testing and commissioning. The engineers will work with equipment vendors, system integrators and the broader data center team to make sure the complete power system operates safely and reliably across normal and failure conditions.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Power Generation and Microgrid Controls
   
   - Design, program and commission plant power controllers (PPCs) and microgrid control systems for gas turbine and reciprocating engine power plants.
   
   - Develop control sequences for grid-connected, islanded and transition modes, including startup, shutdown, synchronization, load sharing, import/export control, load shedding, black start, restoration and resynchronization.
   
   - Coordinate active power, reactive power, voltage and frequency controls across generators, energy storage, MV UPS and other distributed energy resources.
   
   - Define how the plant responds to generator trips, loss of utility power, large load changes, equipment failures and loss of communication.
   
   - Work with OEMs to define the boundaries between turbine or engine controls, generator controls, the PPC, protection systems and data center controls.

 - Electrical systems and utility interconnection
   
   - Review utility and transmission-provider interconnection requirements and translate them into plant control, protection, metering, communications and testing requirements.
   
   - Work with utility and equipment vendors to define controls and interfaces at the point of interconnection, including power limits, voltage and frequency response, reactive, power factor, telemetry and dispatch.
   
   - Review interconnection studies, operating procedures and test requirements, and track the actions needed to demonstrate compliance.
   
   - Work with Engineer-Of-Record (EOR) to review load-flow, short-circuit, stability, step-load and electromagnetic transient (EMT) studies. Use the results to develop control settings, sequences and test cases.

 - Control Architecture:
   
   - Develop and review functional design specifications (FDS), sequences of operation, network architecture diagrams, I/O lists and alarm philosophies.
   
   - Review P&IDs and instrumentation for generation-plant systems, including fuel gas, cooling, lubrication and other balance-of-plant equipment.
   
   - Define equipment interfaces, control modes, permissives, interlocks and failure responses between OEM packages and the plant control system.

 - Real-Time Simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) testing:
   
   - Develop and execute real-time simulation and hardware-in-the-loop (HIL) tests for generation and microgrid control systems using RTDS and RSCAD.
   
   - Work with internal engineering teams and equipment vendors to build and validate representative models of the electrical system, from the generation plant and utility interconnection through the data center distribution system to representative GPU rack loads.
   
   - Develop and execute test cases for normal operation, mode changes, load steps, trips, faults, and system failures.
   
   - Compare simulation and HIL results with equipment data, factory test results and field performance. Document model assumptions and limitations.

 - Testing, commissioning and delivery
   
   - Develop and review FAT, SAT and integrated systems test plans for plant and microgrid controls.
   
   - Participate in factory testing, site testing, energization support, tuning and commissioning of generation and data center power systems.
   
   - Troubleshoot controls and system-integration issues using controller data, alarms, event records, trends and test results.
   
   - Work with OEMs, EPCs, utilities and system integrators to resolve interface gaps and track issues through closure.
   
   - Coordinate the handover of final project deliverables, including software, configurations, backups, test records, operating instructions and training, to the data center operations team.

Qualifications

 - 8+ years of hands-on experience designing, programming, integrating and commissioning industrial controls for power generation, industrial plants, utilities, or mission-critical infrastructure.

 - Strong hands-on experience with PLC, DCS, SCADA, historian, industrial-networking, and control-system integration.

 - Experience with plant power control, generator controls, synchronization, load sharing, islanding and load-shedding schemes.

 - Experience integrating controls with power generation equipment, protective relays, SCADA/EPMS and other plant systems.

 - Experience developing functional specifications, sequences, I/O, alarms, graphics, and factory or site test procedures.

 - Ability to troubleshoot across software, instrumentation, electrical, mechanical, communications, and operating-process boundaries.

 - Understanding of industrial cybersecurity, redundancy, failover, and change-control practices.

 - Bachelor's degree in controls, electrical, mechanical, chemical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.

Preferred Skills

 - Experience with major turbine or reciprocating-engine control platforms and microgrid controllers.

 - Experience with data center power systems and rapidly changing AI or GPU loads.

 - Experience integrating gas generation with BESS, MV UPS and grid-forming or grid-following inverters.

 - Experience with EMT studies and model validation for weak-grid or islanded power systems.

 - Experience developing automated simulation tests and regression test libraries.

 - Experience with network redundancy, industrial protocols, OT cybersecurity and remote support for critical facilities.

 - Experience transitioning from temporary generation to permanent power systems.

 - Experience with IEC 61850 (MMS, GOOSE, SV), Modbus, OPC UA, DNP3, EtherNet/IP, or comparable industrial protocols.

Frontier AI models have the potential to benefit all of humanity, but also pose increasingly severe risks. This team is tasked with identifying, tracking, and preparing for catastrophic risks related to frontier AI models.

The mission of the Preparedness team is to:

 1. Closely monitor and predict the evolving capabilities of frontier AI systems, with an eye towards misuse risks whose impact could be catastrophic to our society

 2. Ensure we have concrete procedures, infrastructure and partnerships to mitigate these risks and to safely handle the development of powerful AI systems

Preparedness tightly connects capability assessment, evaluations, and internal red teaming, and mitigations for frontier models, as well as overall coordination on AGI preparedness. This is fast paced, exciting work that has far reaching importance for the company and for society.

 

About the Role

We’re hiring a Data Scientist to help build, evaluate, and continuously improve mitigations that prevent extreme harms from AI systems. This role is for an experienced, highly autonomous individual contributor who can take ambiguous problem statements, structure rigorous analyses, and translate findings into actionable product and policy changes.

This position goes beyond “running evals.” You’ll help create mitigation intelligence and monitoring systems that enable OpenAI to detect issues early, measure effectiveness over time, and reduce both over-blocking (unnecessary friction) and under-blocking (missed harm).





WHAT YOU’LL DO

 - Evaluate and improve mitigation systems, including classifiers and detection pipelines across domains (e.g., biosecurity, cybersecurity, and emerging risk areas).

 - Diagnose false positives and false negatives with deep error analysis, root cause investigation, and clear recommendations for mitigation adjustments.

 - Build monitoring and measurement frameworks to track mitigation effectiveness over time and across user segments and use cases.

 - Identify trends in over-blocking vs. under-blocking, quantify customer impact, and propose prioritized interventions.

 - Develop insights from customer feedback, complaints, and usage patterns to detect shifts in adversarial behavior and system failure modes.

 - Expand risk monitoring into new areas, including cybersecurity threats and model loss-of-control or sabotage scenarios, in partnership with domain experts.

 - Communicate results to technical and executive stakeholders with crisp narratives, decision-ready metrics, and clear tradeoffs.

You might thrive in this role if you are:

 - An autonomous operator: you can take a problem statement and independently structure the analysis end-to-end.

 - Strong at executive-ready communication: concise, clear, and outcome-oriented.

 - Skilled in turning analysis into productable changes: you’re comfortable influencing across functions to drive mitigation improvements.


QUALIFICATIONS

 - Significant experience in data science or applied analytics in high-stakes domains (e.g., security, trust & safety, abuse prevention, fraud, platform integrity, or reliability).

 - Strong foundations in experimentation, causal thinking, and/or observational inference; ability to design robust measurement under imperfect data.

 - Fluency in SQL and Python (or equivalent) for analysis, modeling, and building monitoring workflows.

 - Experience building metrics, dashboards, and operational monitoring that meaningfully changes outcomes (not just reporting).

 - Track record of driving cross-functional impact with engineering, product, and research partners.
