A fundamental part of the role is understanding OpenAI's group structure, partnering closely with Tax on complex transactions, and providing guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows.

You will own work from source data through close, resolve routine issues independently, and improve processes within established policies and approval controls. You will identify matters requiring technical assessment early and bring clear analysis and supporting facts for review. You will be a pivotal interface between global finance teams, treasury, tax, and systems to support our mission-critical financial close and reporting processes.

 


WHAT YOU WILL DO

 - Develop and maintain an understanding of OpenAI's group structure, ownership relationships and intercompany arrangements and flows.

 - Partner with Tax, Technical Accounting and your manager to assess complex intercompany transactions and coordinate implementation of agreed accounting treatments.

 - Provide guidance to the wider accounting group on intercompany flows, accounting treatments and cross-entity accounting questions.

 - Own monthly and quarterly close activities for assigned accounts, including reconciliations and resolution of reconciling items.

 - Coordinate accounting for intercompany funding and settlements with Treasury and Tax, within established approval and execution controls.

 - Review transfer pricing calculations prepared by the TP team for intercompany accounting accuracy, including entity, account, currency and FX rate treatment.

 - Familiarity with intercompany transactions, settlements, and foreign currency accounting. Experience with transfer pricing calculations or investment accounting is relevant to this role.

 - Careful review habits and the ability to trace a calculation or journal entry to its source, explain discrepancies, and document how they were resolved.

 - The ability to organize a close calendar, manage dependencies, and communicate clearly with Accounting, Treasury, Tax, and Technical Accounting. You follow through independently and raise issues with enough context for others to act.

description:
About the Team

OpenAI, in close collaboration with our capital and delivery partners, is building the infrastructure required to support frontier AI systems. The Data Center Engineering team defines repeatable technical standards and carries them through design, construction, commissioning, and operational readiness. The team works across data center facilities, power generation, compute infrastructure, construction, procurement, and operations to deliver reliable capacity at unprecedented scale and speed.

About the Role

We are seeking a Mechanical Engineer to design and integrate power-generation and balance-of-plant systems for large AI data center campuses. You will work across prime movers, fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, water treatment, heat recovery, acoustics, fire interfaces, and plant auxiliaries. The role combines first-principles engineering with practical vendor and field execution to deliver systems that are safe, efficient, maintainable, and ready for demanding operating profiles.

Travel: 50%

Key Responsibilities

 - Develop mechanical basis-of-design documents, process flow diagrams, P&IDs, specifications, calculations, and equipment requirements for power generation facilities.

 - Design and review prime-mover auxiliaries, fuel gas or liquid fuel systems, exhaust, ventilation, cooling, lubrication, compressed air, water treatment, and heat-recovery systems.

 - Evaluate thermal performance, hydraulic behavior, pressure drop, vibration, acoustics, emissions interfaces, redundancy, and maintenance requirements.

 - Review OEM and EPC proposals, equipment selections, test plans, failure modes, service strategies, and lifecycle tradeoffs.

 - Support procurement, factory acceptance testing, construction, startup, commissioning, performance testing, and root-cause investigations.

 - 8+ years of mechanical engineering experience on power generation, oil and gas, industrial utilities, central plants, or mission-critical projects.

 - Strong knowledge of rotating equipment, piping, heat transfer, fluid systems, thermal performance, ventilation, and mechanical auxiliaries.

 - Experience with combined heat and power, heat recovery, modular generation, or microgrids.

 - Experience with gas turbines, reciprocating engines, generators, or comparable large industrial equipment.

 - Ability to evaluate vendor data, equipment curves, operating scenarios, failure modes, and maintenance constraints.

 - Experience carrying designs through construction, startup, commissioning, and performance validation.

OpenAI’s Hardware organization develops AI-native silicon and system-level solutions for the unique demands of advanced AI workloads. Building on efforts like Jalapeño, the team is developing future generations of AI-native silicon and tightly integrated systems to power the next generation of frontier models. By co-designing chips, systems, tools, and methodologies, the team helps deliver faster, more efficient, and production-ready hardware for OpenAI’s supercomputing platform.

About the Role

We’re looking for a Silicon Design Lead to drive architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of key IP and subsystems for our AI hardware platforms. You will translate functional, performance, and security requirements into efficient silicon designs, owning technical decisions from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

Part of this role will focus on hardware security implementation in close partnership with OpenAI’s Security team. While the Security team owns the overarching security architecture and requirements, you will translate those requirements into silicon microarchitecture and implementation, balancing security capabilities with performance, power, area, and design complexity. The other part of this role will focus on driving general silicon architecture/microarchitecture. 

In this role, you will:

 - Own architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation of silicon IP and subsystems, from requirements and design specifications through integration and validation.

 - Define hardware interfaces, data flows, and microarchitectural tradeoffs to meet functional, performance, power, and area requirements.

 - Partner closely with OpenAI’s Security team to translate security architecture, requirements, and threat models into implementable hardware capabilities.

 - Design and integrate hardware security mechanisms, including encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, and data protection across silicon subsystems.

 - Evaluate architectural and implementation tradeoffs to ensure security capabilities meet functional and performance requirements.

 - Collaborate with silicon architects, RTL, verification, firmware, and software teams to drive subsystem design, integration, and validation.

 - Review and contribute to RTL implementations, ensuring designs align with architectural intent and system requirements.

 - Evaluate existing and third-party IP, identify architectural or implementation gaps, and drive solutions across subsystem boundaries.

 - Have strong experience in silicon IP or subsystem-level architecture, microarchitecture, and implementation.

 - Have owned hardware IP or subsystem designs from architectural definition through implementation and integration.

 - Have experience implementing hardware security features such as memory encryption, key management, access controls, isolation, or secure boot.

 - Understand how to translate functional and security requirements into hardware architectures, interfaces, and microarchitectural specifications.

 - Have working knowledge of RTL design and coding proficiency in Verilog or SystemVerilog, with the ability to read, review, and contribute to RTL.

 - Can evaluate performance, power, area, and complexity tradeoffs across silicon designs.

Our work connects changing research needs with capacity planning, allocation, and scheduling. We build tools and services that help researchers express their compute needs, access the right resources, and run their workloads effectively. As the fleet and our research ambitions grow, we continually improve how compute is planned, allocated, and used.

You will be part of an engineer-first TPM team, partnering closely with the Research Compute Services team. Your primary responsibility will be to build and own the tools, data, and platform that turn Research plans and workload signals into concrete compute demand and manage allocations across the fleet.

This is a hands-on technical role. You will build alongside researchers and engineers, working directly with code and data to prototype solutions, automate workflows, and deliver tools that teams use every day. You will combine technical judgment and program leadership to connect capacity planning with the deployment, scheduling, and optimization systems that make allocated compute usable.

Customer Education helps people and organizations build the skills and confidence to use AI effectively. We create courses, live learning, community programs and product education that help people apply OpenAI’s products to their work.

location: United States - Santa Fe Springs, CA
description:

THE ROLE
Apparel Production Associate
Quince is hiring a Apparel Production Associate t o be a critical utility player across our entire production operation. You'll work across pre-production order staging, machine support, post-decoration finishing, and quality control — adapting daily to where the floor needs you most. On a high-volume floor, you'll stage orders for machine operators one hour, trim and inspect finished goods the next, and support operators with setup and supplies the next. You'll report to the Production Lead and partner closely with the Warehouse + Receiving Lead, machine operators, and the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator to keep production moving seamlessly.
Your success means faster order turnaround, zero quality gaps, operators who never stop working because they have what they need, and a clean, organized production floor. You're the backbone of production efficiency.
This is a fully on-site role, Monday through Friday during regular business hours at our facility in Santa Fe Springs, CA.
Responsibilities
Stage and validate orders for production — confirm all inventory and materials were received, verify work instructions and machine locations are clear, check that threads and supplies are in stock, and ensure the order is ready for operators to pull and produce.
Trim threads, backing, and excess materials from embroidered and decorated goods immediately after decoration — keeping pace with machine output so finished goods do not back up.
Inspect every decorated piece against the job ticket: placement, adhesion, color accuracy, and overall appearance.
Pull and set aside any defective or non-conforming pieces; log defect type, quantity, and job number and hand off to the Production Lead for disposition.
Fold, bag, tag, or poly-bag finished pieces per job ticket and customer specifications (pending packing team rollout); ensure all finished goods are presentation-ready before moving to the handoff area for Shipping.
Assist machine operators — embroidery, heat transfer, DTG, and screen print — with loading, unloading, setup, and in-process support as needed throughout the shift.
Restock machine supplies (thread, backing, transfer paper, tape, polybags, etc.) proactively so operators stay running without interruption.
Support the Warehouse + Receiving Lead with job staging, material pulls, and receiving tasks during high-volume periods.
Assist the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator with packing and order handoffs when finishing volume allows.
Adapt quickly to shifting priorities — the Production Lead will direct where support is most needed at any given time.
Maintain a clean, organized, and safe production floor throughout the shift.
Qualifications
Required:
1+ year of experience in a production, manufacturing, warehouse or similar environment.
Ability to stand, move, and work on your feet for a full shift (8+ hours).
Strong attention to detail — you catch what's off and you don't let it slide.
Ability to maintain accuracy and quality at a consistent production pace.
Adaptable and self-directed — comfortable shifting between tasks as the floor demands.
Reliable and punctual; production schedules depend on everyone showing up and staying focused.
Preferred:
Experience in a production, apparel, manufacturing, or warehouse environment.
Familiarity with embroidery, screen printing, heat transfer, or decorated apparel finishing.
Experience with quality inspection or production order workflows.
Bilingual (English/Spanish) a plus.
PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS:
Fully on-site production floor role.
Must be able to stand and move throughout the full shift.
Ability to lift and carry up to 30 lbs. regularly.
Manual dexterity required for trimming and finishing tasks.
Comfortable working in a production environment with machinery noise, heat press equipment, and production materials.

You'll work across pre-production order staging, machine support, post-decoration finishing, and quality control — adapting daily to where the floor needs you most. On a high-volume floor, you'll stage orders for machine operators one hour, trim and inspect finished goods the next, and support operators with setup and supplies the next. You'll report to the Production Lead and partner closely with the Warehouse + Receiving Lead, machine operators, and the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator to keep production moving seamlessly.
Your success means faster order turnaround, zero quality gaps, operators who never stop working because they have what they need, and a clean, organized production floor. You're the backbone of production efficiency.
This is a fully on-site role, Monday through Friday during regular business hours at our facility in Santa Fe Springs, CA.

Stage and validate orders for production — confirm all inventory and materials were received, verify work instructions and machine locations are clear, check that threads and supplies are in stock, and ensure the order is ready for operators to pull and produce.
Trim threads, backing, and excess materials from embroidered and decorated goods immediately after decoration — keeping pace with machine output so finished goods do not back up.
Inspect every decorated piece against the job ticket: placement, adhesion, color accuracy, and overall appearance.
Pull and set aside any defective or non-conforming pieces; log defect type, quantity, and job number and hand off to the Production Lead for disposition.
Fold, bag, tag, or poly-bag finished pieces per job ticket and customer specifications (pending packing team rollout); ensure all finished goods are presentation-ready before moving to the handoff area for Shipping.

Support the Warehouse + Receiving Lead with job staging, material pulls, and receiving tasks during high-volume periods.
Assist the Shipping + Fulfillment Coordinator with packing and order handoffs when finishing volume allows.

description: About Rivian Rivian is on a mission to keep the world adventurous forever. This goes for the emissions-free Electric Adventure Vehicles we build, and the curious, courageous souls we seek to attract. As a company, we constantly challenge what’s possible, never simply accepting what has always been done. We reframe old problems, seek new solutions and operate comfortably in areas that are unknown. Our backgrounds are diverse, but our team shares a love of the outdoors and a desire to protect it for future generations. Role Summary We are seeking an RTL Design Engineer to join the Neural Network Engine (NNE) design team in Palo Alto. In this hands-on role, you will define the microarchitecture and deliver production-quality RTL for compute, memory, datapath, and control blocks in an advanced SoC environment. You will work from architectural and physical design requirements, develop them into a microarchitecture specification. You partner closely with design verification, physical design, firmware, compiler, and silicon-validation engineers. The ideal candidate is comfortable owning a block from definition through implementation, debug, quality checks, and integration. Responsibilities Translate architectural requirements into clear microarchitectural specifications and design documentation. Analyze performance and power characteristics of existing hardware and software to identify areas for improvement. Develop and utilize AI agents to streamline RTL development tasks Define and review block-level interfaces, including data movement, handshakes, clocking, reset behavior, and error handling. Design, implement, integrate, and debug synthesizable RTL for NNE blocks and interfaces. Design with performance, power, area, functional safety, and physical implementation constraints in mind. Collaborate with design verification engineers to create test plans, assertions, coverage goals, and debug strategies. Use simulation, lint, CDC/RDC, formal or equivalence checking, synthesis, and timing analysis to evaluate and improve RTL quality. Investigate functional, performance, timing, and power issues across RTL, verification, and implementation flows. Participate in design reviews and contribute to coding standards, reusable RTL patterns, and development methodology improvements. Support block integration, regression closure, RTL handoff, and pre-silicon validation. Communicate design decisions, assumptions, risks, and trade-offs clearly across partner teams. What you will bring A disciplined approach to writing simple, readable specifications that enable development of clean, reusable, and verifiable RTL. Join Our Team as a Component Quality Technologist!
The Component Quality Technologist is responsible for the inspection of individual components, both internally manufactured and externally sourced, to ensure they meet required quality standards. The role requires knowledge of geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T), the ability to read technical drawings, and the use of measuring equipment to confirm product conformity. The Technologist ensures that component defects are identified, documented, and resolved before components proceed further in the production process.
In this job you will be responsible for inspecting fabricated parts, sub-assemblies and final assemblies, including painted components, made from various machines such as shears, punch presses, and welding work centers. You will be required to work with assembly and detailed prints, industry standards, routings, BOMs, specifications, instruction bulletins, and customer notes. Inspecting the products will require you to use various pieces of inspection equipment and the ability to select the appropriate measuring equipment such as tape measures, go/no go gages, special gages, torque wrenches, thread plug gages, fluke meters, and fuses holder standards. The job will require you to clearly communicate verbally and in written format. Abnormal conditions, must be clearly recorded on the Checklist, DPU report, and/or on a NMR. All defects will be recorded and clearly explained to assembly team members and shop floor leadership. There will be times when product will be placed on hold until you clearly explain the abnormal conditions to engineers so they can determine if the product could be sent to the customer or needs to be reworked.

Perform detailed inspections of components to ensure they meet dimensional and material specifications.
Interpret technical drawings, BOMs, and GD&T to assess compliance with design requirements.
Record and document inspection results, including the identification of non-conforming materials.
Utilize, maintain, and calibrate precision measuring equipment, such as micrometers and calipers, to verify component dimensions.

location: Remote - Austin; Remote - Seattle; San Francisco, CA, United States
description:

As part of a recently public company, you’ll have the autonomy and support to make an impact as we build for the long term.
About this role:
Samsara’s cloud-connected sensor platform collects observations about the world in near real-time. Samsara builds an extensive set of products, including battery-powered, wireless sensors, Linux-based IoT gateways, and Internet-connected dashcams. These devices are the building blocks Samsara uses to construct enterprise solutions for a wide range of verticals, including commercial fleet management and industrial monitoring. Through a unique integration of sensor data such as GPS, acceleration, temperature, video, and more, we enable our customers to gain greater insights into operations, identify and eliminate inefficiencies, and react to alerts all in near real-time.
As a Firmware Engineer at Samsara, you will develop software that runs on millions of devices, deployed by our industrial and enterprise customers. You’ll tackle challenges including evaluating and selecting hardware components, bringing up new hardware platforms and sensors, building systems to gather data and detect meaningful events, and structuring recorded data to allow efficient analysis across thousands of devices while providing deep insights into individual events.
We use C for our MCU-based platforms, Golang for embedded applications on Linux-based gateways and backend services, Google protocol buffers to structure data, and various AWS technologies to process and store data. Experience with these exact technologies is not required.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Your efforts will result in real-world impact—helping to keep the lights on, get food into grocery stores, reduce emissions, and most importantly, ensure workers return home safely.
You are the architect of your own career: If you put in the work, this role won’t be your last at Samsara. We set up our employees for success and have built a culture that encourages rapid career development, countless opportunities to experiment and master your craft in a hyper growth environment.
You’re energized by our opportunity: The vision we have to digitize large sectors of the global economy requires your full focus and best efforts to bring forth creative, ambitious ideas for our customers.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together and support each other. You will be surrounded by a high-caliber team that will encourage you to do your best.
Click here to learn more about Samsara's cultural philosophy.
In this role, you will:
Shape the hardware, not just the code that runs on it. Sit in reviews with our electrical engineers and help choose the right SoC, amount of flash/RAM, and combination of sensors, then prove those choices out on prototypes that reach real customers in months, not years.
Be the first person to make a new board do anything at all. Bring up new platforms and prototypes from virgin silicon: configure I/O, get SPI, I2C, UART, BLE talking, debug system init, validate the design, and turn unproven hardware into a product.
Build the layers everything else depends on. Peripheral drivers, secure bootloaders, device firmware updates, as well as the core management layers like power and connectivity, that determine whether a device in the field quietly recovers on its own or becomes an RMA.
Chase every microamp. Design protocols and hardware management for battery-powered sensors and gateways where the gap between good firmware and great firmware is measured in years of device life.
Work with the people who ship the whole product. Partner with product, full-stack, mobile and quality engineers so the data your firmware produces arrives intact and useful as it lands in the hands of dispatchers, fleet managers, and technicians who depend on it every shift.
Raise the bar for the engineers around you. Your designs, reviews, and instincts help raise the ceiling for the whole team. You will help shape how Samsara works, keep a high bar, be intellectually honest, work with urgency and deliver iteratively, as we scale globally and across new offices.
What you bring
2+ years building firmware for resource-constrained systems , on products that shipped to real customers and then had to survive in the field.
Fluency in C. You know what the compiler is doing, and you can read a linker map, a stack trace, or a corrupted heap without guessing.
Solid bare-metal and RTOS experience - Zephyr, FreeRTOS, or equivalent. You have made scheduling, memory and timing decisions. Mutexes and semaphores are everyday tools for you.
You have helped bring up new boards. First power-on of unproven hardware, at the bench with the electrical engineer who drew it up, working out whether the bug is in your code, a library, the schematic, or the part itself.
Fluency in the low-level interfaces - SPI, I2C, UART, CAN, ADC and the ability to debug the seam between hardware and software.
Real bench instincts. The usage of an oscilloscope, network analyzer, or RF spectrum analyzer, is how you form a hypothesis, not what you reach for after the print statements run out.
Cross-team scope. You have contributed to work spanning hardware, firmware, cloud and quality from concept to shipped product. You have worked effectively across teams to build consensus.
Cross-layer judgment. You can trace how a decision at the driver level surfaces in a customer's experience three layers up, and you factor that into your design decisions.
You write things down. Design docs, review comments and post-mortems that other engineers can actually act on.
You ship fast without shipping poorly. Comfortable iterating on customer feedback at speed, backed by automated testing and code you would be content to inherit.
You use AI smartly. It’s part of your every day work flow and multiplies your output without watering things down.
What will set you apart
BLE at depth - You understand what’s going on down the PHY and can build orchestration for the system to use in a performant and power efficient way.
Cellular IoT - LTE-M or NB-IoT modem integration, power state management, and the certification gauntlet (FCC, PTCRB, carrier approval).
Securing embedded systems end to end - secure boot, firmware signing, cryptography, and key management that survives contact with manufacturing.
OTA and device firmware update at fleet scale - A/B partitions, rollback, and the discipline of never bricking a device you cannot physically reach.
Embedded Linux on the gateway side - Yocto or Buildroot, kernel drivers, device trees.
CAN and J1939 work on commercial vehicles , including reverse-engineering data bus parameters across makes and models.
Python and Bash for tooling , and hardware-in-the-loop test automation.
You’ve been on the factory floor - You have an understanding of the processes behind the mass production and quality assurance of electronics. You have a track record of fixing production show stoppers.

Optimize inventory for hardware deployed across 98% of US roads and 70+ billion miles driven annually.
Drive sustainability initiatives by reducing waste and improving supply chain efficiency across global operations.

Build demand, inventory and cost forecasting systems for highly variable, seasonal SKUs with intermittent patterns and long lead times.
Model supplier risk using real-time IoT telemetry, geopolitical signals, and market data —not just historical sales.
Design cost optimization algorithms balancing inventory carrying costs, expedite fees, and revenue risk across multiple regions.
Create anomaly detection systems for cellular connectivity spend and supply chain disruptions using multimodal data.

Access to 10+ trillion data points annually from connected operations.
Work with ERP data, IoT sensor streams, third-party market intelligence, and operational metrics.
Build features from unique real-world signals —vehicle diagnostics, utilization patterns, failure modes.

Establish governance frameworks , documentation standards, and quality controls for model development, validation, and lifecycle management
Partner with Ops management to drive adoption of AI tools, define new processes, and train supply chain teams on insights-driven workflows

8+ years in applied data science or ML, ideally in supply chain, operations research, logistics, or manufacturing
Master's or PhD in Computer Science, Statistics, Data Science, EE, OR, or related technical field

Expert in statistical modeling and ML : time series forecasting, optimization, anomaly detection, causal inference
Strong Python coding skills and fluency in SQL ; proven experience developing and deploying production ML systems
Proficiency in MLOps practices : automated testing, CI/CD, model versioning, monitoring, performance tracking
Experience building real-time inference pipelines and managing GPU/TPU resources for training at scale
Familiar with data visualization tools (Tableau, Power BI) and cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, Azure)
Mindset & Collaboration:
Passion for operational excellence, cost efficiency, and scalable solutions
Builder mindset, with a track record of taking products or systems from 0 to 1.
Exceptional  problem-solving, critical thinking, and communication skills—able to explain complex technical concepts to non-technical stakeholders
Track record of  collaborating cross-functionally and driving adoption of data-driven solutions

Time-Series Mastery: Proven track record building advanced forecasting models (e.g., Prophet, LSTMs, Transformer-based) for intermittent demand and seasonal patterns.

Domain Expertise: Deep understanding of supply chain concepts (S&OP, IBP, safety stock, EOQ), ERP systems (SAP, NetSuite, E2DP, Propel), and inventory optimization theory. Ideal background in consumer electronics or B2B hardware manufacturing.

location: Remote - CA; Remote - Chicago; Remote - Seattle; Remote - TX

Samsara's Customer Success team is on the front lines of business value delivery by helping customers adopt our platform, realize measurable business value, and renew and expand with confidence. Today, billing errors, concession requests, and cancellation or return exceptions land with CSMs, CS managers, and several partner teams, each holding part of the picture. No one owns the whole timeline. We are creating a dedicated Contract and Billing Resolution team to close that gap for Mid-Market and Commercial accounts.
As the Manager, Contract and Billing, you will lead this new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists. You will inherit work that CSMs and their managers have handled as best they can, and turn it into a function that is repeatable, measurable, and scalable: the playbook, the intake and routing, the system of record, the root-cause reporting, and the hiring and coaching of the people who do the work.
This role sits between the sales process and the finance process. A bill can look wrong because of something that happened upstream in a quote, an order form, a contract, or a segment change in Salesforce, or downstream in billing and invoicing. You and your team will figure out where it broke, regardless of which team caused it, and work across both sides to fix it. You will partner closely with Customer Success Managers, Sales, Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal, and report the repeat failures to the teams that own the underlying systems and processes.
This is a remote position open to candidates residing in the US except the San Francisco Bay Metro Area, NYC Metro Area, and Washington, D.C. Metro Area.
You should apply if:
You want to impact the industries that run our world: Every billing case your team resolves keeps the organizations that move goods, transport students, and restore power focused on their operations rather than on a billing dispute.
You want to build something from the ground up: This team and function are new. You will hire the team, write the playbook, and set up the systems and metrics that define how Samsara resolves billing and contract cases.
You thrive when solving problems: You figure things out, even without a clean playbook or precedent. With a growth mindset and a desire to learn, you find the fix that works for the customer and for Samsara, and you teach your team to do the same.
You are an investigator: You enjoy rebuilding a timeline from incomplete or conflicting records across sales and finance systems, and you stay curious until the numbers tie out.
You are a people leader: You enjoy hiring, coaching, and developing a team, and you set a high bar for quality, ownership, and follow-through.
You are a natural relationship builder: Whether with our customers or cross-functional teams at Samsara, you are in constant communication and collaboration with key stakeholders to win as a team, and you can maintain clear boundaries while staying warm.
You want to be with the best: At Samsara, we win together, celebrate together, and support each other. You will be surrounded by the best and brightest professionals.
In this role, you will:
Build and lead a new team of 3 to 4 Contract and Billing Resolution Specialists: hire, onboard, coach, and develop them, and set clear expectations for case quality, ownership, and customer communication.
Stand up the function from scratch: take the billing, concession, and cancellation work that CSMs handle today, define what the team owns and what it does not, and turn it into a documented playbook that is repeatable and scalable.
Design and launch the system of record for billing and contract cases, working with CS Ops and Systems partners to set up intake, routing, case tracking, and customer communication in tools such as Zendesk, Salesforce, or Jira.
Own the front door: make sure every billing, concession, and cancellation request is logged in one place, including those that arrive through Slack, email, or Gainsight, and coach CSMs and AEs on what a complete request looks like.
Act as the escalation point for the most complex, sensitive, or high-dollar cases, including accounts that are delinquent or facing suspension, and step in directly with customers and internal leaders when needed.
Define the handoffs, ownership, and service levels with Billing Support, Order-to-Cash, Sales Ops, Deal Desk, Finance, and Legal so cases stop bouncing between teams.
Set the standards for how the team separates a correction of a Samsara error from a concession, a return, a reprocess, and a contract amendment, and how concession and cancellation exceptions are sized, documented, and routed through the approval matrix.
Build the metrics and reporting for the function, including volume, days to resolution, repeat errors, concession dollars, and renewal risk tied to billing issues, and use them to manage the team and show impact.
Fix repeat causes: own the root-cause tagging on every case, separate one-offs from systemic failures, and deliver a monthly read-out to the teams that own the systems and processes involved, such as segment-move bugs, term rounding, and AE handoff gaps.
Partner with Support, Finance, Sales Ops, and Product on billing improvement work, including earlier detection of billing problems that threaten renewals.
Use AI to improve how the team works, from structuring case timelines to drafting summaries, while keeping approvals, amounts, and root-cause conclusions with people.
Champion, role model, and embed Samsara's operating principles, including Keep a High Bar, Be Intellectually Honest, and Solve Problems Together, as we scale.
Minimum requirements for the role:
7+ years of experience in sales operations, deal desk, contracts, billing operations, order to cash, revenue operations, or a similar finance and operations role.
2+ years of experience managing people, ideally in a sales operations or finance capacity.
Experience building a team or function from scratch, or leading a major reorganization of an existing team, including writing the playbook and processes that made the work repeatable.
Deep working knowledge of either the quote-to-contract side (quotes, order forms, amendments, terms, and the sales systems that pass contract data downstream) or the billing side (invoicing, credits, rebills, and collections), and the curiosity to learn the other.
Experience setting up or significantly improving a case management, ticketing, or request-routing system, such as Zendesk, Jira, or Salesforce cases, that worked for both customers and internal teams.
Strong investigative skills: you can rebuild a timeline from incomplete or conflicting information across CRM, billing, and contract systems, and teach others to do the same.
Sound financial judgment about credits, concessions, reprocessing, and refunds, and a clear way of explaining your recommendation.
A record of driving results across teams without authority over them, including Sales, Finance, and Operations partners with competing priorities.
Customer-facing communication that stays honest and composed in hard conversations, and written summaries a leader can read once and decide on.
This is a demanding position with high internal visibility that requires strong priority management, high emotional intelligence, and comfort with ambiguity and incomplete precedent.
An ideal candidate also has:
Has worked on both sides: the sales process and contracting, and the finance and billing process.
Has managed a team that handled escalated or high-dollar billing or contract disputes.
Has experience with Salesforce, NetSuite, and CPQ tools. Familiarity with Zendesk, Gainsight, and Sweethawk.
Has a Customer Success, Support, or account management background with customer-facing financial or contract work.
Has built dashboards, service levels, or root-cause reporting that changed how other teams fixed their processes.
Has exposure to subscription or hardware-plus-subscription billing.
AI First: Experience using AI tooling to drive efficiency and outcomes for themselves and their team.
Has a strong bias for action and insistence on high standards.

As a Sr. Manager of Machine Learning, you will lead teams that fuse on-device computer vision with IMU, GPS, and vehicle diagnostic data to detect, interpret, and surface actionable safety events and continuous risk signals.
You’ll own the model lifecycle across edge and cloud – data curation, training, evaluation (including shadow/online experiments), deployment, monitoring, and iteration—and develop the core AI platform that powers these capabilities at fleet scale. Own the technical direction for Samsara's on-device and cloud safety AI systems — making architectural decisions about what runs on constrained edge hardware vs. cloud, how models are packaged and deployed across more than 2M dashcams, and how the data flywheel is built to drive continuous improvement.
Lead the transition from individual model deployments to a coherent, system-level platform — one that fuses camera, IMU, GPS, and vehicle telemetry data to detect, interpret, and surface safety events with high precision and low latency.
Evaluate and integrate emerging AI capabilities (e.g. VLMs, foundation models, multi-task architectures) and determine when they are ready to move from research to production at fleet scale.

Lead experiment design, offline/online evaluation, and go/no-go decisions for new ML-powered features — grounding every launch in real safety metrics, not just model performance benchmarks.

Experience building and deploying large-scale machine learning systems with feedback loops for continuous improvement.

Customer orientation and intensive focus on improving the customer experience.
Experience building, deploying, and optimizing AI systems than span edge devices and the cloud.
Experience with VLMs, foundation models, or multi-task architectures in production settings — particularly in constrained compute environments.

Build and ship internal data and AI products that help Product and Engineering teams understand platform usage, customer friction, and the highest-impact opportunities to improve.
Analyze large volumes of structured and unstructured data, including product telemetry, support tickets, customer conversations, feature requests, surveys, and product metadata, to find patterns that would be difficult to see manually.
Turn one-time analyses into reliable, repeatable tools and workflows with clear data definitions, quality checks, documentation, and feedback loops.
Translate complex findings into clear, decision-ready recommendations for R&D leadership, while preserving the evidence and methodology behind them.
Quantify the revenue impact of platform investments and report on it, so every roadmap bet has a clear, defensible ARR case before and after launch.
Own projects end to end: scope the problem, identify and connect the right data, build the first version, launch it, measure adoption and business impact, and continue improving it.
Use AI-assisted development tools thoughtfully, checking outputs, debugging failures, and applying sound judgment rather than treating generated work as automatically correct.

Experience structuring and analyzing messy or large datasets, validating the results, and explaining what the analysis does and does not prove.
Strong product and customer judgment: you start with the user problem and business outcome, not the technology.
Clear written and verbal communication. You can explain technical or analytical work to non-technical partners and executives without losing the important details.

Experience in a B2B technology company or working closely with Product and Engineering teams.
Experience in Product Operations functions: defining and tracking product roadmaps and feature requests, and bringing the voice of the customer to every product conversation.
Familiarity with enterprise platform domains such as billing and monetization, identity, access, and org management, or security and compliance, and with what enterprise buyers require in each.

title: Manufacturing & Process Engineer
description:
About Standard Bots

Standard Bots is America's largest manufacturer of AI-native industrial robots. Full-stack robots—hardware, software, and AI—all designed and assembled in Glen Cove, New York. The company makes AI-native robots anyone can buy and deploy, with customers ranging from family-owned machine shops to the Fortune 500. Customers include Sunoco, Lockheed Martin, NASA, and the U.S. Army, along with hundreds of manufacturers nationwide. Standard Bots raised a $200 million Series C at a $1 billion valuation from RoboStrategy, General Catalyst, Amazon Industrial Innovation Fund, and Samsung Next.


About the role

You'll own how Standard Bots robots get built — from the first process design to the last improvement on the production floor. Our factory is in Glen Cove, NY, and you'll be on it every day, so the fixture you design or the fix you make today shows up on the line tomorrow morning. The discipline we build now will define the quality and cost of every robot we ship, and you'll help set it.

This is an individual contributor role for an engineer who wants real ownership early. You'll report to the Manufacturing & Process Engineering Manager and work closely with product, mechanical engineering, quality, and production. As production scales, so will your scope.

📍 Location

You'll work on-site at our factory in Glen Cove, NY, five days a week.


What you'll do

- Sit in DFM/DFA reviews with product and mechanical engineering and bring concrete feedback on assemblability, tolerances, and cost, not vague opinions.

- Design, build, and validate the fixtures, tooling, and workstations used for robot assembly and test.

- Own the process flow for your assigned assemblies, and support NPI as new products move from prototype to production.

- Spot automation opportunities in assembly, test, and material handling, then build the case for the ones actually worth doing.

- Drive measurable gains in yield, cycle time, and first-pass quality on the stations and lines you own.

- Run root cause analysis on defects and nonconformances, put corrective actions in place, and verify they hold.

- Contribute to PFMEAs and control plans, and feed what you learn on the floor back into them.

- Use time studies, capacity analysis, and lean tools (5S/6S, standard work, value stream mapping) to cut waste.

- Write and maintain the work instructions, routings, and BOM accuracy for your processes.

- Track process metrics (capability, yield, cycle time) and report them weekly.


What you'll bring

- 3–5 years in manufacturing or process engineering in a hardware production environment.

- A bachelor's degree in Mechanical, Industrial, Manufacturing, or a related engineering field.

- Hands-on production-level experience with DFM/DFA, fixture design, and process documentation.

- CAD proficiency (SolidWorks, Onshape, or similar) for fixture and tooling design.

- Working knowledge of root cause analysis and lean or continuous improvement methods.

- At least one quality or throughput improvement you scoped, delivered, and can put a number on.

- Comfort on the shop floor every day, in a place where the playbook is still being written.


Nice to have

- Background in robotics, automation hardware, or complex electromechanical assembly.

- Exposure to scaling from low-volume prototype to higher-volume production.

- Experience with PFMEA, control plans, or SPC.

- Exposure to sheet metal, machined components, PCB assembly, or mixed-process manufacturing.

- Familiarity with MES, ERP, or manufacturing data systems.

- Basic scripting or data analysis skills (Python, SQL, or advanced Excel).


Compensation and Benefits

The salary range for this role is $150,000 - $180,000, depending on experience. We are open to a variety of seniority levels for this role and will build compensation packages that are commensurate with seniority and skill level. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All Full-Time Employees are eligible for Employee Stock Options. We also offer a package of benefits including paid time off, medical/dental/vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Staff Firmware Engineer - AMR
description:
ABOUT STANDARD BOTS

Standard Bots' mission is to significantly lower the barrier to entry to real-world automation, bringing the power of bits to the world of atoms and unlocking productivity for entire new industries and users.

Bolt is our mobile manipulation platform: two of our robot arms on an upper body, riding an autonomous mobile base that we are designing and building in-house. Control systems and embedded engineering are the basis of the entire company's mission, and the mobile base is built on them.


WHAT YOU'LL DO

We're looking for an exceptional Staff Firmware Engineer to lead the firmware of Bolt's mobile base. This role sets the firmware architecture for that base from the first prototype: drive and motor control, power and battery systems, sensors and I/O, and the communication that ties them to the robot's compute.

Your impact will be measured by how quickly the first AMRs come to life on the bench and the test floor, how reliably they run once they leave it, and how strong the firmware team around you becomes.


RESPONSIBILITIES

Bring-up and architecture

 - Define the Architecture: Own the firmware architecture across every controller on the base: partitioning, communication buses, timing, update paths, and diagnostics

 - Bring Up the Fleet: Lead firmware bring-up for each prototype build with the electrical and mechanical teams, on a hardware schedule that doesn't move. That includes board support packages, drivers, and bootloaders

 - Pragmatic Trade-Offs: Make clear, pragmatic calls on what each build needs now and what can wait, balancing long-term vision with timely delivery

 - Shape the Hardware: Partner with electrical engineers from schematic review onward, so every board is easy to bring up, test, and debug

 - Standard Setter: Set the coding standards, review practices, test expectations, and release process for all AMR firmware

Motion, power, and sensors

 - Motion Foundations: Own firmware for the drive modules and their motor control. That covers current, velocity, and steering loops, encoder feedback, and coordinated control of all wheels

 - Power and Batteries: Own firmware for power sequencing, battery management communication, charging and docking, and battery swap

 - Sensors and I/O: Integrate the sensors and peripherals on the base, and deliver their data reliably to the robot's compute

 - Cross-Team Interfaces: Define the interfaces between firmware and the navigation, fleet, and safety software, and between the base and Bolt's upper body

Quality and leverage

 - Debug Across Boundaries: Root-cause problems that span firmware, electrical, mechanical, and component behavior. Drive them to closure and turn them into prioritized work that prevents recurrence across the fleet

 - Systemic Quality: Build hardware-in-the-loop tests, fault injection, production test firmware, and diagnostic tools that catch problems before they reach a robot

 - Technical Multiplier: Mentor the AMR embedded engineers, review their designs, and help grow the team


SOFTWARE STACK AND OWNERSHIP AREAS

This role owns board bring-up, motor control, power and battery systems, sensors and I/O, and firmware test tooling for Bolt's mobile base.

Tech Stack

 - Embedded: STM32 or similar, C / C++, FreeRTOS or similar

 - Communications: CAN, EtherCAT, Ethernet

 - Infrastructure & Tooling: Python, GitHub Actions, CI/CD, hardware-in-the-loop rigs


LOCATION

This is an on-site role at our new Boston-area office, where Bolt's mobile base is designed, built, and tested. There's some flexibility on days in the office once you're up to speed. The build area, electronics lab, test floor, and robots are steps from your desk.


WHO YOU ARE

We're looking for a firmware leader who has taken a battery-powered robot or vehicle from first boards to a fielded fleet. You lead by writing the hard parts yourself, and you know what it takes for firmware to survive thousands of hours on a factory floor. You're comfortable operating with complete independence.





SKILLS YOU'LL BRING

 - Experience: 8+ years of embedded firmware development, including leading firmware for a battery-powered product with motors through production

 - Motor Control: Hands-on motor control firmware experience (FOC, current sensing, encoders), ideally for traction or steering drives

 - Embedded Depth: Mastery of C / C++ on microcontrollers, RTOS design, real-time scheduling, interrupts and DMA, and peripheral drivers

 - Bring-Up Skills: Fluent with oscilloscopes, logic analyzers, DMMs, and schematics. You diagnose timing, signaling, and electrical issues at the bench

 - Power Systems: Experience with power sequencing, BMS communication, and charging

 - Leadership: You've led engineers through an NPI cycle and made them better

 - Cross-Functional Influence: Proven ability to influence technical direction without direct authority and successfully partner with hardware engineering, motion planning, safety, and executive leadership

 - Clarity of Communication: Exceptional written and verbal communication skills, capable of synthesizing complex technical risks and strategies for non-technical leadership

 - Impact Driven: You relentlessly seek user impact and value execution over technical idealism

 - Proactive Simplicity: A relentless drive to reduce complexity, improve operational simplicity, and proactively identify organizational-level technical risks and address them before they become crises

 - Excelling in Ambitious Environments: Your best work happened where hardware deadlines were real and the plan changed weekly


NICE TO HAVE

 - Prior work on mobile robots, AGVs, or autonomous vehicles

 - Swerve, omnidirectional, or other multi-wheel steering drive control

 - Functional safety development (ISO 13849, IEC 61508)

 - Over-the-air firmware update systems for fielded fleets


COMPENSATION

The base salary range for this role is [$200,000 to $230,000], depending on experience. Base salary is just one part of the overall compensation at Standard Bots. All full-time employees are eligible for employee stock options. We also offer paid time off, medical, dental, and vision insurance, life insurance, disability insurance, and a 401(k) to regular full-time employees.

title: Lead QA Engineer
description:
Compensation:
National: $110,000-$155,000
NYC/SF: $120,000-$165,000
Tempus AI is a cutting-edge clinical laboratory coupled with powerful automation capabilities. We continually strive to deliver quality results to our patients as quickly as possible. As a Lead QA Engineer, you will own the quality engineering strategy for a portfolio of in-house developed clinical software, including a HIPAA-compliant clinical order platform and its supporting data-query and ETL tooling, and you will be the senior-most technical voice on how we prove that software works. You will set the test architecture and automation standards that our Senior and mid-level QA engineers build against, own nightly regression and CI/CD test orchestration end to end, and lead release readiness and go/no-go decisions with evidence rather than opinion. Knowledge of genetic testing, molecular biology, or other scientific disciplines is a strong plus but is not required. This is a fantastic opportunity to shape how quality is engineered across a growing clinical software organization.
Key Responsibilities
• Own the end-to-end quality engineering strategy across the application portfolio: test architecture, tooling selection, coverage targets.
• Set and enforce the automation framework architecture across multiple suites and repositories, reusable page objects and fixtures, shared utilities, dependency and version management, stable selectors, and act as the final reviewer on test-framework pull requests.
• Own CI/CD test orchestration end to end (GitHub Actions or equivalent): deployment-triggered and nightly regression runs, health checks, artifact and version gating, reporting, and automated notification.
• Lead release readiness and go/no-go: consolidate risk assessment, validation evidence, and quality metrics into a clear recommendation for engineering and product leadership.
• Drive shift-left across the Agile Scrum teams you support, represent quality and testability in design reviews, requirements, and definition of ready/done, and build quality gates into the delivery pipeline rather than at the
end of the sprint.
• Own the compliance posture of our test practice for regulated components: HIPAA and SOX coverage, PHI handling, access controls, audit trails, and requirement-to-test-to-result traceability. Serve as the QA point of
contact for audit and validation activities.
• Define, publish, and act on quality metrics, automation coverage, flake rate, escape rate, MTTR, and regression runtime, and hold the organization to an improvement trend.
• Mentor and grow the QA/SDET team, including Senior engineers: code review, pairing, framework onboarding, technical roadmap, and career development. Partner with hiring managers on interviewing, leveling, and onboarding.
• Serve as the final escalation for complex or systemic failures that span product, environment, test data, and harness, and drive root cause to resolution across team boundaries.
• Set the standard for non-functional testing (performance, load, resilience) and for responsible AI-assisted QA workflows, test authoring, failure triage, and coverage analysis, while keeping the team accountable for the correctness of every test that ships.
• Partner with software engineering, DevOps, and product leadership, and represent quality in architecture, platform, and release-process decisions.
• Stay hands-on: personally design, build, and maintain automation for the highest-risk areas of the portfolio, and validate scheduled night-time and off-hours deployments in lower and production environments.
Qualifications
• 10+ years of experience in software QA or test engineering, with 7+ years of hands-on test automation, including 3+ years as the lead, staff, or principal-level technical owner of a test practice.
• Demonstrated track record of owning test architecture and automation standards across multiple applications or teams, not just within a single suite.
• Expert-level programming ability in Java and/or Python, with strong design instincts (Page Object Model, dependency management, avoiding brittle waits and copy-paste tests) and a habit of treating test code as production code.
• Deep hands-on experience with modern browser automation (Playwright and/or Selenium WebDriver) and test runners such as JUnit 5 or TestNG, built with Maven or Gradle.
• Deep hands-on experience with API test automation and tooling (e.g., REST Assured, Postman), including status/schema/contract validation and authentication flows.
• Experience owning automation in CI/CD (GitHub Actions, Jenkins, GitLab CI, Bamboo, or similar): pipeline design, scheduled and triggered runs, artifacts, and test reporting such as Allure.
• Advanced SQL and relational database skills (e.g., MySQL), plus a defensible approach to test data management for regulated data.
• Experience setting performance and load testing strategy, with hands-on use of tools such as JMeter, k6, or Gatling.
• Experience with cloud-native delivery, especially AWS (ECS/Fargate, Lambda, S3) or Azure, and with containers (Docker) for reproducible, parallelized test execution.
• Practical use of observability tooling (e.g., Datadog, CloudWatch) and application logs to investigate defects and validate non-functional behavior.
• Working knowledge of healthcare standards and compliance (HIPAA, SOX, HL7, FHIR, and similar), and of testing in a validated or regulated environment.
• Proven mentorship of Senior and mid-level engineers through pairing, code review, and framework onboarding.
• Excellent verbal and written communication skills, including the ability to explain quality risk and trade-offs to executive and non-QA stakeholders.
• Ability to set technical direction and drive multi-quarter initiatives independently, making pragmatic trade-off between coverage, speed, and effort.
• Bachelor's or advanced degree in Computer Science or a related discipline, or equivalent professional experience.
Preferred
• ISTQB/ASTQB certification, Advanced Level or above.
• Experience in a CLIA/CAP laboratory, FDA-regulated, or SOX-controlled software environment, including audit support.
• Experience building or operating AI/LLM-assisted QA workflows, automated failure summarization, test generation, or agent-based regression triage.
• Knowledge of genetic testing, molecular biology, or other scientific-related disciplines.

title: Senior Electrical Harness Engineer

title: Staff / Senior Staff Software Engineer - Collision Avoidance System
description:
The Collision Avoidance System (CAS) is Zoox's independent safety layer. It runs alongside our main autonomy stack, constantly watches for imminent collisions, and reacts within milliseconds to prevent or reduce them. By using different methods and data paths than the main stack, CAS gives our robotaxi a second, diverse line of defense in the most challenging dense urban environments. As a Staff or Senior Staff engineer, you will be the technical lead for CAS algorithms, with a focus on CAS perception. You will shape how CAS sees the world, combining interpretable geometric methods with machine learning, and you will own the architecture and roadmap that take these capabilities from idea to safe, real-time deployment on our fleet. Your work will directly affect the safety of every rider and road user around our vehicles. In this role, you will:
  • Serve as the technical lead and architect for CAS perception, defining how lidar, radar, and camera data become reliable obstacle detection, tracking, and collision-risk estimates under tight latency and compute budgets
  • Design, implement, and ship both machine learning and classical perception algorithms (e.g., point-cloud geometry, ground estimation, clustering, state estimation and tracking, learned detection and segmentation, sensor fusion) in production-quality, safety-critical C++
  • Own the end-to-end CAS algorithm architecture and multi-release technical roadmap, making clear trade-offs between safety, performance, latency, compute, and ML vs. non-ML approaches
  • Partner across CAS perception, behavior and planning, and validation to define interfaces, requirements, metrics, and evaluation strategies that show the system is safe and ready to launch
  • Work with sensor, system performance, safety strategy, and main autonomy teams to drive cross-team technical decisions, while mentoring engineers and raising the technical bar across CAS
    • Qualifications

  • BS, MS, or PhD in Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Robotics, or a related field, or equivalent experience

  • At least 10 years of experience developing perception or related algorithms for robotics, autonomous vehicles, or other real-time systems

  • Deep expertise in 3D perception from lidar, radar, and/or camera, with hands-on experience in both machine learning (detection, segmentation, fusion) and classical methods (geometry, state estimation, tracking)

  • Strong C++ or Python skills and a track record of shipping efficient, reliable real-time software to production

  • Experience leading the architecture and technical roadmap of a complex production system across multiple teams

    • Bonus Qualifications

  • Conference or Journal publications in Machine Learning or Robotics-related venues

  • Experience with safety-critical systems or functional safety practices (e.g., ISO 26262, SOTIF), collision avoidance, emergency braking, prediction, or planning systems for autonomous vehicles

  • Experience optimizing and deploying models or algorithms on onboard compute (e.g., GPU / CUDA, TensorRT)
